hayek.lineage_en: Heir to the Austrian School of Menger and Mises, he waged the twentieth century's most famous economics debate with Keynes; echoed by Friedman and the Chicago School, his thought deeply shaped postwar classical liberalism and the policies of Thatcher and Reagan, resonated with Popper's 'open society,' and inspired modern complexity science and institutional economics.
hayek.trivia: 他与凯恩斯虽是论敌，私交却不算坏——二战期间两人甚至曾一同在剑桥国王学院的屋顶值夜、防德军空袭纵火弹。1944 年《通往奴役之路》出乎意料地成为畅销书，《读者文摘》的删节普及版更让他一度在美国声名大噪。
hayek.trivia_en: Though adversaries, he and Keynes were on cordial personal terms — during the Second World War the two even took fire-watch duty together on the roof of King's College, Cambridge, against German incendiary raids. In 1944 The Road to Serfdom unexpectedly became a bestseller, and a condensed Reader's Digest edition briefly made him famous across America.

jensen.bio: 1963 年生于台湾台南，九岁随家移居美国，曾在肯塔基一所招收问题少年的寄宿学校度过一段艰苦时光。俄勒冈州立大学电机工程学士、斯坦福硕士。1993 年与两位伙伴在一家餐厅里创办英伟达（NVIDIA），任首席执行官至今，是科技史上在位最久的创始人 CEO 之一。他带领英伟达从一家几度濒临倒闭的显卡公司，成长为 AI 时代算力的核心供应者、全球市值最高的公司之一，并以标志性的黑色皮夹克闻名。
jensen.bio_en: Born in 1963 in Tainan, Taiwan, he moved to the United States at nine and spent a hard stretch at a Kentucky boarding school that took in troubled boys. He holds a bachelor's in electrical engineering from Oregon State and a master's from Stanford. In 1993 he co-founded NVIDIA with two partners in a diner, and he has been its CEO ever since — one of the longest-serving founder-CEOs in tech history. He led NVIDIA from a graphics-card company that several times nearly went under to the core supplier of compute for the AI era and one of the most valuable companies on earth, famous for his signature black leather jacket.
jensen.ideas:
黄仁勋的思想不写在书里，而是一套从三十年九死一生中淬炼出来的工作信念，核心可拆成几条。
第一，是对『加速计算』的长期押注。早在 AI 热潮之前，他就坚信传统 CPU 一步步串行处理的方式终会触到物理极限，未来属于能同时处理成千上万件小任务的『并行计算』——这正是 GPU（图形处理器）所擅长。他赌的是从图形、科学计算到后来的深度学习，世界会越来越需要这种大规模并行的算力。事实证明，现代 AI、尤其神经网络的训练几乎全靠 GPU，这一押注让英伟达站到了 AI 革命的发动机位置。
第二，是『买得越多，省得越多』的反直觉账。他反复对客户说：看起来昂贵的加速计算硬件，因为把任务做得快得多、能耗效率高得多，综合算下来反而比廉价的传统方案更省钱。这背后是一种算总账、算长期账的思维，而非只盯单次采购的标价。
第三，是『痛苦造就伟大』。他公开说过，不希望员工甚至自己的孩子过得太顺，因为『伟大不来自智慧，而来自苦难与挣扎中锻造出的品格与韧性』。英伟达多次濒死的经历，被他视为公司最宝贵的财富——这是一种把逆境重新定义为养分的心态。
第四，是他独特的组织哲学：极度扁平、极度透明。他有数十位直接下属、不开一对一会议，几乎所有重要信息向全员公开，反对用层层汇报去『保护』高管。他相信把信息摊平、让最有能力的人直接面对真实问题，胜过用科层制去缓冲和过滤——『我希望大家都掌握同样的信息，自己做出最好的判断』。
第五，是亲力亲为的『第一性』工程师本色。即便身为巨头掌门，他仍以钻进技术细节、与工程师直接辩论著称，强调从最根本的物理与原理出发思考，而非依赖二手汇报。几条加在一起，是一个把长期赌注、逆境韧性与透明组织揉在一起的实干者形象。
jensen.ideas_en:
Huang's thinking isn't written in books; it's a set of working convictions forged over thirty years of near-death experiences, and it breaks down into a few strands.
First, a long bet on 'accelerated computing.' Well before the AI boom, he was convinced that the traditional CPU's way of processing one step at a time would eventually hit physical limits, and that the future belonged to 'parallel computing' — handling thousands of small tasks at once, exactly what a GPU (graphics processor) is good at. He bet that from graphics to scientific computing to, later, deep learning, the world would need ever more of this massively parallel compute. He was right: modern AI, especially the training of neural networks, runs almost entirely on GPUs, and that bet put NVIDIA at the engine room of the AI revolution.
Second, the counterintuitive math of 'the more you buy, the more you save.' He tells customers again and again that accelerated-computing hardware, though it looks expensive, gets the work done so much faster and so much more energy-efficiently that, all in, it costs less than cheap traditional gear. Behind this is a habit of counting the total, long-run bill rather than the sticker price of a single purchase.
Third, 'greatness is forged in pain.' He has said publicly that he doesn't want employees — or even his own kids — to have it too easy, because 'greatness comes not from intelligence but from character and resilience forged in suffering and struggle.' NVIDIA's repeated brushes with death he counts as the company's most precious asset — a mindset that redefines adversity as nourishment.
Fourth, his distinctive organizational philosophy: radically flat and radically transparent. He has dozens of direct reports, holds no one-on-ones, keeps nearly all important information open to everyone, and rejects using layers of reporting to 'protect' executives. He believes that flattening information and letting the ablest people face real problems directly beats cushioning and filtering through bureaucracy — 'I want everyone to have the same information and make the best decision themselves.'
Fifth, the hands-on, first-principles engineer at heart. Even as the head of a giant, he is known for diving into technical detail and arguing directly with engineers, insisting on thinking from the most basic physics and principles rather than relying on secondhand reports. Together these make the portrait of a doer who fuses long-horizon bets, resilience under adversity, and a transparent organization.

assessments.text: 将其列为年度全球最具影响力人物之一，称英伟达的芯片是支撑当代人工智能革命的『底层引擎』。
被广泛视为最具远见的科技 CEO 之一，提前十余年押注加速计算与 AI 算力；其在位之久、与公司绑定之深在科技业罕见。
质疑英伟达近乎垄断的市场地位与高定价，以及 AI 算力热潮中潜在的估值泡沫；其『以苦为养』的高压文化亦有争议。

assessments_en.text: Named him among the year's most influential people in the world, calling NVIDIA's chips the 'foundational engine' powering today's AI revolution.

Widely regarded as one of the most visionary tech CEOs, having bet on accelerated computing and AI compute more than a decade early; his tenure and identification with the company are rare in the industry.
Question NVIDIA's near-monopoly position and high pricing, and a possible valuation bubble in the AI-compute frenzy; his 'suffering as nourishment' high-pressure culture is also contested.

quotes: 我们离倒闭永远只有三十天。（黄仁勋常挂嘴边的危机感，大意）
伟大不来自智慧，而来自品格；而品格不是在聪明人身上、是在经受苦难的人身上锻造出来的。（2023 年斯坦福演讲，大意）
买得越多，省得越多。（他推介加速计算时的标志性说法）
quotes_en: We are always thirty days from going out of business. (a sense of crisis Huang often voices; paraphrased)
Greatness comes not from intelligence but from character — and character is forged not in the smart but in those who have suffered. (2023 Stanford address; paraphrased)
The more you buy, the more you save. (his signature line when pitching accelerated computing)
works: 英伟达 CUDA 并行计算平台（2006）
推动 GPU 深度学习生态的奠基
历年 GTC 主题演讲
works_en: Foundational work building the GPU deep-learning ecosystem
jensen.lineage: 工程上深受并行计算与图形学传统影响；与台积电张忠谋、AMD 苏姿丰同属华裔半导体领军群体。他扁平透明的管理哲学，与英特尔安迪·格鲁夫《只有偏执狂才能生存》、亚马逊贝索斯的『Day 1』心态遥相呼应，也常被拿来与乔布斯式的产品独裁相对照。
jensen.lineage_en: Shaped in engineering by the traditions of parallel computing and graphics; he stands with TSMC's Morris Chang and AMD's Lisa Su among the ethnic-Chinese leaders of semiconductors. His flat, transparent management philosophy echoes Intel's Andy Grove (Only the Paranoid Survive) and Amazon's Bezos 'Day 1' mindset, and is often contrasted with Jobs-style product autocracy.
jensen.trivia: 公司名 NVIDIA 取自拉丁语 invidia（嫉妒），寓意让对手『眼红』；当年三位创始人是在加州一家 Denny's 连锁餐厅里敲定创业的——而他少年时正是在 Denny's 端盘子、刷厕所打工。他左臂纹有英伟达 logo，据说是为兑现『股价达标就去纹身』的赌约。
jensen.trivia_en: The name NVIDIA derives from the Latin invidia ('envy'), the idea being to make rivals green with it; the three founders sealed the plan in a Denny's diner in California — the very chain where, as a teenager, Huang had bussed tables and cleaned restrooms. He has the NVIDIA logo tattooed on his arm, reportedly to honor a bet that he'd get inked once the stock hit a target.

dunbar.bio: 1947 年生，英国人类学家、进化心理学家，牛津大学进化心理学荣休教授，曾领导『社会与进化神经科学研究小组』。他以提出『邓巴数』闻名于世——通过比较灵长类大脑新皮层的大小与其社群规模的关系，推算出人类能维持的稳定社会关系上限约为 150。他的研究横跨灵长类行为、人类社会网络、语言与梳毛的演化，以及宗教与笑的社会功能。
dunbar.bio_en: Born in 1947, a British anthropologist and evolutionary psychologist, emeritus professor of evolutionary psychology at Oxford, where he led the Social and Evolutionary Neuroscience Research Group. He is famous for 'Dunbar's number' — by comparing the size of the neocortex in primates with the size of their social groups, he estimated that the upper limit of stable social relationships a human can maintain is about 150. His research spans primate behavior, human social networks, the evolution of language and grooming, and the social functions of religion and laughter.
dunbar.ideas:
邓巴想解开一个谜：为什么灵长类、尤其人类的大脑，那个负责复杂思维的新皮层，长得这么大、这么耗能？他给出的答案是著名的『社会脑假说』——大脑变大，主要不是为了使用工具或找食物，而是为了应对群居生活的复杂：要记住谁是谁、谁跟谁好、谁欠了谁人情、谁上次骗过你……维系一个又大又稳定的社群，是一项极其烧脑的任务，正是这种社交压力推动了智力的进化。
顺着这个思路，他做了个大胆的推算：既然灵长类的社群规模与其新皮层大小高度相关，那把人类的新皮层比例代进去，就能预测人类『天然』的社群规模——算出来约是 150，这就是『邓巴数』：一个人能维持的、有意义且稳定的社会关系的上限。超过它，关系就会『超载』，只能靠规章制度而非私人情谊来维系。这个数字在历史里反复出现：原始部落的典型规模、罗马军队的基本单位、许多公司开始觉得『需要正式管理层』的临界点，都惊人地接近 150。
更实用的是，他指出这 150 不是平的，而是一圈圈同心圆：最里层约 5 个最亲密的人（危难时会求助的），然后约 15 个可深度信任的好友，约 50 个朋友，约 150 个稳定熟人，再外面是约 500 个认识的人、1500 个叫得出名字的人。每往外一层，关系的强度和你愿投入的精力都骤减。
他还有个迷人的『梳毛—语言』假说：猴子靠互相梳毛来结盟、安抚关系，但梳毛一次只能对一个对象，效率太低、撑不起大群体。人类则演化出语言，尤其是『八卦』——聊天就像『用声音梳毛』，能同时安抚好几个人，还能传递『谁可信、谁该防』的社会信息，这才让我们突破梳毛的人数瓶颈、维持起更大的网络。
这些研究对今天有个清醒的提醒：社交媒体让你『好友』上千，却并不能突破大脑的硬约束——你真正在乎、真正维系的，依然是那一小圈人。关系是有成本的、会衰减的，需要时间和面对面的投入去『充值』。认清这一点，反而能帮人把有限的精力，投到真正重要的少数关系上。
dunbar.ideas_en:
Dunbar set out to solve a puzzle: why is the brain of primates — and especially humans — so large and so energy-hungry, particularly the neocortex that handles complex thought? His answer is the famous 'social brain hypothesis': the brain grew large not mainly to use tools or find food but to cope with the complexity of group living — remembering who is who, who is allied with whom, who owes whom a favor, who cheated you last time. Sustaining a large, stable group is an enormously demanding cognitive task, and it was precisely this social pressure that drove the evolution of intelligence.
Following this thread, he made a bold calculation: since group size in primates correlates closely with neocortex size, plugging in the human neocortex ratio should predict our 'natural' group size — and the figure comes out around 150. This is 'Dunbar's number': the upper limit of meaningful, stable social relationships one person can maintain. Beyond it, relationships 'overload' and can only be held together by rules and institutions rather than personal bonds. The number recurs across history: the typical size of hunter-gatherer bands, the basic unit of the Roman army, the headcount at which many companies start to feel they 'need formal management' — all strikingly close to 150.
More usefully, he notes that the 150 is not flat but a set of concentric circles: an innermost layer of about 5 closest people (the ones you'd turn to in a crisis), then about 15 friends you can deeply trust, about 50 friends, about 150 stable acquaintances, and beyond that roughly 500 people you know and 1,500 you can name. Each outward layer brings a sharp drop in both the strength of the tie and the energy you're willing to spend on it.
He also has a charming 'grooming-to-language' hypothesis: monkeys build alliances and soothe relationships by grooming each other, but grooming reaches only one partner at a time — too inefficient to sustain a large group. Humans evolved language, especially 'gossip' — chatting is like 'grooming with the voice,' soothing several people at once while also passing on social information about who can be trusted and who should be watched. That is what let us break past grooming's headcount bottleneck and sustain larger networks.
This work offers a sober reminder for today: social media may give you thousands of 'friends,' but it cannot break the brain's hard constraint — the people you truly care about and truly maintain are still that small inner circle. Relationships have a cost and decay; they need time and face-to-face investment to 'top up.' Recognizing this actually helps you pour your limited energy into the few relationships that really matter.

assessments.text: 『社会脑假说』与『邓巴数』成为进化心理学与社会网络研究的经典框架，被广泛引用于人类学、组织行为乃至网络科学。
指出 150 只是粗略均值、个体差异极大，且部分重复研究未能稳定复现该数字，认为不应把它当成精确的『定律』。
从军队编制、企业团队规模到早期社群产品的人数上限，都有人援引邓巴数作为组织规模设计的参考。

assessments_en.text: The 'social brain hypothesis' and 'Dunbar's number' became classic frameworks in evolutionary psychology and social-network research, widely cited across anthropology, organizational behavior, and even network science.
Note that 150 is only a rough average with large individual variation, and that some replication studies failed to reproduce the number reliably, arguing it should not be treated as a precise 'law.'
From army formations and corporate team sizes to the membership caps of early online communities, the number has been invoked as a reference for organizational scale.

quotes: 你能维持的真正关系，大约就是 150 个——这是你大脑容量决定的。（对邓巴数的通俗表述，大意）
社交媒体能减缓友谊的自然衰减，却无法凭空造出原本不存在的亲密。（其线上社交研究观点，大意）
quotes_en: The number of genuine relationships you can keep up is about 150 — it's set by the capacity of your brain. (a popular rendering of Dunbar's number; paraphrased)
Social media can slow the natural decay of a friendship, but it cannot conjure an intimacy that was never there. (his view from research on online social ties; paraphrased)
works_en: Grooming, Gossip, and the Evolution of Language
Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships
How Many Friends Does One Person Need?
dunbar.lineage: 承达尔文进化论与灵长类社会行为研究（如珍·古道尔一脉）的传统，把『社会脑』思路引入对人类的解释；其工作与进化心理学（科斯米德斯、托比）、社会网络分析（如『六度分隔』研究）互相呼应，深刻影响了组织设计、社群产品与当代友谊科学。
dunbar.lineage_en: Heir to Darwinian evolution and the study of primate social behavior (in the line of Jane Goodall), he brought the 'social brain' idea to bear on humans; his work resonates with evolutionary psychology (Cosmides and Tooby) and social-network analysis (the 'six degrees of separation' research) and has deeply influenced organizational design, community products, and the modern science of friendship.
dunbar.trivia: 他最初推算邓巴数，用的是不同灵长类物种『新皮层比例 vs 群体规模』的回归曲线，再把人类代入外推得约 150；有趣的是，从新石器村落、英格兰《末日审判书》里村庄的平均人口，到现代人寄圣诞贺卡的名单统计，这个数字一再浮现。
dunbar.trivia_en: He first derived the number from a regression of 'neocortex ratio vs. group size' across primate species, then extrapolated humans onto the curve to get about 150; intriguingly, the figure keeps resurfacing — from Neolithic villages and the average village population in England's Domesday Book to modern studies of how many people we send Christmas cards to.

hume.bio: 1711–1776，生于苏格兰爱丁堡。他是苏格兰启蒙运动的核心人物，一位经验主义者、彻底的怀疑论者，也是杰出的历史学家与散文家。生前以多卷本《英格兰史》闻名，身后则因其哲学的深刻与犀利，被公认为英语世界最重要的哲学家之一。
hume.bio_en: 1711–1776, born in Edinburgh, Scotland. A central figure of the Scottish Enlightenment, he was an empiricist, a thoroughgoing skeptic, and a gifted historian and essayist. In his lifetime he was best known for his multi-volume History of England; afterward, the depth and sharpness of his philosophy earned him recognition as one of the most important philosophers in the English language.
hume.ideas:
休谟想弄清一件最根本的事：我们到底能知道什么？他的起点很朴素——人心里的一切内容，都来自经验。他把这些内容分成两类：一类是「印象」，就是你当下亲身感受到的、鲜活强烈的东西，比如此刻看到的红色、尝到的甜、被针扎的痛；另一类是「观念」，是印象在记忆和想象里留下的、较为暗淡的摹本，比如你闭眼回想刚才那个红色。他立下一条检验真伪的利器：任何一个观念，若找不到对应的印象作来源，就是空话。这一刀下去，许多看似高深的概念都现了原形。
他最著名的发现，是关于「因果」的难题，也就是后人说的「归纳问题」。我们都相信「太阳明天会照常升起」「松手石头会落地」，仿佛原因里藏着一种必然把结果拽出来的力量。可休谟追问：你真的「看见」过这种必然的联系吗？以撞球为例——你看到一颗球撞上另一颗，然后第二颗动了。你看到的只是两件事一前一后紧挨着发生，反反复复都如此；至于那根把「撞」和「动」死死拴在一起的「必然纽带」，你从未真正观察到。那我们凭什么如此笃定？休谟的答案石破天惊：靠的不是理性证明，而是「习惯」。看多了两件事总是相伴出现，心里就养成一种期待，下次见到前者，自然就预想后者。因果，在他看来，与其说是世界里的铁律，不如说是我们心灵的一种习性。
他另一个影响深远的洞见是「是与应当」的鸿沟：从「事情实际是怎样」的一堆事实描述里，你永远推不出「我们应当怎样做」的道德结论——中间总是悄悄塞进了一个价值判断。这提醒后人，别把事实和价值混为一谈。
休谟还把怀疑之刃指向宗教。在《自然宗教对话录》里，他细致拆解了「设计论证」——即认为世界如此精巧，必有一位神圣设计者。他指出这类类比千疮百孔，且永远从有限的结果跳不到无限完美的原因。他也论证：再多人证也不足以让一个理性的人相信「神迹」，因为神迹意味着违反自然规律，而支持自然规律的证据总是压倒性的。
他甚至把刀转向「自我」。当你向内审视，你找到的从来只是一个个具体的感受——冷、热、爱、恨、念头——却从未抓住一个住在背后、始终如一的「我」。于是他大胆提出：所谓自我，不过是一束川流不息、彼此相续的知觉，像一座永不停演的剧场。这听来令人不安，但休谟并不教人陷入瘫痪式的虚无。他主张一种「温和的怀疑主义」：哲学上我们承认知识没有铁板钉钉的根基，但生活中照样吃饭、交友、做事——自然和习惯会把我们拉回常识。今天的认知科学、概率推理、乃至对宗教与道德的世俗讨论，仍不断回到他当年提出的问题。
hume.ideas_en:
Hume set out to settle one fundamental question: what can we actually know? His starting point is plain—everything in the mind comes from experience. He sorts this content into two kinds. "Impressions" are what you feel firsthand, vivid and forceful: the red you see right now, the sweetness you taste, the prick of a pin. "Ideas" are the fainter copies impressions leave behind in memory and imagination—the red you picture with your eyes shut. He then forges a sharp test: any idea that can't be traced back to some impression is empty talk. Wielded against fancy-sounding concepts, that blade exposes a great many of them.
His most famous discovery concerns "cause and effect"—what later thinkers call the problem of induction. We all trust that the sun will rise tomorrow, that a dropped stone will fall, as if the cause held some force that drags the effect out of it. But Hume presses: have you ever actually seen this necessary connection? Take two billiard balls—you watch one strike the other, and the second moves. What you observe is merely two events occurring one right after the other, again and again; the "necessary bond" tying the strike to the motion you have never truly witnessed. So on what grounds are we so sure? His answer is startling: not on reasoned proof but on "habit." Having seen the two events paired so often, the mind forms an expectation, and the next time it meets the first it naturally anticipates the second. Causation, for him, is less an iron law in the world than a habit of our minds.
A second far-reaching insight is the gap between "is" and "ought": from any pile of factual claims about how things are, you can never validly derive a moral conclusion about what we ought to do—a value judgment always gets smuggled in along the way. It warns posterity never to confuse facts with values.
Hume also turned his skeptical edge on religion. In the Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion he carefully takes apart the "argument from design"—the claim that a world so intricate must have a divine designer. He shows such analogies to be riddled with holes, and that one can never leap from a finite effect to an infinite, perfect cause. He likewise argues that no amount of testimony should make a reasonable person believe in a "miracle," since a miracle means breaking a law of nature, and the evidence for those laws is always overwhelming.
He even turned the knife on the "self." Look inward and all you ever find are particular feelings—cold, heat, love, hatred, a passing thought—never some unchanging "I" sitting behind them. So he boldly proposed that the self is nothing but a bundle of perceptions, flowing and succeeding one another, like a theater whose show never stops. Unsettling as that sounds, Hume doesn't preach a paralyzing nihilism. He champions a "mitigated skepticism": in philosophy we admit our knowledge has no rock-solid foundation, yet in life we still eat, befriend, and act—nature and habit pull us back to common sense. Today's cognitive science, probabilistic reasoning, and even secular debate about religion and morality keep returning to the questions he first raised.

assessments.text: 在《未来形而上学导论》中坦言，正是休谟「打断了我独断论的迷梦」，促使他重新审视理性的根基。
称休谟「对人类思想产生的影响，无人能出其右」，推崇其论证的彻底与清明。
在好友休谟去世后撰文，称他「无论在世时还是身后，都几乎接近一个全然智慧而有德之人所能达到的程度」。

assessments_en.text: In the Prolegomena he admitted that it was Hume who "interrupted my dogmatic slumber," prompting him to re-examine the very foundations of reason.
He held that "no man has influenced the history of thought more deeply" than Hume, admiring the thoroughness and clarity of his arguments.
Writing after his close friend's death, Smith said Hume approached "as nearly to the idea of a perfectly wise and virtuous man, as perhaps the nature of human frailty will permit."

quotes: 理性是、且只应是激情的奴隶。（《人性论》）
一个智者会让他的信念与证据相称。（《人类理解研究》论神迹一章）
凡是可以无证据断言的，也可以无证据否定。（大意，常归于休谟的论旨）
quotes_en: Reason is, and ought only to be, the slave of the passions. (A Treatise of Human Nature)
A wise man proportions his belief to the evidence. (An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, on miracles)
What can be asserted without evidence can also be dismissed without evidence. (paraphrased; commonly attributed as expressing Hume's principle)
works_en: An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals
hume.lineage: 上承洛克、贝克莱的英国经验主义；下启康德的批判哲学，并深刻影响了实证主义、逻辑经验主义以及当代认识论与心灵哲学。
hume.lineage_en: He built on the British empiricism of Locke and Berkeley; he in turn awakened Kant's critical philosophy and deeply shaped positivism, logical empiricism, and contemporary epistemology and philosophy of mind.
hume.trivia: 他最具原创性的《人性论》出版时几乎无人问津，他自嘲该书「自印刷机上一出生就胎死腹中」；而《自然宗教对话录》因内容敏感，他生前不敢出版，临终交代死后才面世。
hume.trivia_en: His most original work, the Treatise, sold so poorly that he joked it "fell dead-born from the press"; the Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion were so sensitive that he dared not publish them in his lifetime, arranging for them to appear only after his death.

kant.bio: 1724–1804，生于东普鲁士的柯尼斯堡（今俄罗斯加里宁格勒），一生几乎未离开此城。他是启蒙运动的集大成者，德国古典哲学的奠基人，以三大「批判」彻底重塑了认识论、伦理学与美学。其生活之规律据说能让邻居对表。
kant.bio_en: 1724–1804, born in Königsberg in East Prussia (today Kaliningrad, Russia), a city he is said to have hardly ever left. He was the culmination of the Enlightenment and the founder of German classical philosophy, who reshaped epistemology, ethics, and aesthetics through his three "Critiques." His daily routine was reportedly so regular that neighbors could set their clocks by it.
kant.ideas:
康德要解决一场旷日持久的争吵。一派（经验主义者，如休谟）说：知识全来自感官经验。另一派（理性主义者）说：靠纯粹推理就能把握真理。康德给出了一个惊天调和，史称「哥白尼式的转向」。哥白尼当年没让天体绕着观察者转，而是让观察者绕着太阳转，从而看清了天象；康德也把次序倒了过来——不是我们的认识去符合外部对象，而是对象必须先符合我们认识它的方式。换句话说，不是世界单方面塑造心灵，而是心灵主动地为经验立法、塑造了我们所看到的世界。
这听起来玄，其实有个好懂的比方：想象你生来就戴着一副无法摘下的蓝色眼镜，那么你看到的一切必然带蓝。这副「眼镜」就是心灵自带的认知形式。康德说，「空间」和「时间」并不是外面现成存在的容器，而是我们感知一切事物所必须套用的两种内置框架；此外，心灵还备有一组更深的「范畴」（比如因果、实体、数量），像模具一样，把纷乱的感觉材料整理成有条理的经验。正因人人戴着同一副「眼镜」、用着同一套模具，科学知识才有了普遍必然的根基——这正是他对休谟因果难题的回应：因果不是从经验里学来的偶然习惯，而是心灵整理经验时必用的规则。
但这副眼镜有个代价。我们永远只能看到「经过加工的世界」——他称之为「现象」（事物向我们显现的样子）；至于事物「本身」究竟是什么——「物自体」——则永远在眼镜之外，无法被认识。这条界线划得极严：人的理性只在经验范围内才靠得住，一旦越界去追问宇宙有无开端、灵魂是否不朽、上帝是否存在，理性就会陷入自相矛盾，正反两方都能「证明」——他称之为「二律背反」。由此他断言：传统上那些对上帝存在的理论证明，统统不成立，因为它们妄图用只适用于经验的工具去把握超经验的东西。
然而康德并非要消灭信仰。他有句名言：我限制知识，是为了给信仰留出地盘。被理论理性赶出门的上帝、自由与灵魂不朽，从「道德」这道侧门又回来了——它们不是可证明的知识，而是道德生活所必须的「公设」。
这就引出他的伦理学核心：「绝对命令」。它要求你只按那种「你愿意它成为人人通行的普遍法则」的准则去行动。比如「为脱困可以撒谎」——一旦人人都这么做，承诺和信任就崩塌，规则自我瓦解，可见它不能成为普遍法则。由此还推出一条人道原则：永远把人当作目的本身来对待，而绝不可仅仅当成达成你目的的工具。这一思想，至今仍是人权与人的尊严观念的哲学基石。
kant.ideas_en:
Kant set out to end a long-running quarrel. One camp (the empiricists, like Hume) said all knowledge comes from sensory experience. The other (the rationalists) said pure reasoning alone can grasp truth. Kant offered an astonishing reconciliation, known as his "Copernican turn." Just as Copernicus stopped making the heavens revolve around the observer and instead set the observer moving around the sun—thereby making sense of the sky—Kant reversed the order: it is not that our knowledge conforms to outer objects, but that objects must conform to the way we know them. In other words, the mind doesn't merely receive the world; it actively legislates for experience and shapes the world we see.
This sounds abstract, but there's an easy image for it: imagine you were born wearing blue glasses you can never take off—then everything you see must come out tinted blue. Those "glasses" are the mind's built-in forms of cognition. Space and time, Kant says, are not ready-made containers out there but two built-in frameworks we must impose to perceive anything at all; and beneath these the mind holds a set of deeper "categories" (such as cause, substance, quantity) that work like molds, organizing the jumble of raw sensation into orderly experience. Because everyone wears the same glasses and uses the same molds, scientific knowledge gains a foundation that is universal and necessary—and this is his answer to Hume's puzzle about causation: cause is not a contingent habit picked up from experience, but a rule the mind must use in ordering experience.
These glasses come at a price, though. We can only ever see the "processed world"—what he calls "phenomena" (things as they appear to us); what things are "in themselves"—the "noumena"—lies forever beyond the glasses, unknowable. He draws this line strictly: human reason is reliable only within the bounds of experience. Once it oversteps to ask whether the universe had a beginning, whether the soul is immortal, whether God exists, reason falls into contradiction and can "prove" both sides—what he calls the "antinomies." From this he concludes that the traditional theoretical proofs of God's existence all fail, because they try to use tools fit only for experience to grasp what lies beyond it.
Yet Kant did not aim to abolish faith. As he famously put it, he had to deny knowledge in order to make room for faith. God, freedom, and the immortality of the soul, evicted by theoretical reason, return through the side door of "morality"—not as provable knowledge but as "postulates" required by the moral life.
This leads to the heart of his ethics: the "categorical imperative." It demands that you act only on a maxim you could at the same time will to become a universal law for everyone. Take "I may lie to get out of trouble"—if everyone did so, promises and trust would collapse and the rule would dissolve itself, so it cannot be a universal law. From this follows a humane principle: always treat people as ends in themselves, never merely as means to your own ends. That idea remains, to this day, a philosophical cornerstone of human rights and human dignity.

assessments.text: 虽多有批评，仍承认康德哲学是「近代哲学的基础」，标志着思想的一次根本转折。
推崇区分现象与物自体是「康德最大的功绩」，并以此为自己哲学的出发点。
在《正义论》中明确以康德的「人是目的」与理性自律为道德与政治哲学的根基。

assessments_en.text: Despite many criticisms, he acknowledged Kant's philosophy as "the foundation of modern philosophy," marking a fundamental turning point in thought.
He praised the distinction between phenomena and the thing-in-itself as "Kant's greatest merit," and made it the starting point of his own philosophy.
In A Theory of Justice he explicitly grounded his moral and political philosophy in Kant's ideas of treating persons as ends and of rational autonomy.

quotes: 有两样东西，我越是持久地思索，就越是充满敬畏：我头顶的星空，和我心中的道德法则。（《实践理性批判》结语）
我必须限制知识，以便为信仰留出地盘。（《纯粹理性批判》第二版序言）
要只按照你同时愿意它成为普遍法则的那个准则去行动。（绝对命令，《道德形而上学奠基》）
quotes_en: Two things fill the mind with ever new and increasing admiration and awe: the starry heavens above me and the moral law within me. (conclusion of the Critique of Practical Reason)
I had to deny knowledge in order to make room for faith. (preface to the second edition of the Critique of Pure Reason)
Act only according to that maxim by which you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law. (the categorical imperative, Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals)
works_en: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
kant.lineage: 综合了莱布尼茨—沃尔夫的理性主义与休谟的经验主义；直接催生了费希特、谢林、黑格尔的德国唯心论，并经罗尔斯等人深刻影响当代伦理学与政治哲学。
kant.lineage_en: He synthesized the rationalism of Leibniz and Wolff with the empiricism of Hume; he directly spawned the German Idealism of Fichte, Schelling, and Hegel, and through figures like Rawls profoundly shaped contemporary ethics and political philosophy.
kant.trivia: 康德终身未婚，生活极有规律，据说邻居会根据他每天下午散步经过的时间来对表——唯一一次例外，据说是因为他读卢梭的《爱弥儿》入了迷。
kant.trivia_en: Kant never married and lived with such regularity that neighbors are said to have set their clocks by his afternoon walk—the one exception, legend has it, being when he became so absorbed in reading Rousseau's Émile that he forgot to go out.

darwin.bio: 1809–1882，生于英格兰什鲁斯伯里。英国博物学家，因乘「小猎犬号」环球考察五年而积累了海量观察。1859年出版《物种起源》，提出以自然选择为机制的演化论，彻底改变了人类对生命与自身的理解。
darwin.bio_en: 1809–1882, born in Shrewsbury, England. A British naturalist who amassed vast observations during a five-year voyage around the world aboard HMS Beagle. In 1859 he published On the Origin of Species, setting out the theory of evolution by natural selection and transforming forever how humanity understands life and itself.
darwin.ideas:
达尔文要解释一个古老的谜：地球上为什么会有这么多种类的生物，而且每一种都和它的生活环境配合得如此精妙？啄木鸟的喙正好凿木，眼睛的构造精密如相机。在他之前，最自然的答案是：必定有一位神圣的设计师，逐一精心造就。达尔文给出了一个截然不同、却同样能解释「精巧」的答案——「自然选择」。
这个机制可以从零拆解成三步。第一，「变异」：同一物种的个体并非完全相同，有的跑得快些、毛厚些、喙长些，这些差异有的能遗传给后代。第二，「生存竞争」：生物繁殖出的后代，远多于环境所能养活的数量，于是它们不得不为食物、配偶、生存而竞争，大部分注定夭折。第三，「差别繁殖」：在这场竞争里，那些恰好带有有利变异的个体，活下来、留下后代的机会更大，于是它们的特征就更多地传给下一代。一代代累积，物种就慢慢「适应」了环境。
举个具体例子：一群兔子里，偶然有几只跑得更快。狐狸来了，跑得慢的更容易被吃掉，跑得快的更容易活下来繁殖。它们把「快」的特征传下去，下一代里快兔子的比例就高了。如此重复成千上万代，整个种群都变得善跑。注意：没有谁在「设计」快兔子，也没有兔子「想要」变快——只是跑得慢的被淘汰了。这就是关键洞见：看似精巧的「设计」，其实是一个盲目的、无目的的过程，在极其漫长的「深时间」里一点点累积出来的结果。设计的表象是真的，但背后并没有设计师。
由此他还推出第二个震撼的结论——「共同祖先」。如果物种会随时间分化，那么把时间往回倒，不同的物种就会汇聚到共同的祖先上。所有生命因此连成一棵巨大的「生命之树」：人与黑猩猩是近枝，与橡树是远亲，但归根结底同根同源。在《人类的由来》中，他鼓起勇气把人也放进这幅图景——人并非凌驾于自然之上的特殊造物，而是这棵树上的一根枝条。
值得一提的是达尔文本人的审慎。他深知此说会激起怎样的风暴，因而反复打磨证据二十余年才发表。他在宗教上倾向于不可知，自称「不可知论者」；他也并不歌颂自然，反而为其中的残酷而不安——他在信中提到，一想到某些寄生蜂把卵产在活生生的毛虫体内、幼虫从内部将其吃空，便难以相信有一位仁慈而全能的神会刻意如此设计。今天，从医学、农业到对抗细菌耐药性，演化论依然是整个现代生物学的统一基石。
darwin.ideas_en:
Darwin set out to solve an ancient riddle: why are there so many kinds of living things on Earth, each fitted so exquisitely to where it lives? A woodpecker's beak is just right for drilling wood; the eye is as intricate as a camera. Before him, the most natural answer was that a divine designer must have crafted each one with care. Darwin gave a wholly different answer that could explain the same intricacy—"natural selection."
The mechanism can be unpacked from scratch in three steps. First, "variation": individuals of the same species are not identical—some run faster, have thicker fur, or longer beaks, and some of these differences can be passed to offspring. Second, "the struggle for existence": creatures produce far more offspring than the environment can support, so they must compete for food, mates, and survival, and most are bound to perish. Third, "differential reproduction": in that struggle, the individuals that happen to carry favorable variations are more likely to survive and leave offspring, so their traits pass more often to the next generation. Accumulated over generations, the species gradually "adapts" to its environment.
A concrete example: among a population of rabbits, a few by chance run faster. When foxes come, the slower ones are more easily caught and the faster ones more likely to survive and breed. They pass on their "fast" trait, and the next generation has a higher proportion of fast rabbits. Repeat this over thousands of generations and the whole population becomes good at running. Notice: no one "designed" the fast rabbit, and no rabbit "wanted" to become faster—the slow ones were simply weeded out. Here is the key insight: what looks like exquisite "design" is in fact the product of a blind, purposeless process, built up little by little over the immense span of "deep time." The appearance of design is real, but there is no designer behind it.
From this he drew a second startling conclusion—"common descent." If species diverge over time, then running the clock backward, different species converge on shared ancestors. All life thus links into one vast "tree of life": humans and chimpanzees are near branches, humans and oaks distant cousins, but ultimately of one root. In The Descent of Man he found the courage to place humanity into this picture too—not as a special creation lording over nature, but as one branch on the tree.
Darwin's own caution is worth noting. He knew well what a storm this would stir, and so refined his evidence for over twenty years before publishing. On religion he leaned toward the unknowable, calling himself an "agnostic"; nor did he glorify nature—he was instead troubled by its cruelty. In a letter he remarked that he could not believe a benevolent and omnipotent God would deliberately design certain parasitic wasps to lay their eggs inside living caterpillars, the larvae devouring them alive from within. Today, from medicine and agriculture to the fight against antibiotic resistance, evolution remains the unifying foundation of all modern biology.

assessments.text: 读完《物种起源》后说：「我竟没想到这一点，真是太蠢了！」此后自称「达尔文的斗犬」，公开为演化论辩护。

assessments.by: 特奥多修斯·杜布赞斯基
assessments.text: 提出名言：「若无演化之光，生物学中的一切都将无从理解。」
称达尔文的自然选择理论是「人类有史以来最伟大的思想之一」。

assessments_en.text: On reading the Origin he exclaimed, "How extremely stupid not to have thought of that!" and thereafter called himself "Darwin's bulldog," publicly defending evolution.
He coined the famous dictum: "Nothing in biology makes sense except in the light of evolution."
He called Darwin's theory of natural selection "one of the greatest ideas ever conceived by the human mind."

quotes: 并非最强壮的物种存活下来，也非最聪明的，而是最能适应变化的。（大意，常归于达尔文，实为后人的概括）
如此简单的开端，无尽美丽而奇异的生命形式，曾经并且仍在不断演化出来。（《物种起源》结尾）
我们对所有生灵的爱，是人最高贵的品质。（《人类的由来》）
quotes_en: It is not the strongest of the species that survives, nor the most intelligent, but the one most adaptable to change. (paraphrased; widely attributed to Darwin but actually a later summary of his ideas)
From so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved. (closing of the Origin of Species)
The love for all living creatures is the most noble attribute of man. (The Descent of Man)
works_en: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals
The Variation of Animals and Plants under Domestication
darwin.lineage: 受莱尔的地质学「渐变」思想与马尔萨斯人口论启发；与华莱士各自独立提出自然选择。其理论经20世纪与遗传学融合为「现代综合论」，奠定了整个现代生物学。
darwin.lineage_en: He was inspired by Lyell's gradualist geology and Malthus's essay on population; he and Wallace arrived at natural selection independently. In the twentieth century his theory fused with genetics into the "Modern Synthesis," the foundation of all of modern biology.
darwin.trivia: 1858年，年轻的华莱士寄来一篇独立得出相同结论的论文，促使一向迟疑的达尔文加紧发表——两人的成果于同年共同宣读，次年《物种起源》才问世。
darwin.trivia_en: In 1858 the young Wallace sent Darwin a paper that had independently reached the same conclusion, spurring the long-hesitant Darwin to publish—their work was read jointly that year, and Origin of Species appeared only the year after.

einstein.bio: 1879–1955，生于德国乌尔姆的犹太家庭。1905 年还是瑞士专利局小职员时，他在一年内连发数篇划时代论文，史称「奇迹年」；后以相对论彻底重塑了人类对时间、空间与引力的理解，1921 年获诺贝尔物理学奖（因光电效应）。晚年流亡美国，既是二十世纪最负盛名的科学家，也是和平与人道的公共良心。
einstein.bio_en: 1879–1955, born into a Jewish family in Ulm, Germany. In 1905, while still a junior clerk at the Swiss patent office, he published several epoch-making papers within a single year—his "miracle year"—and went on to reshape humanity's understanding of time, space, and gravity through relativity; he received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics (for the photoelectric effect). Exiled to the United States in his later years, he was both the most celebrated scientist of the twentieth century and a public conscience for peace and humanity.
einstein.ideas:
爱因斯坦最颠覆的发现，是「时间」并不是宇宙里一只统一的大钟。他从一个简单事实出发：光速对每个人都一样快，不管你是追着光跑还是迎面冲它而去——这听起来荒唐，却是实验铁证。要让光速恒定，就必须牺牲别的东西，于是被牺牲的是「同时」与「时间的快慢」。这就是「狭义相对论」：运动得越快，你的时间相对别人就走得越慢。这不是错觉，而是真实的——如果你坐近光速的飞船绕一圈回来，会发现自己比留在地球的双胞胎兄弟更年轻。今天的 GPS 卫星就必须按相对论校正时间，否则定位每天会偏出好几公里。
由同一套逻辑，他还推出了那个最著名的方程：E=mc²。它说的是「质量」和「能量」本是一回事，可以互相转换；而且因为光速 c 极大，c² 大得惊人，一丁点质量就能释放出骇人的能量。这正是太阳为何能燃烧亿万年，也是原子弹威力的来源。
十年后，他更进一步，问了一个孩子气却深刻的问题：引力到底是什么？答案是「广义相对论」——引力根本不是一种「力」，而是时空本身被弯曲了。想象一张绷紧的橡皮膜，你放上一个保龄球，膜就凹下去；旁边滚过的小弹珠会顺着凹陷打转，仿佛被大球「吸」了过去——其实没有任何「吸力」，弹珠只是沿着被压弯的膜在走「最近的路」。太阳让周围时空凹陷，地球便沿着这凹陷绕行，这就是「引力」。这套理论预言光线经过太阳会被掰弯，1919 年的日食观测果然证实，爱因斯坦一夜成为世界名人。它还预言了黑洞和引力波，都已被后世证实。
然而面对量子力学，这位革命者却变成了保守派。量子理论说，微观世界的本质是随机的——一个粒子在被测量前没有确定的位置，只有概率。爱因斯坦无法接受一个靠掷骰子运行的宇宙，留下名言「上帝不掷骰子」。他相信背后一定还有更深的、确定的规律没被发现。这场与玻尔的世纪之争，他大体上输了，但他逼出的尖锐问题至今仍在推动物理学前沿。
最后值得一提的是他的「宗教感」。他常说自己信「斯宾诺莎的上帝」——那不是一位会聆听祈祷、赏善罚恶的人格神，而是宇宙本身那套和谐、理性、井然的法则。让他敬畏到颤栗的，是这样一件怪事：宇宙居然是可被理解的，人类的数学竟能道出星辰的运行。这种「宇宙宗教感」，是一种面对自然之深邃秩序的谦卑与赞叹。
einstein.ideas_en:
Einstein's most subversive discovery was that "time" is not one great clock ticking uniformly across the universe. He began from a simple fact: the speed of light is the same for everyone, whether you chase after a beam or rush head-on toward it—absurd as it sounds, the experiments are ironclad. To keep light's speed constant, something else had to give, and what gave way were "simultaneity" and the very rate at which time flows. This is "special relativity": the faster you move, the slower your time runs relative to others. It is not an illusion but real—travel near light speed and return, and you will be younger than your twin who stayed on Earth. Today's GPS satellites must correct their clocks for relativity, or positions would drift by kilometers each day.
From the same logic came his most famous equation: E=mc². It says that "mass" and "energy" are really the same thing, convertible into each other; and because the speed of light c is enormous, c² is staggeringly huge, so a tiny bit of mass can release a terrifying amount of energy. This is why the Sun can burn for billions of years, and the source of the atomic bomb's power.
A decade later he went further, asking a childlike yet profound question: what is gravity, really? The answer is "general relativity"—gravity is not a "force" at all, but the bending of spacetime itself. Picture a taut rubber sheet: set a bowling ball on it and the sheet dips; a marble rolling past curves around the dip as if "pulled" toward the ball—yet there is no "pull" at all, the marble is simply taking the straightest path it can across the warped sheet. The Sun dents the spacetime around it, and the Earth orbits along that dent—that is "gravity." The theory predicted that light passing the Sun would be bent, and the 1919 eclipse observations confirmed it, making Einstein a worldwide celebrity overnight. It also predicted black holes and gravitational waves, both since confirmed.
Yet facing quantum mechanics, this revolutionary turned conservative. Quantum theory says the microscopic world is fundamentally random—before measurement a particle has no definite position, only probabilities. Einstein could not accept a universe run by dice, leaving the famous line "God does not play dice." He believed there had to be a deeper, deterministic order not yet uncovered. He largely lost this century-defining argument with Bohr, but the sharp questions he forced still drive the frontiers of physics today.
Finally, his "sense of religion" deserves mention. He often said he believed in "Spinoza's God"—not a personal deity who hears prayers and rewards or punishes, but the harmonious, rational, lawful order of the universe itself. What awed him to trembling was a strange fact: that the universe is comprehensible at all, that human mathematics can spell out the motions of the stars. This "cosmic religious feeling" is a humility and wonder before the deep order of nature.

assessments.text: 在与爱因斯坦关于量子力学的长期论辩中，玻尔反复回应那句「上帝不掷骰子」时说：别去指挥上帝该怎么做。他视这场争论为自己一生最大的思想激励。
1999 年末，《时代》评选爱因斯坦为「世纪人物」，称他是二十世纪科学与想象力的象征。

assessments_en.text: Through their long debate over quantum mechanics, replying again and again to "God does not play dice," Bohr retorted that one should stop telling God what to do. He regarded the exchange as the greatest intellectual stimulus of his life.
At the end of 1999, Time named Einstein "Person of the Century," calling him the symbol of twentieth-century science and imagination.

quotes: 上帝不掷骰子。（致玻恩的信，大意）
宇宙最不可理解之处，就在于它居然是可以理解的。（《物理学与实在》，大意）
想象力比知识更重要。（《论科学》访谈，大意）
quotes_en: God does not play dice. (from a letter to Max Born, paraphrased)
The most incomprehensible thing about the universe is that it is comprehensible. ("Physics and Reality," paraphrased)
Imagination is more important than knowledge. (from an interview, paraphrased)
works: 《论动体的电动力学》（1905，狭义相对论）
《物体的惯性同它所含的能量有关吗？》（1905，E=mc²）
《相对论：狭义与广义理论》（科普读本，1916）
works_en: "On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies" (1905, special relativity)
"Does the Inertia of a Body Depend Upon Its Energy Content?" (1905, E=mc²)
"The Foundation of the General Theory of Relativity" (1916)
Relativity: The Special and the General Theory (a popular account, 1916)
The World As I See It (collected essays)
einstein.lineage: 承牛顿与麦克斯韦的物理传统，又在哲学上深受斯宾诺莎、休谟与马赫影响；他的相对论与量子贡献奠定了现代物理学，启发了从玻尔、海森堡到当代宇宙学与引力波研究的整个谱系。
einstein.lineage_en: He inherited the physics of Newton and Maxwell while drawing philosophically on Spinoza, Hume, and Mach; his relativity and quantum contributions laid the foundation of modern physics, inspiring a whole lineage from Bohr and Heisenberg to contemporary cosmology and gravitational-wave research.
einstein.trivia: 他去世后大脑被病理学家未经家属许可取走保存研究，一度成为科学史上的奇谈；而他生前曾被提议出任以色列第二任总统，他婉拒了。
einstein.trivia_en: After his death his brain was removed and preserved for study by a pathologist without the family's permission, becoming a strange episode in the history of science; in life he had been offered the presidency of Israel, which he politely declined.

hawking.bio: 1942–2018，生于英国牛津。21 岁被诊断患有渐冻症（肌萎缩侧索硬化，ALS），医生断言他只剩几年寿命，他却带病工作了半个多世纪。作为剑桥大学的理论物理学家，他在黑洞与宇宙起源上做出奠基性贡献，更以科普巨著《时间简史》让全世界仰望星空。
hawking.bio_en: 1942–2018, born in Oxford, England. At twenty-one he was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (ALS) and told he had only a few years to live, yet he worked for more than half a century despite it. As a theoretical physicist at Cambridge, he made foundational contributions to the study of black holes and the origin of the universe, and through his blockbuster A Brief History of Time he taught the whole world to look up at the stars.
hawking.ideas:
霍金一生追问的是宇宙最极端的两端：黑洞，和时间的开端。
先说黑洞。所谓黑洞，是一团质量大到连光都逃不出去的天体——它的引力强到把周围的时空压成一个无底洞，任何东西一旦越过那道叫「事件视界」的边界，就再也回不来。按经典理论，黑洞应该是绝对的「黑」，只进不出。但霍金 1974 年的惊人发现彻底改写了这一点：把量子力学考虑进去后，黑洞其实会极其微弱地「发光」、缓缓向外辐射能量——这就是「霍金辐射」。打个比方，真空并非空无一物，而是不断有成对的虚粒子瞬间冒出又湮灭；在事件视界边缘，偶尔一个粒子掉进黑洞、另一个逃了出来，看上去就像黑洞在往外吐东西。这意味着黑洞并非永恒，它会极其缓慢地「蒸发」，最终消失。这一发现第一次把引力、量子论和热力学三大支柱联系在了一起，被公认为现代物理学最深刻的洞见之一。
再说宇宙的开端。霍金早年与彭罗斯合作证明：如果广义相对论成立，宇宙必然始于一个「奇点」——一个密度无穷大、时空曲率无穷大的起点，也就是「大爆炸」。这等于用数学说明，宇宙有一个明确的开始。这里他有一个常被误解、却极优雅的想法：很多人问「大爆炸之前是什么？」，霍金说这个问题本身可能是问错了——因为「时间」本身就是从大爆炸那一刻才开始的。就像问「北极的北边是哪里？」——到了北极，再没有「更北」可言。既然时间有起点，「之前」二字便失去了意义。
基于此，他还提出一个大胆主张：宇宙未必需要一位创世者。在他看来，由于引力这样的物理定律存在，宇宙完全可以从「无」中自发地、自然地诞生，无需谁去点燃第一把火。这并非要证明上帝不存在，而是说：用物理学本身，就足以解释宇宙为何会无中生有。
他毕生的终极梦想，是找到一套「万有理论」——一组能同时解释从最微小的粒子到最宏大的星系、把所有物理定律统一起来的方程，让人类「读懂上帝的心思」。这个梦至今未竟，却指引着无数后来者。
而所有这些思考，都是在一具几乎完全瘫痪的身体里完成的。渐冻症逐渐夺走了他的行动与声音，最后他只能靠脸颊肌肉操控一台语音合成器，一个字一个字地「说话」。他活了七十六岁，远超医生预言，本身就是对人类意志的礼赞。
hawking.ideas_en:
Hawking spent his life questioning the two most extreme ends of the cosmos: black holes, and the beginning of time.
First, black holes. A black hole is an object so massive that not even light can escape it—its gravity crushes the surrounding spacetime into a bottomless pit, and once anything crosses the boundary called the "event horizon," it can never return. By classical theory a black hole should be utterly "black," letting things in but never out. But Hawking's astonishing 1974 discovery rewrote this entirely: once you bring quantum mechanics into the picture, a black hole actually "glows" ever so faintly, slowly radiating energy outward—this is "Hawking radiation." By way of analogy, the vacuum is not truly empty; pairs of virtual particles constantly flicker into being and annihilate. At the edge of the event horizon, now and then one particle falls in while the other escapes, so it looks as if the black hole is spitting something out. This means black holes are not eternal—they very slowly "evaporate" and eventually vanish. The discovery, for the first time, tied together the three great pillars of gravity, quantum theory, and thermodynamics, and is regarded as one of the most profound insights of modern physics.
Now, the beginning of the universe. Working early on with Roger Penrose, Hawking proved that if general relativity holds, the universe must have begun in a "singularity"—a starting point of infinite density and infinite spacetime curvature, the "Big Bang." This was, in effect, a mathematical demonstration that the universe had a definite beginning. Here he had an idea often misunderstood yet wonderfully elegant: many people ask "what came before the Big Bang?", and Hawking said the question itself may be malformed—because "time" itself began only at the moment of the Big Bang. It is like asking "what lies north of the North Pole?"—once you reach the Pole, there is no "further north." If time has a starting point, the word "before" loses its meaning.
On this basis he made a bold claim: the universe need not require a creator. As he saw it, because physical laws such as gravity exist, the universe could perfectly well arise spontaneously and naturally from "nothing," with no one needed to light the first spark. This was not meant to prove God does not exist, but to say: physics itself suffices to explain why there is something rather than nothing.
His ultimate lifelong dream was to find a "theory of everything"—a single set of equations uniting all physical laws, from the tiniest particle to the grandest galaxy, that would let humanity "read the mind of God." That dream remains unfulfilled, yet it guides countless successors.
And all of this thinking was done inside an almost completely paralyzed body. ALS gradually robbed him of movement and voice, until at last he could "speak" only by twitching a cheek muscle to drive a speech synthesizer, one word at a time. He lived to seventy-six, far beyond his doctors' prediction—an event that is itself a tribute to the human will.

assessments.text: 在霍金的讣告中，这位合作者与后来的诺奖得主称他的工作「在结合广义相对论与量子论上做出了最杰出的贡献」，并赞其面对病痛的坚韧。
在霍金辞世时公开悼念，称他的离去在宇宙学的知识版图上留下了一片真空。

assessments_en.text: In Hawking's obituary, his collaborator and later Nobel laureate wrote that his work made "the most outstanding contribution" toward combining general relativity with quantum theory, praising his resilience in the face of illness.
On Hawking's death he paid public tribute, saying his passing left a kind of intellectual vacuum on the map of cosmology.

quotes: 我的目标很简单：就是把宇宙彻底理解透——它为何如此，以及它究竟为何存在。（《时间简史》相关访谈，大意）
记得仰望星空，而不要总盯着自己的脚。（公开讲话，大意）
无论生活看起来多么艰难，总有你能做、并能做好的事。（公开讲话，大意）
quotes_en: My goal is simple: a complete understanding of the universe—why it is as it is, and why it exists at all. (from interviews around A Brief History of Time, paraphrased)
Remember to look up at the stars and not down at your feet. (from a public address, paraphrased)
However difficult life may seem, there is always something you can do, and succeed at. (from a public address, paraphrased)
works: 《时空的大尺度结构》（与埃利斯合著，1973，专著）
works_en: The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time (with George Ellis, 1973, monograph)
Brief Answers to the Big Questions (2018, posthumous)
hawking.lineage: 学术上承爱因斯坦的广义相对论与量子理论传统，与彭罗斯合作奠定奇点定理；其黑洞热力学的洞见深刻影响了贝肯斯坦、萨斯坎德等人，并直接推动了今日关于量子引力与黑洞信息悖论的研究。
hawking.lineage_en: Academically he carried forward Einstein's general relativity and the quantum tradition, and with Penrose laid the singularity theorems; his insights into black-hole thermodynamics deeply influenced Bekenstein, Susskind, and others, and directly drive today's research on quantum gravity and the black-hole information paradox.
hawking.trivia: 他曾在 2009 年为「时间旅行者」举办过一场派对——却故意在派对结束后才发出请柬，结果无人赴约，他以此幽默地「证明」了时间旅行行不通；他还客串过《辛普森一家》《星际迷航》和《生活大爆炸》。
hawking.trivia_en: In 2009 he threw a party for time travelers—but sent out the invitations only after the party was over, and when no one showed up he wryly took it as "proof" that time travel does not work; he also made cameo appearances on The Simpsons, Star Trek, and The Big Bang Theory.

nagarjuna.bio: 约150–250，生于古印度南部（据传为婆罗门家庭），是大乘佛教中观学派的创立者。他以严密的逻辑论证「空」的思想，被后世尊为「第二佛陀」，影响遍及整个东亚与藏传佛教。其生平多与传说交织，确切事迹已难考。
nagarjuna.bio_en: c. 150–250 CE, born in southern India (traditionally into a Brahmin family), he was the founder of the Madhyamaka ("Middle Way") school of Mahayana Buddhism. Through rigorous logic he argued the doctrine of "emptiness" and was revered by later generations as a "second Buddha," with influence reaching across all of East Asian and Tibetan Buddhism. His life is heavily interwoven with legend, and its exact facts are now hard to verify.
nagarjuna.ideas:
龙树思想的核心只有一个字：「空」（śūnyatā）。但这个「空」极易被误解——它绝不是说「什么都没有」，不是虚无主义。要懂它，得先弄清它在否定什么。
龙树要否定的，是「自性」（svabhāva）——即事物拥有一种独立、固有、自己就能存在的本质。我们平常都默认：一张桌子有「桌子性」，一个「我」有固定不变的自我，万物各自有一个内在的、自给自足的核心。龙树说，仔细一推敲，这样的「自性」根本找不到。
他用一个经典比喻：一辆马车。马车在哪里？是车轮吗？车轮不是马车。是车轴、车厢、辕木吗？都不是。把零件一件件拆开摆在地上，你找不到任何一处是「马车本身」。可一旦它们以恰当方式组合起来，「马车」就出现了，能载人、能行路。所以「马车」并非某个独立实体，它只是「依赖各部分、依赖人的安立」而暂时成立的——这就是「缘起」（pratītyasamutpāda）：一切事物都不是自己独立存在的，而是依赖种种条件、关系才得以成立。条件聚则生，条件散则灭。
龙树最深刻的一步，是把「缘起」和「空」划上等号：正因为万物都是依赖条件而起，所以它们都没有独立自存的自性——「缘起」即「空」。空，恰恰意味着事物是开放的、相互依存的、可以变化的。如果一样东西真有铁板一块的固定自性，它反而无法生长、无法改变、无法与他物互动。所以「空」不是把世界抽走，反而正是世界能够运转、生灭流转的根本原因。
为了破除人们对「实有」的执着，他发明了一套犀利的逻辑武器，叫「四句破」（catuṣkoṭi）：对任何主张，他都逐一推翻它的四种可能——「是」、「非」、「亦是亦非」、「非是非非」。这不是诡辩，而是层层剥除一切让我们误以为抓住了某个终极实体的执见。他自己并不另立一套教条，只负责拆掉别人的执着，这便是「中道」——不落「有」（以为万物实在）与「无」（以为一切虚无）两个极端。
那如果一切皆空，日常生活、因果、佛法岂不都垮了？龙树用「二谛」化解：有「世俗谛」与「胜义谛」两层真理。在世俗层面，桌子是桌子、因果照样运作、行善仍会得善果，这些约定俗成的真实完全有效；但在究竟层面，这一切又都是缘起无自性的、是空的。两层并不矛盾——正因为空，世俗世界才能如其所是地运作。这套两千年前的思辨，至今仍在哲学上回响，连一些现代物理学家谈论「关系性」「没有孤立存在的事物」时，都会想起这位印度论师。
nagarjuna.ideas_en:
The heart of Nāgārjuna's thought is a single word: "emptiness" (śūnyatā). But this "emptiness" is easily misread—it does not mean "nothing exists," and it is not nihilism. To grasp it, you must first see what it denies.
What Nāgārjuna denies is "inherent nature" (svabhāva)—the idea that things possess an independent, intrinsic essence by which they exist on their own. We ordinarily assume that a table has "table-ness," that an "I" has a fixed unchanging self, that everything carries its own inner, self-sufficient core. Nāgārjuna says that on close inspection, no such "inherent nature" can be found at all.
He uses a classic image: a chariot. Where is the chariot? Is it the wheels? The wheels are not the chariot. Is it the axle, the cab, the pole? None of these is the chariot either. Take the parts off one by one and lay them on the ground, and you will find no single spot that is "the chariot itself." Yet once they are assembled in the right way, "the chariot" appears—it can carry people and travel the road. So "chariot" is not some independent entity; it is only provisionally established "in dependence on its parts and on our designation." This is "dependent origination" (pratītyasamutpāda): nothing exists on its own; everything arises in dependence on conditions and relations. When conditions gather, it arises; when they disperse, it ceases.
Nāgārjuna's most profound step is to set an equals sign between "dependent origination" and "emptiness": precisely because everything arises in dependence on conditions, nothing has an independent, self-existing nature—dependent origination is emptiness. Emptiness, far from erasing the world, means that things are open, interdependent, and capable of change. If a thing truly had a rock-solid fixed nature, it could not grow, could not change, could not interact with anything else. So "emptiness" does not remove the world; it is the very reason the world can function, arise, and pass away.
To break people's clinging to "real existence," he devised a sharp logical weapon, the "tetralemma" (catuṣkoṭi): for any thesis he overturns each of its four possibilities in turn—"it is," "it is not," "it both is and is not," "it neither is nor is not." This is not sophistry but a layer-by-layer stripping away of every fixed view that tricks us into thinking we have seized some ultimate entity. He sets up no doctrine of his own, only dismantles others' attachments—this is the "Middle Way," falling into neither extreme of "existence" (thinking things are real) nor "non-existence" (thinking all is void).
But if everything is empty, don't daily life, cause and effect, and the Buddhist teaching all collapse? Nāgārjuna resolves this with the "two truths": there is a "conventional truth" and an "ultimate truth." On the conventional level a table is a table, cause and effect still operate, good deeds still bear good fruit—these agreed-upon realities are fully valid; yet on the ultimate level all of this is dependently arisen, without inherent nature, and empty. The two levels do not contradict each other—it is precisely because things are empty that the conventional world can work just as it does. This reasoning of two thousand years ago still echoes in philosophy today, and even some modern physicists, when they speak of "relationality" and "no thing existing in isolation," find themselves recalling this Indian dialectician.

assessments.text: 这位将龙树论著译入汉地的高僧极为推崇他，所译《中论》《十二门论》成为东亚三论宗的根本经典，龙树由此被尊为汉传八宗共祖。
藏传佛教格鲁派创始人宗喀巴奉龙树中观为最究竟的见地，在《菩提道次第广论》与《辨了不了义论》中悉心阐发其空性思想。

assessments_en.text: The eminent monk who translated Nāgārjuna's treatises into Chinese held him in the highest esteem; his renderings of the Mūlamadhyamakakārikā and other works became the foundational scriptures of East Asia's Three-Treatise (Sanlun) school, and Nāgārjuna came to be revered as a common patriarch of the major schools of Chinese Buddhism.

Tsongkhapa, founder of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism, took Nāgārjuna's Madhyamaka as the most ultimate of views, carefully expounding his teaching of emptiness in the Great Treatise on the Stages of the Path and his work on interpretable and definitive meaning.

quotes: 凡是缘起的，我们便说它是空。（《中论》，大意）
不依世俗谛，不得第一义；不得第一义，则不得涅槃。（《中论·观四谛品》，大意）
诸法不自生，亦不从他生，不共不无因，是故知无生。（《中论》开篇，大意）
quotes_en: Whatever is dependently arisen, that we call emptiness. (Mūlamadhyamakakārikā, paraphrased)
Without relying on conventional truth, the ultimate truth cannot be taught; without the ultimate truth, nirvana is not attained. (Mūlamadhyamakakārikā, paraphrased)
Things do not arise from themselves, nor from another, nor from both, nor without cause; therefore know that there is no inherent arising. (opening of the Mūlamadhyamakakārikā, paraphrased)
works: 《宝行王正论》（致友书一类的劝诫之作）
works_en: Mūlamadhyamakakārikā (Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way)
Ratnāvalī (Precious Garland, a work of counsel to a king)
nagarjuna.lineage: 上承般若类大乘经典的「空」义，下开中观一派；经提婆、佛护、清辨、月称等论师层层发展，传入汉地成三论宗、传入西藏成格鲁等派的根本见地，深刻塑造了整个大乘佛教的哲学骨架。
nagarjuna.lineage_en: He drew the meaning of "emptiness" from the Mahayana Perfection of Wisdom scriptures and founded the Madhyamaka school; developed in turn by masters such as Āryadeva, Buddhapālita, Bhāviveka, and Candrakīrti, his thought became the Sanlun school in China and the root view of schools such as the Gelug in Tibet, profoundly shaping the philosophical skeleton of all Mahayana Buddhism.
nagarjuna.trivia: 传说他曾潜入龙宫，从龙王处取回佛陀秘藏的《般若经》，「龙树」之名也由此而来；现代化学元素并无关联，但「龙树」二字在东亚至今是智慧与思辨的代名词。
nagarjuna.trivia_en: Legend holds that he descended into the realm of the nāgas (serpent-dragons) and retrieved from the Nāga King the Perfection of Wisdom scriptures the Buddha had hidden there—the very source of his name "Nāgārjuna"; to this day in East Asia his name remains a byword for wisdom and dialectical insight.

sunzi.bio: 约前544–前496，春秋末期军事家、《孙子兵法》作者，相传名孙武，齐国人，后仕于吴。史载他以兵法十三篇见吴王阖闾，受任为将，助吴大破强楚、威震诸侯。其书是世界上现存最早、影响最深远的兵学经典。
sunzi.bio_en: c. 544–496 BC, a military thinker of the late Spring and Autumn period and author of The Art of War. Traditionally named Sun Wu, a native of the state of Qi who later served Wu. The histories say he presented his thirteen chapters on war to King Helu of Wu, was made a general, and helped Wu crush the powerful state of Chu. His book is the oldest and most influential treatise on strategy that survives.
sunzi.ideas:
孙子最颠覆的一点，是把战争从『比谁更勇猛』变成了『比谁更会算』。在他之前，打仗常被当成血气与英雄主义的较量；他却冷静地说，真正的高手，是在开打之前就已经在沙盘上算清了胜负——『多算胜，少算不胜』。
他最有名的两句话是骨架。一是『知己知彼，百战不殆』：先把自己的家底（人力、补给、士气）和对手的虚实都摸清，再决定打不打、怎么打；信息不足就不要轻举妄动。二是『不战而屈人之兵，善之善者也』：能不打就达成目的，才是最高明的——打仗（哪怕赢）本身就是巨大的消耗。
他还提出一个对管理极有启发的概念：『势』。与其指望手下每个人都是英雄，不如把局面、节奏、赏罚、地形布置好，让一块普通的石头放到陡坡上也能滚出千钧之力——『求之于势，不责于人』。这其实是在说：好的系统能让平凡的人做出不凡的事，而坏的系统会浪费掉最好的人。
后世常误以为《孙子兵法》是教人耍诈，其实它的底色是『慎战』：因为深知战争的代价，所以反复劝人不要轻易开战、不要因愤怒而出兵。它早已超出军事，被广泛用于商业竞争、谈判、管理与人生决策。
sunzi.ideas_en:
Sun Tzu's most subversive move was to turn war from a contest of who is braver into a contest of who calculates better. Before him, battle was often treated as a clash of blood and heroism; he coolly insisted that the real master has already worked out victory or defeat on the planning table before the fighting starts: 'more calculation wins, less calculation loses'.
Two lines form his skeleton. First, 'know yourself and know the other, and in a hundred battles you are never in peril': understand your own resources (manpower, supply, morale) and the real state of your opponent before deciding whether and how to fight, and do not act rashly when information is short. Second, 'to subdue the enemy without fighting is the supreme excellence': achieving your aim without battle is the highest skill, because war, even when won, is itself a vast drain.
He also offered a concept rich for management: shi, configuration or momentum. Rather than hope every subordinate is a hero, arrange the situation, timing, rewards, and terrain so that even an ordinary stone, placed on a steep slope, rolls with enormous force: 'seek victory from configuration, not from individuals'. In effect: a good system lets ordinary people do extraordinary things, while a bad system wastes even the best people.
Later readers often mistook The Art of War for a manual of trickery, but its undertone is caution about war: precisely because he knew its cost, he repeatedly urged against fighting lightly or out of anger. The work long ago outgrew the military and is widely applied to business competition, negotiation, management, and life decisions.

assessments.text: 司马迁在《孙子吴起列传》中记其『以兵法见于吴王阖闾』，并以『吴宫教战、斩美姬立威』之事，描述他治军纪律之严。
三国曹操为《孙子》作注（《孙子略解》），称『吾观兵书战策多矣，孙武所著深矣』，是历史上最重要的注家之一。

assessments_en.by: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian)
assessments_en.text: Sima Qian's biography records that Sun Tzu 'presented his art of war to King Helu of Wu', and through the episode of drilling the palace women and beheading two royal favorites to establish authority, depicts the severity of his military discipline.
Cao Cao of the Three Kingdoms wrote the most important early commentary on The Art of War, saying 'I have read many books on war and strategy, but what Sun Wu wrote is the most profound'.

quotes: 知己知彼，百战不殆。（《孙子兵法·谋攻》）
不战而屈人之兵，善之善者也。（《孙子兵法·谋攻》）
善战者，求之于势，不责于人。（《孙子兵法·势篇》）
quotes_en: Know yourself and know the other, and in a hundred battles you will never be in peril. (The Art of War, 'Strategic Attack')
To subdue the enemy without fighting is the supreme excellence. (The Art of War, 'Strategic Attack')
The skilled warrior seeks victory from the configuration of force, not from individuals. (The Art of War, 'Configuration')
sunzi.lineage: 上承春秋兵学传统，下启孙膑、《吴子》《尉缭子》等兵家；自曹操注本后，历代注家辈出。其思想东传日本（武田信玄『风林火山』即出于此），近世经《战争论》对照与商业管理引用，影响遍及全球军事、商战与战略研究。
sunzi.lineage_en: He drew on the military traditions of the Spring and Autumn era and gave rise to a lineage including Sun Bin and the Wuzi and Weiliaozi treatises; after Cao Cao's commentary, annotators multiplied through the dynasties. His thought spread to Japan (Takeda Shingen's 'wind, forest, fire, mountain' banner derives from it), and in modern times, read alongside Clausewitz and cited in business management, it shapes military, commercial, and strategic study worldwide.
sunzi.trivia: 《孙子兵法》是史上被翻译、研究最多的兵书之一，从拿破仑到现代商学院都奉为经典；硅谷与体育界也常引用。书中虽以战争为题，却通篇反对好战，主张『慎战』『全胜』——以最小代价、甚至不流血达成目标。
sunzi.trivia_en: The Art of War is among the most translated and studied books on war in history, revered from Napoleon to modern business schools, and often quoted in Silicon Valley and sport. Though its subject is war, the whole text argues against bellicosity, urging caution and 'complete victory': achieving the aim at minimal cost, even without bloodshed.

wangyangming.bio: 1472–1529，名守仁，号阳明，明代思想家、教育家、军事家、政治家，心学集大成者。早年遍习程朱理学，因『龙场悟道』而创立心学。一生事功卓著：平定宁王之乱、治理地方，是中国历史上罕见的『立德、立功、立言』三不朽兼具者。
wangyangming.bio_en: 1472–1529, given name Shouren, styled Yangming, a thinker, educator, military commander, and statesman of the Ming dynasty, and the great synthesizer of the 'mind-school' (xinxue). After steeping himself in Cheng-Zhu Neo-Confucianism, he founded his own school following his famous awakening in exile at Longchang. His public achievements were remarkable, including suppressing the rebellion of the Prince of Ning and governing provinces, making him one of the rare figures in Chinese history credited with the 'three immortal feats': virtue, deed, and word.
wangyangming.ideas:
王阳明要解决一个让无数读书人痛苦的问题：为什么道理我都懂，却做不到？当时主流的程朱理学教人『格物穷理』——到外部世界、到一本本书里去探求天理。年轻的王阳明真的去『格』竹子，盯着竹子看了七天，把自己看病了，也没格出什么道理来。
被贬到偏远的贵州龙场后，他在绝境中顿悟：天理不在竹子里、不在书本里，而在你自己心中——这就是『心即理』。每个人心里都本有一种分辨是非善恶的能力，他叫它『良知』，是与生俱来、不学而知的。所谓修养，不是向外灌输知识，而是把这点良知在具体事情上推扩、实现出来，他称为『致良知』。
他最广为人知的是『知行合一』。常人以为先有『知』、再去『行』，知道却做不到只是『还没去做』。王阳明却说：真正的知道一定包含行动，『知而不行，只是未知』——你说你知道孝顺，却从不行孝，那其实你并不真懂孝。知与行是一件事的两面。
这套思想的现代回响很强：它把道德和能力的主场从『读了多少书、懂多少道理』，转回到『你在真实处境里做了什么』。他特别强调『事上磨练』——心性不是打坐冥想出来的，而是在做事、在与人冲突、在处理麻烦中练出来的。对今天纠结于『知道很多却改变不了自己』的人，这是极对症的一剂。
wangyangming.ideas_en:
Wang Yangming set out to solve a problem that tormented countless scholars: why is it that I understand the principle yet cannot live it? The dominant Cheng-Zhu Neo-Confucianism taught one to 'investigate things to exhaust principle', seeking the cosmic order out in the external world and in book after book. The young Wang actually tried to 'investigate' bamboo, staring at it for seven days until he fell ill, and extracted no principle at all.
Banished to remote Longchang in Guizhou, he had a sudden awakening in that extremity: principle is not in the bamboo or the books but in your own mind, which is 'mind is principle'. Everyone's mind already holds a capacity to tell right from wrong and good from bad, which he called liangzhi, innate moral knowing, present from birth and known without study. Cultivation, then, is not pouring in outside knowledge but extending and realizing that innate knowing in concrete affairs, which he called 'extending innate moral knowing'.
He is best known for 'the unity of knowing and acting'. Ordinary people assume that knowing comes first and acting follows, and that to know yet not do is merely 'not yet having done'. Wang insisted instead that genuine knowing already contains action: 'to know and not to act is simply not to know'. If you say you know filial piety yet never act on it, you do not truly understand it. Knowing and acting are two sides of one thing.
The modern resonance is strong: it shifts the home ground of morality and ability from 'how many books you have read, how much principle you grasp' back to 'what you actually did in a real situation'. He stressed 'honing in affairs': character is forged not by sitting in meditation but in doing things, in conflict with people, in handling trouble. For anyone today caught in 'knowing so much yet unable to change myself', this is a remarkably apt remedy.

assessments.text: 明末清初思想家黄宗羲在《明儒学案》中推尊阳明之学，称其『致良知』一说『发先儒之所未发』，是有明一代儒学的高峰。
近代梁启超极推崇阳明，认为知行合一之教于救治空疏士风、振奋实践精神最为有力，对其评价甚高（大意）。

assessments_en.text: The early-Qing thinker Huang Zongxi, in his Records of Ming Scholars, honored Wang's learning, holding that the doctrine of 'extending innate moral knowing' 'expressed what earlier Confucians had not', a summit of Ming Confucianism.

The modern reformer Liang Qichao greatly admired Wang, holding that the teaching of the unity of knowing and acting was most powerful for curing empty scholasticism and rousing a spirit of practice (paraphrased).

quotes: 知是行之始，行是知之成。（《传习录》）
知而不行，只是未知。（《传习录》）
人须在事上磨，方立得住。（《传习录》）
quotes_en: Knowing is the beginning of acting; acting is the completion of knowing. (Instructions for Practical Living)
To know and not to act is simply not to know. (Instructions for Practical Living)
A person must be honed in actual affairs to stand firm. (Instructions for Practical Living)
wangyangming.lineage: 上承陆九渊『心即理』之绪、与程朱理学相抗，集心学之大成；下启王畿、王艮及泰州学派，深刻影响晚明思潮。其学东传日本，对幕末维新志士（如吉田松阴、西乡隆盛）影响尤巨，被视为推动明治维新的精神资源之一。
wangyangming.lineage_en: He carried forward Lu Jiuyuan's 'mind is principle' against Cheng-Zhu orthodoxy and synthesized the mind-school; he gave rise to Wang Ji, Wang Gen, and the Taizhou school, deeply shaping late-Ming thought. His learning spread to Japan, where it strongly influenced late-Tokugawa reformers such as Yoshida Shoin and Saigo Takamori, and is counted among the spiritual resources behind the Meiji Restoration.
wangyangming.trivia: 王阳明不是书斋里的哲学家，而是带兵打仗的统帅：他以少胜多、用兵如神，仅用约四十天便平定了筹划已久的宁王朱宸濠之乱，堪称『知行合一』最硬核的现实注脚。临终弟子问遗言，他只答：『此心光明，亦复何言。』
wangyangming.trivia_en: Wang was no armchair philosopher but a commander who led troops: outnumbered, he put down the long-planned rebellion of the Prince of Ning in roughly forty days, the hardest real-world footnote to 'the unity of knowing and acting'. When a disciple asked for last words at his deathbed, he answered only: 'This heart is luminous; what more is there to say?'

jobs.bio: 1955–2011，美国企业家、苹果公司联合创始人，个人电脑、智能手机与数字媒体时代的关键塑造者。1976 年与沃兹尼亚克创立苹果，1985 年被逐出公司，创办 NeXT、收购并壮大皮克斯，1997 年回归苹果并带领其推出 iMac、iPod、iPhone、iPad，把濒临破产的苹果变为全球市值最高的公司之一。
jobs.bio_en: 1955–2011, an American entrepreneur and co-founder of Apple, a key shaper of the personal-computer, smartphone, and digital-media eras. He co-founded Apple with Wozniak in 1976, was forced out in 1985, founded NeXT and built up Pixar, then returned to Apple in 1997 and led it through the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad, turning a near-bankrupt company into one of the most valuable in the world.
jobs.ideas:
乔布斯的核心信念可以浓缩成一句被他改写的话：『设计不只是它看起来怎样、感觉怎样，设计是它如何运作。』在他眼里，美不是表面装饰，而是把复杂的东西想透、再做到极简之后，自然浮现的结果。他对细节的偏执近乎传奇——连用户永远看不到的电路板内部，他也要求做得漂亮。
他反复强调『科技与人文的十字路口』：纯粹的工程师造得出强大的机器，却未必造得出人愿意爱的产品；苹果的差异，在于让技术服务于审美、直觉与情感。由此延伸出他著名的『聚焦』哲学——他回归苹果后大砍产品线，因为他相信『决定不做什么，和决定做什么同样重要』。
在用人上，他笃信『A 级人才』：第一流的人只愿与第一流的人共事，一旦放进平庸者，团队会逐级稀释。他用近乎苛刻的高标准逼出人们自己都不知道能达到的水准，称之为对人的尊重；但这也使他以暴躁、不留情面著称，是其管理风格中长期被争议的一面。
他还有一种罕见的、近乎艺术家的产品直觉：不靠用户调研，而是『为用户造出他们还不知道自己想要的东西』。这套方法极难复制——它依赖一个人对品味的极致自信，成也萧何、败也萧何。理解乔布斯，既要看到他点石成金的远见，也要看到这种风格对身边人的代价。
jobs.ideas_en:
Jobs's core belief can be compressed into a line he liked to reframe: 'Design is not just what it looks like and feels like; design is how it works.' To him, beauty was not surface decoration but what emerges naturally once you have thought a complex thing through and then made it ruthlessly simple. His obsession with detail was near-legendary, demanding that even the inside of a circuit board, which a user would never see, be made beautiful.
He stressed again and again 'the intersection of technology and the liberal arts': pure engineers can build powerful machines but not necessarily products people love, and Apple's difference was to put technology in the service of aesthetics, intuition, and feeling. From this flowed his famous philosophy of focus: after returning to Apple he cut the product line drastically, believing that 'deciding what not to do is as important as deciding what to do'.
On people he was a believer in 'A-players': the first-rate only want to work with the first-rate, and the moment mediocrity enters, a team dilutes level by level. He used standards harsh to the point of cruelty to pull from people a level they did not know they could reach, calling it a form of respect; but it also made him famous for being volatile and merciless, the long-contested side of his management style.
He also had a rare, almost artistic product intuition: rather than relying on user research, he aimed to 'make for users what they don't yet know they want'. This method is very hard to copy, resting on one person's extreme confidence in their own taste, which was both his making and his undoing. To understand Jobs is to see both his Midas-touch vision and the cost of that style on those around him.

assessments.text: 其授权传记作者艾萨克森评价：乔布斯把对完美的偏执与现实扭曲力场结合，既能激励团队做出不可能之事，也常因苛刻与情绪化伤害身边的人——是天才与难处并存的复杂人物（大意）。
长期对手兼同行盖茨曾表示，乔布斯在『品味、对人的本能判断和产品营销』上有近乎魔法般的天赋，是自己难以企及的（大意）。

assessments_en.text: His authorized biographer judged that Jobs fused a perfectionist obsession with a 'reality distortion field', able both to inspire teams to do the impossible and, through harshness and volatility, to wound those around him, a complex figure of genius and difficulty (paraphrased).
His longtime rival and peer remarked that Jobs had an almost magical gift for 'taste, an instinct for people, and product marketing' that he himself could not match (paraphrased).

quotes: 求知若饥，虚心若愚。（Stay hungry, stay foolish，2005 斯坦福毕业演讲）
你的时间有限，不要浪费时间活在别人的生活里。（2005 斯坦福毕业演讲）
专注与简单……一旦你抵达那里，便能撼动山岳。（大意）
quotes_en: Stay hungry, stay foolish. (2005 Stanford commencement address)
Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life. (2005 Stanford commencement address)
Focus and simplicity... once you get there, you can move mountains. (paraphrased)
jobs.lineage: 师法包豪斯与极简设计、禅宗美学与日本工艺，深受其早年印度之行与禅修影响；其产品哲学经由乔纳森·艾夫等设计师延续，并定义了此后整个消费电子与移动互联网时代的审美与交互范式。
jobs.lineage_en: He drew on Bauhaus and minimalist design, Zen aesthetics, and Japanese craft, deeply marked by his early trip to India and his Zen practice; his product philosophy carried on through designers such as Jony Ive and defined the aesthetic and interaction paradigm of the entire consumer-electronics and mobile-internet era that followed.
jobs.trivia: 乔布斯长期只穿黑色高领衫配牛仔裤，是有意为之的『个人制服』，以减少日常决策的消耗。他年轻时曾赴印度寻道、长期修习禅宗，这份对简约与专注的执念，深刻影响了苹果的产品哲学。
jobs.trivia_en: Jobs wore the same black turtleneck and jeans for years, a deliberate 'personal uniform' to cut the drain of daily decisions. In youth he traveled to India seeking the spiritual and practiced Zen for years, and this devotion to simplicity and focus deeply shaped Apple's product philosophy.

munger.bio: 1924–2023，美国投资家、律师，伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司副主席，沃伦·巴菲特长达数十年的事业搭档与思想挚友。早年从军、学法，后转向投资。他以渊博、犀利、毒舌的智慧著称，被巴菲特称为深刻影响了自己投资哲学的人。享年九十九岁。
munger.bio_en: 1924–2023, an American investor and lawyer, vice-chairman of Berkshire Hathaway, and for decades Warren Buffett's business partner and intellectual companion. He served in the military, trained in law, then turned to investing. Famous for erudite, sharp, acerbic wisdom, he was credited by Buffett with profoundly shaping his own investment philosophy. He lived to ninety-nine.
munger.ideas:
芒格最核心的主张，是建立一套跨学科的『思维模型格栅』。他打了个有名的比方：『在手里拿着锤子的人看来，全世界都像钉子。』只懂一门学科的人，会把所有问题都硬塞进自己那一套框架里。解药是去掌握各大学科（数学、物理、生物、心理、经济、历史）里真正重要的几十个基本模型，遇到问题时让它们交叉印证——这才接近世界本来的复杂样子。
他另一件招牌武器是『逆向思维』（反过来想）。与其拼命想『怎样才能成功』，不如先问『怎样会必败』，把通往灾难的路一条条找出来、避开。他常说：『我只想知道我将来会死在哪里，这样我就永远不去那儿。』在他看来，避免愚蠢，比追求聪明，回报高得多也可靠得多。
他极重视『能力圈』：诚实地知道自己懂什么、不懂什么，只在圈内下注，对圈外的诱惑坚决说不。配套的还有他对『激励』近乎执念的强调——『给我看激励机制，我就告诉你结果』。他认为人的行为绝大部分由所处的奖惩结构决定，所以设计制度时，第一要务是别让激励逼着好人做坏事。
这些看似投资和商业的智慧，本质是一套『如何少犯错地过一生』的实用理性。芒格反复推崇诚实、耐心、可靠这些『无聊的美德』，并尖锐批判嫉妒、自怜与意识形态。他的思想对管理者尤其有用：与其当个事必躬亲的聪明人，不如请来正直可靠的人、对齐激励、然后管住自己别添乱。
munger.ideas_en:
Munger's central proposal was to build a cross-disciplinary 'latticework of mental models'. He gave a famous analogy: 'To the man with only a hammer, every problem looks like a nail.' Someone who masters only one discipline forces every problem into that single frame. The remedy is to grasp the few dozen truly important basic models across the great disciplines (mathematics, physics, biology, psychology, economics, history) and let them cross-check one another when a problem arises, which comes closer to the world's actual complexity.
His other signature weapon was inversion (turning it around). Rather than strain to think 'how do I succeed', first ask 'how would I surely fail', and find and avoid each road to disaster. He often said, 'All I want to know is where I'm going to die, so I'll never go there.' To him, avoiding stupidity pays far better and far more reliably than chasing brilliance.
He prized the 'circle of competence': honestly knowing what you do and don't understand, betting only within the circle, and firmly saying no to temptations outside it. Alongside came his near-obsessive emphasis on incentives: 'Show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome.' He held that most behavior is decided by the surrounding structure of reward and punishment, so the first duty in designing a system is not to let incentives force good people into bad acts.
This seemingly investment-and-business wisdom is at bottom a practical rationality for 'how to go through life making fewer mistakes'. Munger repeatedly praised the 'boring virtues' of honesty, patience, and reliability, and sharply criticized envy, self-pity, and ideology. His thought is especially useful for managers: rather than be a clever person who does everything himself, hire upright, reliable people, align incentives, and then restrain yourself from meddling.

assessments.text: 巴菲特多次表示，芒格让自己从『以便宜价格买平庸公司』转向『以合理价格买伟大公司』，深刻改变了他的投资哲学，称其为最好的合伙人与老师（大意）。
该书汇编其演讲与格言，将芒格塑造为本杰明·富兰克林式的实用智者——以多元学科、逆向思维与道德常识，教人理性地避免愚蠢（大意）。

assessments_en.text: Buffett said repeatedly that Munger moved him from 'buying mediocre companies at cheap prices' to 'buying great companies at fair prices', profoundly changing his investment philosophy, and called him the best partner and teacher (paraphrased).

The volume gathering his speeches and maxims casts Munger as a Benjamin-Franklin-style practical sage who teaches one to rationally avoid stupidity through multiple disciplines, inversion, and moral common sense (paraphrased).

quotes: 给我看激励机制，我就告诉你结果。
反过来想，总是反过来想。（Invert, always invert.）
我这辈子遇到的聪明人，没有不每天阅读的——一个都没有。（大意）
quotes_en: Show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome.
Invert, always invert.
In my whole life, I have known no wise people who didn't read all the time, none, zero. (paraphrased)
works: 历年伯克希尔股东大会问答
works_en: Berkshire annual-meeting Q&A over the years
munger.lineage: 承本杰明·富兰克林的实用理性与格言传统，融汇达尔文、亚当·斯密及现代心理学；与巴菲特共同塑造了价值投资的现代形态，其『多元思维模型』与『逆向思维』广泛影响投资界、商界与理性决策研究。
munger.lineage_en: He carried on Benjamin Franklin's tradition of practical reason and maxim, blending Darwin, Adam Smith, and modern psychology; together with Buffett he shaped the modern form of value investing, and his 'latticework of mental models' and 'inversion' widely influence investing, business, and the study of rational decision-making.
munger.trivia: 芒格年轻时遭遇离婚、幼子病逝、一只眼睛因手术并发症失明等接连打击，却始终以斯多葛式的坚韧面对，从不自怜。他酷爱建筑设计，曾亲自为大学设计宿舍楼；也是本杰明·富兰克林的终身崇拜者。
munger.trivia_en: In his youth Munger endured divorce, the death of a young son to leukemia, and the loss of an eye to surgical complications in succession, yet faced it all with Stoic toughness and never self-pity. He loved architecture and personally designed university dormitories, and was a lifelong admirer of Benjamin Franklin.

damasio.bio: 1944–，葡萄牙裔美国神经科学家，南加州大学脑与创造力研究所所长。以研究情绪、决策与意识的神经基础著称，通过对脑损伤病人的长期观察，挑战了『理性与情绪对立』的传统观念。著有《笛卡尔的错误》《感受发生的一切》等多部影响广泛的著作。
damasio.bio_en: Born 1944, a Portuguese-American neuroscientist and director of the Brain and Creativity Institute at the University of Southern California. Renowned for studying the neural basis of emotion, decision-making, and consciousness, he challenged the traditional opposition of reason and emotion through long observation of brain-damaged patients. He is the author of widely influential books including Descartes' Error and The Feeling of What Happens.
damasio.ideas:
达马西奥毕生反对一个根深蒂固的偏见：以为理性是高贵的、情绪是干扰理性的杂音，最好的决策应当『冷静而无情』。他的研究把这个观念彻底翻了过来。
关键证据来自他的脑损伤病人，尤其是一位被他称为现代『盖奇』的患者：手术切除了一小块负责连接情绪的脑区（腹内侧前额叶）后，这个人智商、记忆、逻辑全部正常，却变得无法做决定——哪怕只是选今天用哪支笔、约哪天见面，他都能没完没了地理性权衡，却迟迟定不下来。原来，情绪并非理性的敌人，而是帮我们在选项间『赋予权重、快速取舍』的关键机制；情绪一旦缺席，纯逻辑反而瘫痪。
由此他提出著名的『躯体标记假说』：过往的经验会把某种身体感受（比如一想到某选择就胃里发紧、心头一沉）和特定选项绑定，像给选项贴上情绪标签。当你面对复杂决定时，这些『躯体标记』会先于缜密推理，给你一个直觉性的趋避信号——那种『说不清但就是觉得不对』，往往是身体在替你预警。
他把这一切上升为对哲学的批判，即《笛卡尔的错误》：笛卡尔『我思故我在』把心灵与身体、理性与情感截然二分，是错的。在达马西奥看来，心智是从身体里长出来的，情绪、感受、意识都根植于维持生命的生理过程。这一思想深刻影响了管理、教育与人工智能：它提醒我们，一个忽视情绪与身体信号的『纯理性』组织或机器，恰恰会在真实决策上变得愚蠢。
damasio.ideas_en:
Damasio spent his career opposing a deep-seated bias: that reason is noble and emotion is noise interfering with it, and that the best decisions should be 'cool and unfeeling'. His research turned that idea completely around.
The key evidence came from his brain-damaged patients, especially one he likened to a modern Phineas Gage: after surgery removed a small region linking emotion (the ventromedial prefrontal cortex), the man's IQ, memory, and logic were all intact, yet he became unable to decide, weighing endlessly and rationally over even which pen to use today or which day to schedule a meeting, never settling. It turned out that emotion is not reason's enemy but the very mechanism that lets us 'assign weight and choose quickly' among options; remove emotion and pure logic itself seizes up.
From this he proposed the famous somatic marker hypothesis: past experience binds a bodily feeling (a tightening in the stomach, a sinking in the chest at the thought of some choice) to particular options, like an emotional tag. Facing a complex decision, these somatic markers fire ahead of careful reasoning and give you an intuitive approach-or-avoid signal, and that 'I can't say why but it just feels wrong' is often the body warning you in advance.
He raised all this into a critique of philosophy in Descartes' Error: Descartes' 'I think therefore I am', splitting mind from body and reason from feeling, is mistaken. For Damasio the mind grows out of the body, and emotion, feeling, and consciousness are all rooted in the physiology that sustains life. This thought has deeply influenced management, education, and artificial intelligence, warning us that a 'purely rational' organization or machine that ignores emotional and bodily signals becomes, precisely, stupid at real decisions.

assessments.text: 《笛卡尔的错误》被广泛评为以严谨的神经科学证据，优雅地重写了理性与情绪的关系，对心智哲学影响深远（大意）。
达马西奥的躯体标记假说被视为情感神经科学的奠基性贡献之一，虽具体机制仍有争论，但『情绪参与决策』已成主流共识（大意）。

assessments_en.text: Descartes' Error has been widely judged to rewrite, elegantly and on rigorous neuroscientific evidence, the relationship between reason and emotion, with deep influence on philosophy of mind (paraphrased).

Damasio's somatic marker hypothesis is regarded as a founding contribution to affective neuroscience; while its precise mechanism is still debated, 'emotion participates in decision-making' has become mainstream consensus (paraphrased).

quotes: 我们不是会思考的机器，我们是会感受的机器，恰好也会思考。
笛卡尔的错误，是把心灵与身体截然分开。（大意）
情绪是理性大厦的根基，而非它的对立面。（大意）
quotes_en: We are not thinking machines that feel; we are feeling machines that think.
Descartes' error was the abrupt separation of mind and body. (paraphrased)
Emotion is the foundation of the edifice of reason, not its opposite. (paraphrased)
damasio.lineage: 批判笛卡尔身心二元论，思想上亲近斯宾诺莎与威廉·詹姆斯的情绪理论；其工作奠定了情感神经科学，影响了具身认知、决策科学、行为经济学乃至情感计算与人工智能伦理的讨论。
damasio.lineage_en: Critiquing Cartesian dualism, he stands intellectually close to Spinoza and to William James's theory of emotion; his work founded affective neuroscience and shaped embodied cognition, decision science, behavioral economics, and debates in affective computing and the ethics of artificial intelligence.
damasio.trivia: 达马西奥常以十九世纪铁路工人菲尼亚斯·盖奇的著名病例开篇：一根铁棍穿过其前额叶后，盖奇智力如常，性情与决策能力却剧变——这成了情绪参与理性决策的经典证据。他与同为神经科学家的妻子汉娜·达马西奥长期合作研究。
damasio.trivia_en: Damasio often opens with the famous nineteenth-century case of the railway worker Phineas Gage: after an iron rod passed through his prefrontal lobe, Gage's intelligence was unchanged but his temperament and decision-making were transformed, a classic proof that emotion participates in rational decision. He has long collaborated with his wife, the neuroscientist Hanna Damasio.

covey.bio: 1932–2012，美国管理学家、教育家、演说家，全球畅销书《高效能人士的七个习惯》作者。该书自 1989 年出版以来售出数千万册，被译为数十种语言，深刻影响了现代领导力与个人成长领域。他拥有哈佛 MBA 与杨百翰大学博士学位，长期从事组织领导力培训。
covey.bio_en: 1932–2012, an American management thinker, educator, and speaker, author of the global bestseller The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People. Published in 1989, the book has sold tens of millions of copies in dozens of languages and deeply shaped modern leadership and personal-development thought. He held an MBA from Harvard and a doctorate from Brigham Young University, and spent his career in organizational leadership training.
covey.ideas:
柯维的出发点是一个尖锐的观察：市面上多数成功学只教『技巧』——如何说服、如何给人好印象、如何快速搞定。他称之为『个人魅力论』，并指出它治标不治本。真正可持续的效能，必须『由内而外』：先打磨内在的品格与原则，外在的方法才有根基。一个内心算计的人，再高超的沟通技巧也会被对方的直觉识破。
他把这套修炼组织成著名的『七个习惯』，分三个阶段。前三个走向『独立』：①积极主动——在刺激与回应之间，人永远有选择的自由，别把人生交给情绪和环境；②以终为始——先想清楚你真正要的结果（甚至你希望葬礼上别人怎么评价你），再倒推今天怎么做；③要事第一——按重要性而非紧急性安排时间，优先做那些不紧急却真正重要的事。
中间三个走向『互赖』，是其领导思想的精华：④双赢思维——把人际当成可以共同把饼做大的合作，而非你死我活；⑤知彼解己——先真正理解对方，再求被理解，这是多数人最缺的沟通习惯；⑥统合综效——尊重并融合差异，让合作产生『一加一大于二』的结果。第七个『不断更新』则贯穿始终：定期『磨刀』，在身体、心智、情感、精神四个维度自我修复。
柯维有一句广为流传的区分：『管理是把梯子爬得更快，领导是确认梯子搭对了墙。』他提醒人们，在拼命提升效率之前，先确认方向是对的——这对今天被各种效率工具裹挟、却忘了问『为什么』的人，格外有警醒意义。
covey.ideas_en:
