Covey began from a sharp observation: most success literature teaches only technique, how to persuade, how to make a good impression, how to close fast. He called this the 'personality ethic' and argued it treats symptoms, not causes. Truly sustainable effectiveness must work 'inside-out': polish inner character and principles first, and only then do outer methods have a foundation. A person calculating within will have even the finest communication skill seen through by the other's intuition.
He organized this cultivation into the famous 'seven habits', in three stages. The first three move toward independence: (1) be proactive, since between stimulus and response a person always has the freedom to choose, so don't hand your life to mood and circumstance; (2) begin with the end in mind, first clarifying the result you truly want (even how you wish to be remembered at your funeral) and working back to what to do today; (3) put first things first, arranging time by importance rather than urgency and prioritizing what is not urgent yet truly matters.
The middle three move toward interdependence and are the heart of his leadership thought: (4) think win-win, treating relationships as cooperation that can grow the pie together rather than a zero-sum fight; (5) seek first to understand, then to be understood, the communication habit most people most lack; (6) synergize, respecting and combining differences so cooperation yields 'one plus one is greater than two'. The seventh, 'sharpen the saw', runs throughout: renew yourself regularly across the physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual dimensions.
Covey offered a widely quoted distinction: 'Management is climbing the ladder of success faster; leadership is making sure the ladder is leaning against the right wall.' He reminds us to confirm the direction is right before straining to raise efficiency, a warning with special force for people today swept along by productivity tools yet forgetting to ask 'why'.

assessments.text: 《时代》将柯维评为 1996 年全美最具影响力的二十五人之一，肯定其在领导力与个人成长领域的广泛影响（大意）。
评论者普遍认为《七个习惯》的贡献在于把零散的成功建议整合为一套以原则与品格为根基的系统框架，但也有人批评其内容偏常识、缺乏严格实证（大意）。

assessments_en.text: Time named Covey one of the twenty-five most influential Americans of 1996, recognizing his broad influence in leadership and personal development (paraphrased).

Reviewers generally credit The 7 Habits with integrating scattered success advice into a systematic framework grounded in principle and character, while some criticize it as commonsensical and lacking rigorous empirical support (paraphrased).

quotes: 管理是把梯子爬得更快，领导是确认梯子搭对了墙。（大意）
在刺激与回应之间，存在着空间；我们成长与自由的力量，正在这空间里的选择。（大意）
先去理解，再求被理解。
quotes_en: Management is climbing the ladder of success faster; leadership is making sure the ladder is leaning against the right wall. (paraphrased)
Between stimulus and response there is a space; in that space lies our freedom and power to choose, and in our choices lie our growth. (paraphrased)
Seek first to understand, then to be understood.
works_en: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
covey.lineage: 思想上融汇富兰克林式的品格修养传统、亚里士多德的德性伦理与基督教信仰；其原则中心领导学影响了此后数十年的企业培训、教练文化与个人成长产业，与德鲁克等管理思想家并称大众领导力的奠基者之一。
covey.lineage_en: Intellectually he blended a Franklin-style tradition of character cultivation, Aristotelian virtue ethics, and Christian faith; his principle-centered leadership shaped decades of corporate training, coaching culture, and the personal-development industry, ranking alongside thinkers like Drucker as a founder of popular leadership thought.
covey.trivia: 柯维育有九个子女、数十名孙辈，常以家庭生活作为讲授原则的鲜活案例。他笃信终身学习，晚年仍坚持锻炼与写作；2012 年因骑自行车摔伤并发症去世。其著作长年位居全球商业畅销榜，影响遍及企业、学校与政府。
covey.trivia_en: Covey raised nine children and dozens of grandchildren, often drawing on family life as vivid case material for teaching principles. A believer in lifelong learning, he kept exercising and writing into old age, and died in 2012 from complications of a bicycle fall. His books remained on global business bestseller lists for years, with influence reaching companies, schools, and governments.

epictetus.bio: 约公元 50–135 年，古罗马斯多葛派哲学家。出身为奴，少年时在罗马为奴隶，后获自由，在希腊尼科波利斯开学授徒。他本人一字未留，今天读到的《谈话录》与《手册》都由学生阿里安记录整理。
epictetus.bio_en: c. 50–135 CE, a Roman Stoic philosopher. Born into slavery, he spent his youth as a slave in Rome, was later freed, and opened a school in Nicopolis in Greece. He wrote nothing himself; the Discourses and the Enchiridion (Handbook) we read today were recorded by his student Arrian.
epictetus.ideas:
爱比克泰德的整套哲学，可以浓缩成开篇那句话：世上的事分两类，一类「由得了我们」，一类「由不得我们」。由得了我们的，是我们的判断、意愿、欲求与回避——也就是「我怎么看、怎么选、怎么回应」；由不得我们的，是身体、财产、名声、地位、别人怎么待我、明天会不会下雨。他把这叫「控制二分法」。痛苦的根源，几乎总是我们把心思押在了「由不得我们」的那一堆上：想控制控制不了的，于是焦虑、愤怒、患得患失。把注意力收回到「由得了我们」的那一小块，人反而自由了。
这里有个关键转折：让我们难受的，往往不是事情本身，而是我们对事情的判断。「有人骂你」是中性的事件，真正刺痛你的，是你心里那句「他不该这样对我、这太羞辱了」。斯多葛叫这个内在的评判机能 prohairesis（意愿/抉择）——它才是真正属于你、谁也夺不走的东西。改判断，就能改感受；这一思路两千年后被现代认知行为疗法(CBT)直接继承。
爱比克泰德最戳当代人的，是他对「知道却做不到」的态度：哲学不是拿来谈的，是拿来练的。他讥讽那些把斯多葛理论背得滚瓜烂熟、一遇事却原形毕露的学生——「别再空谈你信奉什么，把它活出来给我看」。在他眼里，懂得道理只是第一步，真正算数的是 askēsis（操练）：像运动员一样，在一次次小事上反复演练「分清能控制的与不能控制的、守住自己的判断」，直到它成为临场的本能。他还有个生动的提醒：每天可以先「预演逆境」——出门前想一想可能遇到的添堵、刁难、损失，心里先过一遍，真碰上时就不至于乱了阵脚。
他出身奴隶、腿有残疾、一生清贫，却把斯多葛讲得格外接地气——因为他谈的不是书斋里的玄理，而是一个曾经连人身自由都没有的人，如何在最不由自己的处境里，守住那块谁也拿不走的内在自由。
epictetus.ideas_en:
Epictetus's whole philosophy can be compressed into his opening line: things fall into two kinds — those that are "up to us" and those that are "not up to us." Up to us are our judgments, will, desires, and aversions — how we see, choose, and respond. Not up to us are the body, property, reputation, status, how others treat us, whether it rains tomorrow. He calls this the "dichotomy of control." The root of suffering is almost always that we stake our minds on the pile that is not up to us: we try to control the uncontrollable, and so we churn with anxiety, anger, and clinging. Pull your attention back to the small zone that is genuinely yours, and you become free.
Here is the key pivot: what disturbs us is usually not the thing itself but our judgment about it. "Someone insulted you" is a neutral event; what stings is the line in your head — "he shouldn't treat me this way, this is humiliating." The Stoics call this inner faculty of judgment and choice prohairesis — the one thing that is truly yours and that no one can take. Change the judgment and you change the feeling; two thousand years later this idea was inherited directly by modern cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
What speaks most sharply to us today is his stance on "knowing yet not doing": philosophy is not for discussing, it is for training. He mocked students who could recite Stoic theory flawlessly yet fell apart at the first setback — "don't tell me what you believe, show me by living it." In his eyes, understanding the principle is only step one; what counts is askēsis (practice): like an athlete, you rehearse "separate what you can control from what you can't, and hold your own judgment" over and over in small moments, until it becomes instinct under pressure. He offered a vivid drill: each morning, rehearse adversity in advance — picture the hassles, slights, and losses the day might bring, run through them in your mind, so that when they actually come you are not thrown.
Born a slave, lame in one leg, poor all his life, he made Stoicism unusually down-to-earth — because he was not spinning study-room abstractions but showing how a man who once lacked even bodily freedom could, in the least free of circumstances, hold onto the one inner freedom no one can seize.

assessments.text: 罗马皇帝在自己的私人札记里多次援引爱比克泰德，把他列为对自己影响最深的精神导师之一。
CBT/REBT 公开把『困扰我们的不是事情，而是我们对事情的看法』追溯到爱比克泰德，视其为认知疗法的古代先声。

assessments_en.text: In his private notebooks the Roman emperor repeatedly draws on Epictetus, naming him among the spiritual teachers who shaped him most.
CBT and REBT openly trace the principle 'it is not things that disturb us but our judgments about them' back to Epictetus, treating him as an ancient forerunner of cognitive therapy.

quotes: 困扰人的不是事情本身，而是人对事情的看法。
别再空谈你信奉的哲学，把它活出来。（大意）
quotes_en: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views they take of things.
Don't explain your philosophy. Embody it. (paraphrased)
epictetus.lineage: 上承芝诺、克律西波斯开创的斯多葛学派，师从穆索尼乌斯·鲁弗斯；下启马可·奥勒留，并经由蒙田、现代 CBT 一路影响至今。
epictetus.lineage_en: He stands in the Stoic line founded by Zeno and Chrysippus, having studied under Musonius Rufus; he in turn shaped Marcus Aurelius, and his influence runs on through Montaigne to modern CBT.
epictetus.trivia: 他终身未婚、生活极简，晚年才收养了一个差点被遗弃的孩子；据传一条腿有残疾（一说为奴时被折磨所致），他却以此平静示人，正是『接受由不得自己的事』的活注脚。
epictetus.trivia_en: He never married and lived with extreme simplicity, adopting a child late in life who would otherwise have been left to die. He was said to be lame in one leg (by one account from mistreatment in slavery), which he bore with calm — a living footnote to his own teaching of accepting what is not up to us.

thaler.bio: 1945 年生，美国经济学家，芝加哥大学教授，2017 年因对行为经济学的贡献获诺贝尔经济学奖。他把心理学系统地装进了经济学，是这门交叉学科的主要奠基人之一。
thaler.bio_en: Born 1945, an American economist at the University of Chicago who won the 2017 Nobel Prize in Economics for his contributions to behavioral economics. He systematically built psychology into economics and is one of the main founders of that interdisciplinary field.
thaler.ideas:
传统经济学假设人是「理性人」(Econ)：信息齐全、算计精准、意志坚定，永远为自己做最优选择。塞勒一辈子都在拆这个假设。他说现实里的人是「凡人」(Human)：会算错、会冲动、会拖延、会被情绪和默认选项牵着走——而这些「不理性」并非随机噪声，而是有规律、可预测的。
他几个招牌概念都很贴生活。「心理账户」：同样是钱，我们却在心里分门别类——发的工资舍不得花，中彩票的钱却挥霍得心安理得；明明可以互相挪用，我们偏要画地为牢。「禀赋效应」：一旦东西归我所有，我就觉得它更值钱——让你卖掉手里的杯子，要价往往高过你当初愿意买它的价。「沉没成本」：电影难看到一半，你却因为「票都买了」硬撑着看完，被已经花掉、收不回的成本绑架。
但塞勒最有现实分量的，是关于「自控」的部分，这恰好戳中「知道却做不到」。他用「计划者—行动者」的模型描述我们内心的分裂：有一个为长远打算的「计划者」(想存钱、想减肥、想早睡)，也有一个只顾眼前快活的「行动者」(想花钱、想吃、想再刷一集)。两者持续打架，而眼前的诱惑往往赢——这就是「当下偏好」：未来的好处被我们打了很重的折扣。
他给的解法不是「你要更自律」，而是聪明地设计环境：「助推」(nudge)。在不禁止、不强制、不改变经济激励的前提下，靠调整「选择架构」温和地把人推向更好的选项。最著名的例子是退休储蓄——把「默认不参加、想存得自己去登记」改成「默认自动参加、不想存可以退出」，参与率就大幅提升；他还设计了「为明天多存一点」，让人预先承诺把未来加薪的一部分自动转入储蓄，绕开了「现在就要少花钱」的痛。这套思路的精髓是：与其指望人人修炼出钢铁意志，不如把好行为变成默认、把坏行为加点摩擦。他常打趣自己也很懒——正因为懂凡人的弱点，他才不开「你要更努力」的空头支票。
thaler.ideas_en:
Classical economics assumes people are rational "Econs": fully informed, sharp at calculation, iron-willed, always choosing what's optimal. Thaler spent his career dismantling that assumption. Real people, he argued, are "Humans": they miscalculate, act on impulse, procrastinate, and get steered by emotions and default options — and this "irrationality" is not random noise but regular and predictable.
His signature ideas all hug everyday life. Mental accounting: money is money, yet we file it into separate mental jars — we hate to spend our salary but blow lottery winnings with a clear conscience, fencing off funds that are perfectly interchangeable. The endowment effect: once something is mine, I value it more — ask someone to sell the mug in their hand and they'll demand more than they would have paid for it. Sunk cost: a movie is half over and dreadful, yet you sit through it because "I already paid," held hostage by money already spent and unrecoverable.
But Thaler's most consequential work concerns self-control — exactly the "knowing yet not doing" gap. He models our inner split as a "planner versus doer": a far-sighted planner (wants to save, lose weight, sleep early) and a present-focused doer (wants to spend, eat, watch one more episode). They fight constantly, and the immediate temptation usually wins — this is "present bias": we steeply discount future benefits.
His fix is not "have more willpower" but to design the environment cleverly: the nudge. Without banning, forcing, or changing economic incentives, you adjust the "choice architecture" to gently steer people toward better options. The famous case is retirement saving — switch the default from "opt in if you want to save" to "auto-enroll, opt out if you don't," and participation soars; he also designed "Save More Tomorrow," which lets people pre-commit to divert part of future raises into savings, sidestepping the pain of spending less now. The essence: rather than hope everyone forges an iron will, make good behavior the default and add friction to bad behavior. He likes to joke that he, too, is lazy — it's precisely because he understands human weakness that he refuses to write the blank check of "just try harder."

assessments.text: 2017 年表彰其『将心理上现实的假设纳入经济决策分析』，揭示有限理性、社会偏好与缺乏自控如何系统地影响个人决策与市场。
塞勒曾在片中本色客串，用赌场『热手谬误』向观众解释金融泡沫，足见其概念已渗入大众文化。

assessments_en.text: Its 2017 citation honored him "for incorporating psychologically realistic assumptions into analyses of economic decision-making," showing how bounded rationality, social preferences, and lack of self-control systematically shape choices and markets.
Thaler made a cameo as himself, using the casino "hot-hand" fallacy to explain financial bubbles to viewers — a sign of how far his concepts have seeped into popular culture.

quotes: 如果你想让人去做一件事，就把它变容易。（大意）
我们要做的是『为善而助推』。（大意）
quotes_en: If you want people to do something, make it easy. (paraphrased)
Our goal should be to 'nudge for good.' (paraphrased)
thaler.lineage: 直接承接卡尼曼与特沃斯基的判断与决策研究，与法学家桑斯坦合著《助推》，把行为洞见推向公共政策；其『选择架构』思想影响了多国政府的『助推小组』。
thaler.lineage_en: He builds directly on Kahneman and Tversky's work on judgment and decision-making, co-wrote Nudge with the legal scholar Cass Sunstein, and carried behavioral insights into public policy; his idea of "choice architecture" shaped "nudge units" in governments around the world.
thaler.trivia: 他常自嘲『懒惰』，并说正因为自己也管不住自己，才更相信要靠制度设计而非空喊自律；获诺奖时被问到打算如何花掉奖金，他笑答『会尽量用最不理性的方式花掉』。
thaler.trivia_en: He often calls himself "lazy," saying it's because he can't control himself either that he trusts design over willpower; asked how he'd spend his Nobel winnings, he joked he would "try to spend it as irrationally as possible."

wood.bio: 当代美国社会心理学家，长期研究『习惯』的科学，著有《好习惯，坏习惯》(2019)。她用数十年的实验和数据，重新定义了我们对『行为如何改变』的常识。
wood.bio_en: A contemporary American social psychologist who has spent decades on the science of habit, author of Good Habits, Bad Habits (2019). Through years of experiments and data she has reshaped our common-sense picture of how behavior actually changes.
wood.ideas:
伍德要回答一个特别普通、又特别折磨人的问题：为什么我们明明知道该做什么(锻炼、早睡、少刷手机)，却年复一年做不到？她给的答案颠覆直觉：因为我们高估了『决定』，低估了『习惯』。
她有一项被反复引用的发现：人每天约四成的行为，并不是当下临时决定的，而是在固定情境里自动重复的习惯。也就是说，你以为自己一整天都在『做选择』，其实近一半时间是被环境的线索牵着走——走进厨房就开冰箱、坐上沙发就摸手机、一到下午三点就想买咖啡。习惯的本质是一条回路：某个『情境线索』(地点、时间、前一个动作、心情)触发一个固定『行为』，行为带来某种『奖励』，奖励又让这条线索—行为的连接越来越牢，最后牢到不假思索、几乎绕过了意识。这套自动化主要交给大脑较深处的基底神经节，而不是负责深思熟虑的前额叶——所以光靠『想通了、下决心』很难撼动它，因为决心动用的是另一套系统。
这正解释了『知道却做不到』：知道是慢系统的事，做不做却常由快系统的习惯说了算。于是她的核心主张很务实，甚至有点泼冷水——别再迷信意志力。研究显示，真正能长期坚持好行为的人，往往不是自控力特别强的人，而是把自己放进了『不需要太多自控』的环境里。想多运动？把跑鞋放在门口、健身房选在通勤必经之路，给好行为『减摩擦』；想少刷手机？把 App 删掉、把手机放到另一个房间，给坏行为『加摩擦』。改变情境，比改变内心更可靠。
她给出形成习惯的三个要素：稳定的情境(同一个地点、同一个时间反复做)、足够的重复(让动作自动化，平均要相当一段时间，而非传说中的『21 天』)、即时的奖励(行为之后马上有点甜头，让大脑愿意再来一次)。打破坏习惯则反过来：拆掉触发它的线索、增加它的阻力。她最想纠正的迷思是——把行为改变当成一场意志力的硬仗；在她看来，那恰恰是大多数人屡战屡败的原因。真正的高手，是悄悄重新设计自己的环境，让正确的事变成最省力的那条路。
wood.ideas_en:
Wood set out to answer a very ordinary, very tormenting question: why, when we plainly know what we should do (exercise, sleep early, scroll less), do we fail to do it year after year? Her answer is counterintuitive: because we overrate "deciding" and underrate "habit."
One of her most-cited findings: about 40% of our daily behavior is not freshly decided in the moment but a habit repeated automatically in a fixed context. You think you spend the day "making choices," but nearly half the time you're being led by environmental cues — walk into the kitchen and open the fridge, sink into the couch and reach for the phone, hit 3 p.m. and crave coffee. A habit is essentially a loop: a context cue (place, time, the preceding action, a mood) triggers a fixed behavior, the behavior delivers some reward, and the reward tightens the cue-behavior link until it runs without thought, all but bypassing consciousness. This automation lives mostly in the brain's deeper basal ganglia rather than the deliberating prefrontal cortex — which is why "figuring it out and resolving to change" rarely shifts it, since resolve draws on a different system.
This is exactly why we know yet don't do: knowing is the slow system's job, but whether we act is often decided by the fast system's habits. So her core stance is practical, even a little cold-water: stop worshiping willpower. Research shows the people who sustain good behavior over the long run usually aren't those with exceptional self-control, but those who place themselves in environments that demand little self-control. Want to exercise more? Put your running shoes by the door, pick a gym on your commute — reduce friction for the good behavior. Want to scroll less? Delete the app, leave the phone in another room — add friction to the bad one. Changing the situation is more reliable than changing your heart.
She names three ingredients for forming a habit: a stable context (do it in the same place, at the same time, repeatedly), enough repetition (long enough to automate the action — on average a good while, not the mythical "21 days"), and an immediate reward (a little payoff right after, so the brain wants to come back). Breaking a bad habit runs in reverse: dismantle the cue that triggers it and raise its friction. The myth she most wants to correct is treating behavior change as a pitched battle of willpower; in her view that's precisely why most people keep losing. The real adepts quietly redesign their environment so the right thing becomes the path of least resistance.

assessments.text: 伍德与合作者的一项日记研究发现，人们约 43% 的日常行为在相同情境中重复发生、出于习惯而非当下决定——这成为习惯科学最常被引用的数据之一。
《掌控习惯》《习惯的力量》等大众读物，把伍德这一脉实验室研究——情境线索、重复与奖励如何铸成自动行为——带给了普通读者。

assessments_en.text: A diary study by Wood and colleagues found that roughly 43% of everyday behavior recurs in the same context out of habit rather than fresh decision — one of the most-cited figures in habit science.
Mass-market books like Atomic Habits and The Power of Habit carried the lab science in Wood's line — how context cues, repetition, and reward forge automatic behavior — to general readers.

quotes: 我们以为是自己在做决定，其实近四成的日常都是习惯替我们做的。（大意）
想改变行为，别只靠下决心，去改变你所处的情境。（大意）
quotes_en: We think we're deciding, but nearly 40% of daily life is habit deciding for us. (paraphrased)
To change behavior, don't just resolve harder — change the situation you're in. (paraphrased)
works: 关于习惯与自动化行为的系列实证研究
works_en: a body of empirical research on habit and automaticity
wood.lineage: 承接威廉·詹姆斯以来对『习惯』的关注，并与神经科学对基底神经节、自动化行为的研究相接；其情境与摩擦的思想，被《掌控习惯》等通俗写作进一步普及。
wood.lineage_en: She continues a line of attention to "habit" reaching back to William James, joined to neuroscience on the basal ganglia and automatic behavior; her emphasis on context and friction was further popularized by works such as Atomic Habits.
wood.trivia: 她常提醒人们一个反直觉的事实：那些看起来『特别自律』的人，往往不是更能咬牙硬撑，而是早早把生活安排成了不太需要硬撑的样子。
wood.trivia_en: She likes to point out a counterintuitive fact: people who look exceptionally "disciplined" usually aren't gritting their teeth harder — they've arranged their lives so that little teeth-gritting is needed.

beauvoir.bio: 1908–1986，法国存在主义哲学家、作家、女性主义理论家。生于巴黎天主教中产家庭，索邦大学哲学高材生，在备考最高教师资格考试（agrégation）时认识萨特，二人结成终身的开放式伴侣关系。1949 年出版《第二性》，成为现代女性主义的奠基之作。她拒绝只被当作『萨特的伴侣』，是 20 世纪最重要的哲学家与公共知识分子之一。
beauvoir.bio_en: 1908–1986, a French existentialist philosopher, writer, and feminist theorist. Born in Paris to a Catholic middle-class family, she was a brilliant philosophy student at the Sorbonne; while preparing for the agrégation she met Sartre, with whom she formed a lifelong open partnership. Her 1949 book The Second Sex became a founding work of modern feminism. Refusing to be seen merely as "Sartre's companion," she stands among the most important philosophers and public intellectuals of the twentieth century.
beauvoir.ideas:
波伏娃把存在主义的核心命题——『存在先于本质』，人没有被预先写定的本质，而是通过选择不断造就自己——推到了它最尖锐的社会处境里。她最著名的一句话是：『女人不是天生的，而是后天被塑造成的。』意思是：『女性气质』不是生理决定的命运，而是社会一层层教化、规训出来的角色。这一句把『天经地义』变成了『历史造物』，也就把它变成了可以质疑、可以改变的东西。
在《第二性》里她提出一个贯穿全书的结构：男性被设为『主体』（自我、标准、普遍的人），女性则被设为『他者』（the Other）——被定义、被观看、被当作相对于男人而存在的第二性。她追问：女性如何一步步被困在『内在性』（internal、重复、依附的生活）里，而被剥夺了通往『超越性』（transcendence、去开创、去行动、去自我实现）的机会。她的解放主张不是让女人变成男人，而是让女人也能成为自由的、自我筹划的主体。
在伦理学上（《模糊性的伦理学》），她不接受『既然没有上帝、一切皆虚无』的虚无主义。她认为：正因为人是自由的、生命是有限的、没有现成答案，我们才必须为自己和彼此的自由负责——真正的伦理，是在承认这种『模糊与不确定』的前提下，仍然选择投身、行动、对他人的自由负责。晚年她又写《论老年》，揭露社会如何把老人推入沉默与无用，是最早严肃对待衰老处境的哲学著作之一。
beauvoir.ideas_en:
Beauvoir pushed existentialism's core claim—"existence precedes essence," the idea that we have no pre-written nature but make ourselves through our choices—into its sharpest social setting. Her most famous line is: "One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman." Femininity, she argued, is not a biological destiny but a role drilled in, layer by layer, by society. That single sentence turns what looks "natural and self-evident" into a historical product—and therefore into something that can be questioned and changed.
In The Second Sex she lays out a structure that runs through the whole book: man is set up as the "Subject" (the self, the norm, the universal human), while woman is cast as the "Other"—defined, looked at, existing only relative to man, the second sex. She asks how women come to be trapped in "immanence" (a repetitive, dependent life) and denied access to "transcendence" (the freedom to initiate, to act, to realize oneself). Her call for liberation is not for women to become men, but for women, too, to become free, self-projecting subjects.
In ethics (The Ethics of Ambiguity) she refused the nihilist conclusion that "since there is no God, nothing matters." Precisely because we are free, life is finite, and there are no ready-made answers, she held, we are responsible for our own freedom and for one another's. Genuine ethics means choosing to commit and to act while owning that ambiguity. Late in life she wrote The Coming of Age, exposing how society pushes the old into silence and uselessness—one of the first philosophical works to take aging seriously.

assessments.by: 对第二波女性主义的影响
assessments.text: 《第二性》被公认为现代女性主义的奠基文本，深刻影响了贝蒂·弗里丹、凯特·米利特乃至后来的朱迪斯·巴特勒（性别『操演』论可上溯她『成为女人』的洞见）；尽管出版时曾被梵蒂冈列入禁书目录、并遭右翼猛烈攻击。

assessments.by: 长期被低估的哲学原创性
assessments.text: 她生前常被定位为萨特思想的『追随者』；但后世研究（如对《模糊性的伦理学》《皮洛士与西涅阿斯》的重估）日益指出，她在伦理与他者问题上有独立且早于萨特的贡献，是不折不扣的一流哲学家。

assessments_en.text: The Second Sex is widely regarded as a founding text of modern feminism, deeply shaping Betty Friedan, Kate Millett, and later Judith Butler (whose notion of gender as "performance" traces back to Beauvoir's insight that one "becomes" a woman)—even though the Vatican placed the book on its Index of Forbidden Books and the right attacked it fiercely.

In her lifetime she was often filed as a "follower" of Sartre; later scholarship (reassessing The Ethics of Ambiguity and Pyrrhus and Cineas) increasingly shows that her contributions on ethics and the problem of the Other were independent and in some respects ahead of Sartre's—marking her as a first-rate philosopher in her own right.

quotes: 女人不是天生的，而是后天被塑造成的。（《第二性》）
人之所以伟大，正因为他所处的境况是无可救药的；他明知如此，仍要去行动、去爱、去创造。（《模糊性的伦理学》大意）
quotes_en: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman. (The Second Sex)
It is in the knowledge of the genuine conditions of our life that we must draw our strength to live and our reason for acting. (The Ethics of Ambiguity)
works_en: The Mandarins (winner of the Prix Goncourt)
beauvoir.lineage: 汲取黑格尔的『主奴辩证法』与承认理论、胡塞尔与海德格尔的现象学，与萨特的存在主义相互砥砺；上承她所批判与改造的卢梭、笛卡尔身心传统；下启第二波女性主义（弗里丹、米利特）与性别理论（巴特勒）。
beauvoir.lineage_en: She drew on Hegel's master–slave dialectic and theory of recognition and on the phenomenology of Husserl and Heidegger, sharpening her thought alongside Sartre's existentialism; she engaged and reworked the Rousseauian and Cartesian traditions she criticized; and she opened the way for second-wave feminism (Friedan, Millett) and gender theory (Butler).
beauvoir.trivia: 她与萨特维持了 51 年不结婚、不独占、彼此坦白的开放式关系，二人死后合葬于巴黎蒙帕纳斯公墓；1946 年的小说《人都是要死的》以一个被诅咒永生的男人为主角，借他的厌倦与虚无，反推出『正因为会死，人的选择与爱才有分量』。
beauvoir.trivia_en: She and Sartre kept an open, unmarried, non-exclusive, radically candid partnership for 51 years and are buried together in Paris's Montparnasse Cemetery; her 1946 novel All Men Are Mortal centers on a man cursed with immortality whose boredom and emptiness make the reverse case—that it is precisely because we die that our choices and our love carry weight.

thiel.bio: 1967 年生于德国法兰克福，幼年随家移居美国。斯坦福哲学本科、法学博士。1998 年共同创办 PayPal（『PayPal 黑帮』的核心人物），2004 年成为 Facebook 第一位外部投资人，后联合创办大数据公司 Palantir，并设立创投基金 Founders Fund。他既是硅谷最有影响力的投资人之一，也是一位以『逆向思维』著称、立场极具争议的公共人物。
thiel.bio_en: Born in 1967 in Frankfurt, Germany, he moved to the United States as a child. He holds a philosophy degree and a law doctorate from Stanford. In 1998 he co-founded PayPal (a central figure of the "PayPal Mafia"), in 2004 became Facebook's first outside investor, later co-founded the big-data firm Palantir, and set up the venture fund Founders Fund. He is at once one of Silicon Valley's most influential investors and a deeply controversial public figure known for "contrarian" thinking.
thiel.ideas:
蒂尔思想的轴心是一道面试题：『有什么重要的真相，是几乎没人同意你的？』他认为真正的价值创造，永远来自少数人看到、多数人还没看到的逆向真相——随大流只能赚到平均回报。
在《从 0 到 1》里，他区分两种创业：『从 1 到 n』是复制已有的东西（把成功的模式再做一遍），『从 0 到 1』是创造前所未有的新东西。他主张创业者应当追求『垄断』而非『竞争』——这里的垄断不是指作恶，而是指做出独一无二、别人无法替代的产品，从而摆脱在红海里互相压价的消耗。他那句『竞争是留给失败者的』正是此意：激烈竞争往往意味着大家都在做同质的事、谁也赚不到钱。他还区分『明确的乐观』（相信未来更好，并且有具体计划去建造它）与『模糊的乐观』（笼统地觉得会变好却无所作为），批评当代社会滑向了后者，失去了规划宏大未来的勇气——他著名的抱怨是：『我们想要会飞的汽车，结果却只得到了 140 个字符。』
蒂尔深受其斯坦福老师、思想家勒内·基拉尔的影响：基拉尔的『模仿欲望』理论认为，人的欲望大多是模仿他人而来——我们想要某样东西，常常只因为别人也想要，于是陷入彼此较劲的竞争与冲突。蒂尔把这套理论用到商业（别盲目挤进众人争抢的赛道）与社会观察上。他也是一位坚定的技术乐观主义者与自由意志论者，公开主张人类应当用技术延长寿命、抵抗衰老——把死亡当成一个有待攻克的问题，而非必须接受的命运。
thiel.ideas_en:
The axis of Thiel's thinking is an interview question: "What important truth do very few people agree with you on?" Real value creation, he believes, always comes from a contrarian truth a few people see before the crowd does—following the herd earns only average returns.
In Zero to One he distinguishes two kinds of venture: going "from 1 to n" is copying what already exists (repeating a proven model), while going "from 0 to 1" is creating something genuinely new. He argues founders should seek "monopoly" rather than "competition"—not monopoly in the predatory sense, but building a product so unique and irreplaceable that you escape the margin-grinding bloodbath of a red ocean. His line "competition is for losers" means just this: fierce competition usually signals everyone is doing the same thing and no one is making money. He also distinguishes "definite optimism" (believing the future will be better and having a concrete plan to build it) from "indefinite optimism" (a vague sense things will improve, with no action), and faults modern society for sliding into the latter, losing the nerve to plan grand futures—hence his famous complaint: "We wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters."
Thiel was deeply shaped by his Stanford teacher, the thinker René Girard, whose theory of "mimetic desire" holds that most human wanting is imitated from others—we crave a thing largely because others crave it, trapping us in rivalry and conflict. Thiel applied this to business (don't blindly pile into the lane everyone is fighting over) and to social observation. A committed techno-optimist and libertarian, he has publicly argued that humans should use technology to extend lifespan and resist aging—treating death as a problem to be solved rather than a fate to be accepted.

assessments.text: 他被广泛视为当代最具影响力的科技投资人之一：早期投资 Facebook、共同缔造 PayPal 与 Palantir，所著《从 0 到 1》成为创业圈的现象级读物，其『垄断/逆向思维』框架被反复引用。
他是公认极具争议的人物：政治上活跃且立场鲜明、资助诉讼搞垮媒体 Gawker、对民主与高等教育的某些言论广受批评。许多人欣赏其智识胆识，也有许多人强烈反对其政治主张——评价两极。

assessments_en.by: How Silicon Valley's venture world sees him
assessments_en.text: He is widely regarded as one of the most influential tech investors of his era: an early Facebook backer and co-creator of PayPal and Palantir, his book Zero to One became a phenomenon in startup circles, and its "monopoly/contrarian" framework is endlessly cited.

He is, by common acknowledgment, a highly controversial figure: politically active and outspoken, he bankrolled the litigation that destroyed the media outlet Gawker, and some of his remarks on democracy and higher education have drawn sharp criticism. Many admire his intellectual nerve; many strongly oppose his politics—opinion is polarized.

quotes: 竞争是留给失败者的。（《从 0 到 1》）
我们想要会飞的汽车，结果却只得到了 140 个字符。（Founders Fund 宣言）
quotes_en: Competition is for losers. (Zero to One)
We wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters. (Founders Fund manifesto)
works: 《从 0 到 1：开启商业与未来的秘密》（与布莱克·马斯特斯合著）
works_en: Zero to One: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future (with Blake Masters)
thiel.lineage: 思想上深受勒内·基拉尔『模仿欲望』理论影响，并融合古典自由意志论（哈耶克、兰德一脉）；实践上是『PayPal 黑帮』网络的核心，深刻塑造了硅谷的『创始人崇拜』与科技乐观主义文化。
thiel.lineage_en: Intellectually he was deeply shaped by René Girard's theory of mimetic desire, fused with classical libertarianism (a lineage running through Hayek and Rand); in practice he is a hub of the "PayPal Mafia" network and has profoundly shaped Silicon Valley's "founder" cult and techno-optimist culture.
thiel.trivia: 他在斯坦福师从勒内·基拉尔，基拉尔的理论成为其商业判断的底层操作系统；他公开签署了人体冷冻协议、并长期资助抗衰老研究（如 Methuselah 基金会），是『向死亡宣战』这一硅谷潮流最直言不讳的推手之一。
thiel.trivia_en: At Stanford he studied under René Girard, whose theory became the operating system beneath his business judgment; he has publicly signed up for cryonic preservation and long funded anti-aging research (such as the Methuselah Foundation), making him one of the most outspoken champions of Silicon Valley's "war on death."

feynman.bio: 1918–1988，美国理论物理学家，因量子电动力学（QED）的奠基性工作与朝永振一郎、施温格共获 1965 年诺贝尔物理学奖。曾参与曼哈顿计划，长期任教于加州理工。他以惊人的物理直觉、独树一帜的教学、以及对一切的好奇心（开保险柜、打邦戈鼓）闻名，是 20 世纪最富个人魅力的科学家之一。
feynman.bio_en: 1918–1988, an American theoretical physicist who shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physics with Sin-Itiro Tomonaga and Julian Schwinger for foundational work on quantum electrodynamics (QED). He worked on the Manhattan Project and taught for years at Caltech. Famous for his stunning physical intuition, his singular teaching, and his curiosity about everything (cracking safes, playing the bongos), he was one of the twentieth century's most charismatic scientists.
feynman.ideas:
费曼留给物理学最深的印记是『费曼图』与『路径积分』。在他之前，量子电动力学的计算冗长晦涩；他发明了一套画小图来代表粒子相互作用的方法，把繁复的计算变成可视、可操作的图形——今天全世界的物理学家仍在用。他的『路径积分』表述更给出一种惊人的图景：一个粒子从 A 到 B，并非只走一条路，而是『同时尝试所有可能的路径』，最终的概率由这些路径叠加而成。
但费曼真正影响最广的，是他对『科学态度』的示范。他反复强调一条原则：『你绝不能欺骗自己——而你恰恰是最容易被自己骗到的人。』科学方法的核心，在他看来不是积累正确答案，而是一套不让自己自欺的纪律：诚实面对证据、主动去找能推翻自己的反例。他用『草包族科学』（cargo cult science）讽刺那些只学了科学的外表、却没有这种诚实内核的研究——形式齐全，飞机却永远不会降落。
他还是位了不起的『启蒙者』与预言家。1959 年的演讲《底下的空间还大得很》提前勾勒了纳米技术的图景；他最早设想用量子系统来做计算（量子计算的思想源头之一）。他对生命与死亡也有一句著名的物理学家式观察：在全部生物学里，找不到任何迹象表明死亡是必然的。在他看来，凡是原子按物理定律运作能解释的，原则上都可被理解、被改变——这种『万物皆可追问』的乐观，正是他留给后人的精神底色。
feynman.ideas_en:
Feynman's deepest mark on physics is the "Feynman diagram" and the "path integral." Before him, calculations in quantum electrodynamics were long and opaque; he invented a way of drawing little pictures to represent particle interactions, turning forbidding algebra into something visual and workable—physicists worldwide still use it today. His path-integral formulation offers an astonishing picture: a particle going from A to B does not take a single route but "tries all possible paths at once," the final probability built from the sum over those paths.
But Feynman's widest influence was as a model of the scientific attitude. He hammered one principle: "The first principle is that you must not fool yourself—and you are the easiest person to fool." The core of method, for him, is not piling up correct answers but a discipline against self-deception: facing evidence honestly and actively hunting for what could prove you wrong. He coined "cargo cult science" to mock research that copies the outward form of science but lacks that honest core—everything looks right, yet the plane never lands.
He was also a remarkable popularizer and prophet. His 1959 talk "There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom" foreshadowed nanotechnology; he was among the first to imagine using quantum systems to compute (a seed of quantum computing). On life and death he made a famously physicist-like observation: in all of biology there is no clue that death is inevitable. Anything that atoms obeying physical law can produce, he held, can in principle be understood—and changed. That "everything is open to question" optimism is the spirit he left behind.

assessments.text: 他被同行公认为 20 世纪最伟大的物理学家之一；其同事弗里曼·戴森称他兼具魔术师般的直觉与小丑般的幽默。《费曼物理学讲义》至今被视为物理教学的经典。

assessments.by: 公共形象与挑战者号调查
assessments.text: 1986 年挑战者号航天飞机失事，费曼作为调查委员会成员，在听证会上把 O 形密封圈泡进冰水、当众演示其在低温下失去弹性，一举点破事故根源——成为科学诚实直面权力的经典一幕。

assessments_en.text: His peers count him among the greatest physicists of the twentieth century; his colleague Freeman Dyson described him as having both a magician's intuition and a clown's humor. The Feynman Lectures on Physics remain a classic of physics teaching.

assessments_en.by: Public image and the Challenger inquiry
assessments_en.text: After the 1986 Challenger shuttle disaster, Feynman, serving on the investigation commission, dunked an O-ring seal into ice water during a hearing to show on live television that it lost its resilience in the cold—pinpointing the cause in one stroke, a classic image of scientific honesty confronting power.

quotes: 第一条原则是：你绝不能欺骗自己——而你恰恰是最容易被自己骗到的人。（加州理工毕业演讲）
在全部生物科学里，没有任何线索表明死亡是必然的，这是最值得注意的事情之一。（讲演大意）
quotes_en: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself—and you are the easiest person to fool. (Caltech commencement address)
It is one of the most remarkable things that in all of the biological sciences there is no clue as to the necessity of death. (from a lecture, paraphrased)
works: 《量子电动力学：光与物质的奇异理论》
演讲《底下的空间还大得很》
works_en: QED: The Strange Theory of Light and Matter
What Do You Care What Other People Think?
The lecture "There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom"
feynman.lineage: 师从约翰·惠勒，受狄拉克的量子理论启发；与施温格、朝永振一郎各自独立完成 QED 的重整化而共获诺奖；其『底下的空间还大得很』启发了纳米科技，量子计算设想则启发了后来的量子信息领域。
feynman.lineage_en: He studied under John Wheeler and was inspired by Dirac's quantum theory; he, Schwinger, and Tomonaga independently achieved the renormalization of QED and shared the Nobel; his "Plenty of Room at the Bottom" inspired nanotechnology, and his idea of quantum computation seeded the later field of quantum information.
feynman.trivia: 他在洛斯阿拉莫斯造原子弹期间以撬开同事的保险柜（里面装着核机密）为乐，借此戳破军方的安全漏洞；他还痴迷打邦戈鼓、画画、研究玛雅象形文字，把『找出事物运作之道的乐趣』当作一生的座右铭。
feynman.trivia_en: While building the atomic bomb at Los Alamos he amused himself by cracking colleagues' safes (which held nuclear secrets), exposing the military's security holes; he was also obsessed with playing the bongos, drawing, and deciphering Maya hieroglyphs, and took "the pleasure of finding things out" as the motto of his life.

dawkins.bio: 1941 年生于肯尼亚内罗毕（父母为英国人），英国演化生物学家、动物行为学家，长期任教于牛津大学，曾任牛津『公众理解科学』教席。1976 年的《自私的基因》使他声名大噪，既是当代最有影响力的科普作家之一，也是『新无神论』四骑士之一。
dawkins.bio_en: Born in 1941 in Nairobi, Kenya (to British parents), he is a British evolutionary biologist and ethologist who taught for years at Oxford, where he held the chair for the Public Understanding of Science. His 1976 book The Selfish Gene made his name; he is both one of the most influential popular-science writers of his era and one of the "Four Horsemen" of New Atheism.
dawkins.ideas:
道金斯最核心的贡献，是把演化的视角从『个体』或『物种』下沉到了『基因』。在《自私的基因》里他提出一个反直觉却极有解释力的图景：自然选择真正作用的单位是基因，而我们这些生物体，不过是基因为了让自己被复制下去而打造的『生存机器』（survival machine）。所谓基因『自私』，不是说它有意图，而是说：那些更善于让自己被复制的基因会留存、扩散，于是世界上充满了『擅长延续自己』的基因。这一框架漂亮地解释了利他行为为何存在——比如父母为子女牺牲、蜜蜂为蜂群献身，从基因角度看其实是在保全自己的副本（亲缘选择）。
他还创造了一个今天人人挂在嘴边的词：『模因』（meme）。他设想，文化（曲调、口号、观念、时尚）也像基因一样，会被复制、变异、被选择而流行——观念也在进行着自己的『演化』，这成了后来研究网络爆款、文化传播的思想源头。
在《盲眼钟表匠》里，他回应了一个古老的诘难：精巧如眼睛的器官，难道不需要一位设计者吗？他的回答是『累积选择』：复杂不必出自蓝图，只需『微小随机变异 + 一代代非随机的存活筛选』，经过漫长时间的累积，就能从简单中『盲目地』雕出惊人的精巧——这个过程没有目的、没有远见，却足以造出整个生物界。他晚年以《上帝错觉》成为最直言不讳的无神论者之一，主张以科学与理性、而非信仰与权威来理解世界。
dawkins.ideas_en:
Dawkins's central contribution was to drop the lens of evolution from the "individual" or "species" down to the "gene." In The Selfish Gene he offered a counterintuitive but powerfully explanatory picture: the true unit on which natural selection acts is the gene, and we organisms are merely "survival machines" built by genes to get themselves copied. Calling a gene "selfish" doesn't mean it has intentions; it means genes better at getting themselves replicated will persist and spread, so the world fills up with genes that are "good at perpetuating themselves." This framework elegantly explains why altruism exists—parents sacrificing for offspring, bees dying for the hive—since from the gene's view they are preserving copies of themselves (kin selection).
He also coined a word now on everyone's lips: the "meme." He proposed that culture (tunes, slogans, ideas, fashions) also gets copied, mutated, and selected like genes—ideas undergo their own "evolution." This became a seed for later studies of viral content and cultural transmission.
In The Blind Watchmaker he answered an old challenge: surely an organ as intricate as the eye needs a designer? His reply is "cumulative selection": complexity needs no blueprint, only "small random variation plus the non-random survival of each generation," accumulated over vast time, can "blindly" carve astonishing intricacy out of simplicity—a process with no purpose and no foresight, yet enough to produce the whole living world. Late in life, with The God Delusion, he became one of the most outspoken atheists, arguing that we should understand the world through science and reason rather than faith and authority.

assessments.text: 他与古生物学家斯蒂芬·杰·古尔德长期论战：古尔德批评其『基因中心论』过于还原、忽视个体与更高层次的选择，并以『间断平衡』强调演化的偶然与跳跃。这场『达尔文主义内部之争』丰富了整个演化生物学。
他被公认为当代最杰出的科学传播者之一，《自私的基因》四十余年长销不衰；但其在《上帝错觉》中对宗教的强硬批判，也使他在公共领域评价两极。

assessments_en.text: He long sparred with the paleontologist Stephen Jay Gould, who criticized his "gene's-eye" view as overly reductive and dismissive of individual- and higher-level selection, and who stressed (via "punctuated equilibrium") the contingency and jumps in evolution. This "argument within Darwinism" enriched the whole field of evolutionary biology.

assessments_en.by: His standing as a science writer
assessments_en.text: He is widely regarded as one of the finest science communicators of his time, and The Selfish Gene has stayed in print for over forty years; but his fierce critique of religion in The God Delusion has also made opinion of him sharply polarized in the public arena.

quotes: 我们都是生存机器——被盲目编程、用以保存那些名为基因的自私分子的机器人载具。（《自私的基因》）
我们终将死去，而这正使我们成为幸运儿。（《解析彩虹》大意）
quotes_en: We are survival machines—robot vehicles blindly programmed to preserve the selfish molecules known as genes. (The Selfish Gene)
We are going to die, and that makes us the lucky ones. (Unweaving the Rainbow, paraphrased)
dawkins.lineage: 直承达尔文，并整合费舍尔的群体遗传学、汉密尔顿的亲缘选择、乔治·威廉斯与梅纳德·史密斯的基因中心论；他创造的『模因』开启了模因学，对演化心理学与文化演化研究影响深远。
dawkins.lineage_en: A direct heir of Darwin, he synthesized Fisher's population genetics, Hamilton's kin selection, and the gene-centric views of George Williams and Maynard Smith; his coinage of "meme" launched memetics and deeply influenced evolutionary psychology and the study of cultural evolution.
dawkins.trivia: 『模因』（meme）一词正是他 1976 年生造的，本意是『文化的基因』，没想到几十年后被互联网借去指代表情包与爆款梗；他与丹尼特、哈里斯、希钦斯并称新无神论『四骑士』。
dawkins.trivia_en: He coined the word "meme" in 1976 to mean a "gene of culture," never guessing the internet would borrow it decades later for image macros and viral jokes; with Dennett, Harris, and Hitchens he is counted among the "Four Horsemen" of New Atheism.

ramachandran.bio: 1951 年生于印度，神经科学家，加州大学圣迭戈分校大脑与认知研究中心主任。原本受训为医生，后转向行为神经病学，擅长从罕见的神经病例（幻肢、联觉、错认综合征）反推大脑与意识的运作，被达尔文学者理查德·道金斯誉为『神经科学界的马可·波罗』。
ramachandran.bio_en: Born in 1951 in India, he is a neuroscientist and director of the Center for Brain and Cognition at the University of California, San Diego. Originally trained as a physician, he turned to behavioral neurology, excelling at inferring how the brain and consciousness work from rare neurological cases (phantom limbs, synesthesia, misidentification syndromes)—Richard Dawkins dubbed him "the Marco Polo of neuroscience."
ramachandran.ideas:
拉马钱德兰的招牌方法，是把罕见而离奇的神经病例当作『打开大脑的窗口』：一个看似古怪的症状，往往泄露了正常大脑平时藏得很好的运作机制。
最著名的是他对『幻肢』的研究。许多截肢者会感到那条已不存在的肢体仍在，甚至剧痛难忍。他推断这是大脑皮层『重新布线』的结果——管理手的脑区因失去输入，被相邻的脸部脑区『侵占』，于是触摸脸竟会被感知成触摸幻手。据此他发明了极其廉价的『镜盒』：让患者把健全的手伸进镜箱，镜中影像看起来就像那条失去的手回来了，大脑被这一视觉骗局『安抚』，幻肢痛竟随之缓解——一个用大脑可塑性反向治病的漂亮例子。
他还深入研究『联觉』（如把数字看成有颜色）、『卡普格拉妄想』（坚信至亲被冒名顶替者掉包——他解释为『认脸的视觉通路』与『产生亲情感受的情绪通路』断了连接：看得出长得像妈妈，却感觉不到那份熟悉的情感，于是大脑只好编出『她是假的』）。他对镜像神经元寄予厚望，认为这类『看到别人做、自己脑中也激活』的神经元是共情与文化模仿的基础，甚至称其为『塑造文明的神经元』（这一论断学界仍有争议）。贯穿这一切的，是他对一个终极问题的痴迷：这一团一千多克的『果冻』，何以能思考无限、能反观自身、能生出『我』这个感觉？在他看来，自我并非一个固定的内核，而是大脑各系统协同『建构』出来的、可以被神经损伤拆解的东西。
ramachandran.ideas_en:
Ramachandran's signature method is to treat rare, bizarre neurological cases as "windows into the brain": a strange symptom often betrays the normally well-hidden machinery of the ordinary brain.
Most famous is his work on "phantom limbs." Many amputees feel that the missing limb is still there, sometimes in agonizing pain. He reasoned that this is the result of cortical "rewiring"—the brain region that managed the hand, deprived of input, gets "invaded" by the neighboring face region, so that touching the face is perceived as touching the phantom hand. From this he invented an absurdly cheap "mirror box": the patient puts the intact hand into a mirrored box, the reflection looks like the lost hand has returned, the brain is "soothed" by this visual trick, and the phantom pain eases—an elegant case of curing the brain by exploiting its own plasticity.
He also studied "synesthesia" (seeing numbers as colored) and the "Capgras delusion" (the conviction that a loved one has been swapped for an impostor—which he explained as a severed link between the visual pathway that recognizes faces and the emotional pathway that generates feelings of kinship: you can see she looks like mother but feel none of the familiar warmth, so the brain confabulates that "she's a fake"). He placed great hope in mirror neurons—cells that fire both when you act and when you watch another act—seeing them as the basis of empathy and cultural imitation, even calling them "the neurons that shaped civilization" (a claim still debated in the field). Running through all of it is his fascination with one ultimate question: how can this kilo-and-a-half lump of "jelly" contemplate infinity, reflect on itself, and generate the feeling of "I"? For him the self is not a fixed inner core but something the brain's systems jointly "construct"—and that neurological damage can take apart.

assessments.text: 理查德·道金斯称他为『神经科学界的马可·波罗』，赞其大胆探入认知的未知疆域；他善于用最简陋的工具（镜子、棉签）做出深刻发现，被视为『低成本巧思』实验的典范。
也有同行认为他的若干理论（尤其对镜像神经元在共情、自闭症、文明起源中作用的宏大推断）过度依赖个案、推论偏大胆、缺乏大样本验证；其洞见富启发性，但部分结论仍待更严格的证据。

assessments_en.text: Richard Dawkins called him "the Marco Polo of neuroscience," praising his bold forays into uncharted cognitive territory; adept at making profound discoveries with the crudest tools (mirrors, cotton swabs), he is seen as a model of "low-cost, ingenious" experiment.

Some peers hold that several of his theories (especially his sweeping inferences about mirror neurons in empathy, autism, and the origins of civilization) lean too heavily on single cases, reach too far, and lack large-sample confirmation; his insights are stimulating, but some conclusions await more rigorous evidence.

quotes: 这团一千多克的果冻——你的大脑——竟能思索星际空间的浩瀚，这本身就是奇迹。（演讲大意）
我们能用一面普通的镜子，骗过大脑、抚平一条根本不存在的手臂的疼痛。（《脑中魅影》大意）
quotes_en: This kilo-and-a-half of jelly—your brain—can contemplate the vastness of interstellar space; that itself is a marvel. (from a talk, paraphrased)
With an ordinary mirror we can fool the brain and soothe the pain of an arm that no longer exists. (Phantoms in the Brain, paraphrased)
works: 《脑中魅影：探索心智之谜》（与桑德拉·布莱克斯利合著）
works_en: Phantoms in the Brain (with Sandra Blakeslee)
A Brief Tour of Human Consciousness
ramachandran.lineage: 承继布罗卡、格施温德以降的行为神经病学传统——从脑损伤推断功能定位；其工作推动了关于神经可塑性、镜像神经元、共情与神经美学的研究，并把神经科学带向大众。
ramachandran.lineage_en: He carries on the behavioral-neurology tradition from Broca and Geschwind—inferring functional localization from brain damage; his work spurred research on neural plasticity, mirror neurons, empathy, and neuroaesthetics, and brought neuroscience to a wide public.
ramachandran.trivia: 他发明的『镜盒』疗法成本几乎为零，却切实缓解了无数截肢者与中风患者的幻肢痛与瘫痪，至今仍在临床使用；他常说自己最好的实验器材是『一面镜子和一根棉签』。
ramachandran.trivia_en: His "mirror box" therapy costs almost nothing yet genuinely relieves phantom-limb pain and post-stroke paralysis in countless patients and is still used clinically; he likes to say his best lab equipment is "a mirror and a cotton swab."

sushi.bio: 1037–1101，字子瞻，号东坡居士，北宋眉州眉山（今属四川）人。诗、词、文、书、画无所不精，与父苏洵、弟苏辙合称『三苏』，名列『唐宋八大家』。一生因卷入新旧党争而屡遭贬谪，从黄州、惠州一路远至海南儋州；却在颠沛中活出旷达通透，是中国文化史上最受爱戴的全才之一。
sushi.bio_en: 1037–1101, courtesy name Zizhan, art name Dongpo Jushi ("the Recluse of the Eastern Slope"), a native of Meishan in Mei Prefecture (in today's Sichuan) under the Northern Song. A master of poetry, lyric song (ci), prose, calligraphy, and painting alike, he is grouped with his father Su Xun and brother Su Zhe as the "Three Sus" and ranks among the "Eight Great Prose Masters of the Tang and Song." Caught in the factional strife over reform, he was repeatedly exiled—from Huangzhou and Huizhou all the way to distant Danzhou on Hainan island—yet through all the upheaval he lived with a luminous equanimity, making him one of the best-loved all-round geniuses in Chinese cultural history.
sushi.ideas:
苏轼的过人之处，在于把儒、释、道三家熔成一种可以安身立命的生活智慧，再以绝顶的文字把它说得动人。儒家给他入世的担当（做官时兴水利、办医坊、赈饥荒），道家给他顺应自然的从容，佛家（禅宗）给他看破执着的清明——三者在他身上不是教条，而是顺逆之间随手取用的定力。
他最深的一层思想，凝在贬谪黄州时写的《赤壁赋》里。面对长江明月，他先是哀叹人生短暂如蜉蝣、羡慕江水无穷；转念却悟出：『自其变者而观之，则天地曾不能以一瞬；自其不变者而观之，则物与我皆无尽也。』——若只盯着变化，连天地都留不住一瞬；可若从『不变』的角度看，江水虽逝而长在、明月虽缺而长圆，我与万物本就同样无穷无尽。他由此把对『长生不老』的痴望，化解成一种当下即足的丰盈：清风明月『取之无禁，用之不竭』，何必另求长生？
这种『旷达』在《定风波》里更见洒脱：风雨途中他『竹杖芒鞋轻胜马』，归来时『也无风雨也无晴』——把人生的顺逆都看淡，心便不再被天气牵着走。他的艺术观同样自由：论画反对只求『形似』（『论画以形似，见与儿童邻』），主张传达内在神韵；写字作文讲究如行云流水、自然天成。这套『在有限里活出无限、在风雨里活出晴明』的态度，正是他留给后人最实用的功课。
sushi.ideas_en:
Su Shi's genius lay in fusing Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism into a livable wisdom—and then saying it in matchless prose and verse. Confucianism gave him worldly responsibility (in office he built waterworks, founded clinics, relieved famines); Daoism gave him an easy accord with nature; Chan (Zen) Buddhism gave him the clarity to see through attachment. In him these were not doctrines but a composure he could draw on at will, in fortune and misfortune alike.
His deepest thought crystallizes in the "Red Cliff Rhapsody," written in exile at Huangzhou. Gazing at the great river and the moon, he first laments how fleeting human life is, brief as a mayfly, and envies the river's endlessness; then he turns and realizes: "Seen from the side of change, heaven and earth cannot last even an instant; seen from the side of the changeless, all things and I alike are inexhaustible." If you fix only on change, not even heaven and earth hold for a moment; but viewed through the "changeless," the river flows yet endures, the moon wanes yet is forever full, and I and the ten thousand things are equally without end. Thus he dissolves the craving for bodily immortality into a fullness sufficient in the present: the clear breeze and bright moon are "inexhaustible, free for the taking"—why seek to live forever?
This "broad-minded transcendence" shows even more freely in "Calming the Wind and Waves": caught in a storm, "bamboo staff and straw sandals, lighter than a horse," he returns to find "neither wind and rain nor clearing skies"—taking life's ups and downs lightly so the heart is no longer jerked about by the weather. His view of art was equally free: he scorned judging a painting by mere "likeness" ("to judge a painting by its likeness is the view of a child") and prized conveying inner spirit; his calligraphy and prose aimed at the unforced naturalness of "moving clouds and flowing water." This stance—living the infinite within the finite, finding clear skies within the storm—is the most practical lesson he left behind.

assessments.text: 苏门弟子、与之并称『苏黄』的黄庭坚极推崇其书法，谓东坡书『学问文章之气，郁郁芊芊发于笔墨之间』，将其字的高妙归于胸中学养，而非单纯技巧。
现代作家林语堂为他立传《The Gay Genius》（苏东坡传），称他是一个『不可救药的乐天派』、一个具有现代精神的伟大人道主义者——把他的旷达介绍给了世界读者。

assessments_en.text: Huang Tingjian—of the Su circle and paired with him as "Su and Huang"—greatly admired his calligraphy, saying that in Dongpo's hand "the air of learning and letters wells up, lush and abundant, between brush and ink," crediting the excellence of his characters to the cultivation within him rather than to technique alone.

The modern writer Lin Yutang wrote his biography, The Gay Genius: The Life and Times of Su Tungpo, calling him an "incorrigible optimist" and a great humanist of modern spirit—introducing his broad-minded serenity to readers worldwide.

quotes: 哀吾生之须臾，羡长江之无穷……自其不变者而观之，则物与我皆无尽也。（《赤壁赋》）
回首向来萧瑟处，归去，也无风雨也无晴。（《定风波》）
但愿人长久，千里共婵娟。（《水调歌头》）
quotes_en: I grieve that my life is but an instant, and envy the endless flow of the great river … yet seen from the side of the changeless, all things and I alike are inexhaustible. (Red Cliff Rhapsody)
I turn to look back at the bleak place I came through—I go home, where there is neither wind and rain nor clearing skies. (Calming the Wind and Waves)
May we live long, and share the moon's beauty though a thousand miles apart. (Prelude to Water Melody)
works: 《黄州寒食帖》（书法，号称『天下第三行书』）
works_en: The First and Second Rhapsodies on the Red Cliff
"Charms of Niannu: Meditation on the Past at the Red Cliff"
"Prelude to Water Melody: When Will the Bright Moon Appear"
"Written on the Wall of West Forest Temple"
The Cold Food Observance scroll (calligraphy, called "the third-greatest running script under heaven")
sushi.lineage: 受知于文坛宗主欧阳修，承韩愈、欧阳修的古文运动而集大成；与父苏洵、弟苏辙合称『三苏』，书法与黄庭坚、米芾、蔡襄并称『宋四家』；开豪放词风，与辛弃疾并称『苏辛』，影响后世词坛与文人画甚巨。
sushi.lineage_en: Recognized by the literary arbiter Ouyang Xiu, he brought to fruition the classical-prose movement of Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu; with his father Su Xun and brother Su Zhe he forms the "Three Sus," and in calligraphy he is grouped with Huang Tingjian, Mi Fu, and Cai Xiang as the "Four Masters of the Song." He pioneered the "bold and unrestrained" school of ci lyrics—paired with Xin Qiji as "Su and Xin"—and profoundly influenced later lyric poetry and literati painting.
sushi.trivia: 他是个不折不扣的美食家，贬居黄州时发明了慢炖猪肉的吃法，后世称『东坡肉』；1079 年他因诗作被指讥讽朝政而下狱（『乌台诗案』），几遭杀身，获释后贬往黄州，自号『东坡居士』，反在逆境中写出一生最伟大的作品。
sushi.trivia_en: A genuine gourmet, while exiled in Huangzhou he devised a way of slow-braising pork later named "Dongpo pork" in his honor; in 1079 he was jailed when his poems were read as mocking the court (the "Crow Terrace Poetry Trial") and nearly executed, then banished to Huangzhou, where he took the name "Recluse of the Eastern Slope"—and, in adversity, wrote the greatest works of his life.

taleb.bio: 1960– ，黎巴嫩裔美国学者、前期权交易员、随机性与风险哲学家。在贝鲁特的富裕家庭长大，少年时亲历黎巴嫩内战，目睹一个看似稳定的世界顷刻崩塌——这成了他一生思想的底色。后赴美，在华尔街做了约二十年衍生品交易，靠为『罕见而剧烈的崩盘』下注获利，再转向写作与学术，现任纽约大学坦顿工程学院风险工程特聘教授。代表作『不确定性五部曲』（Incerto）让『黑天鹅』『反脆弱』成为日常词汇。
taleb.bio_en: 1960– , a Lebanese-American scholar, former options trader, and philosopher of randomness and risk. He grew up in a prosperous family in Beirut and as a teenager lived through the Lebanese civil war, watching a seemingly stable world collapse overnight — an experience that became the bedrock of his thinking. He later moved to the United States, traded derivatives on Wall Street for some two decades — profiting by betting on rare, violent crashes — then turned to writing and academia, and is now Distinguished Professor of Risk Engineering at NYU's Tandon School of Engineering. His five-volume Incerto made 'Black Swan' and 'antifragile' household terms.
taleb.ideas:
塔勒布一辈子在死磕一件事：我们对『不确定性』的理解几乎全是错的——而这些错误，恰恰在最关键、最罕见的时刻让我们栽最大的跟头。
他最有名的概念是『黑天鹅』：那种事前几乎没人预料、影响却极其巨大、事后却人人都说『早该看出来』的事件（金融海啸、疫情、某项颠覆性技术）。他的要害提醒是：历史不是被无数小事推着走的，而是被极少数黑天鹅决定的；可我们偏偏把全部精力花在预测那些可预测的小波动上，对真正改写命运的极端事件视而不见。打个比方：一只被农夫天天喂食的火鸡，会用上千天的数据『证明』人类爱它——直到感恩节前一天。它的错，不在数据太少，而在它要算的那件事，根本不在它见过的数据里。
由此引出他最重要的贡献——『反脆弱』（antifragile）。东西分三种：脆弱的，一震就碎（瓷器）；强韧的，扛得住冲击但不变（石头）；而反脆弱的，受到适度冲击反而变得更强——肌肉越练越壮、骨头越压越密、免疫系统靠接触少量病菌而强健、一个不断试错的创业生态因失败而进化。他说，活在一个充满黑天鹅的世界里，正确的目标不是徒劳地预测风险，而是把自己的处境调成反脆弱：让意外大多数时候伤不到你，偶尔还能让你受益。
配套的操作叫『杠铃策略』：别把赌注全押在中间地带，而是两头下注——绝大部分资源极度保守、稳如磐石（先防破产），留一小部分去博高风险高回报的机会。这样最坏不过损失那一小块，却始终留着被『正面黑天鹅』砸中的可能。
他还死磕一个道德原则——『skin in the game』（利益攸关）：你若不为自己的判断承担后果，就没资格替别人下判断。只动嘴给建议、却不必为后果负责的专家，把风险转嫁给整个社会的银行家，在他眼里都是系统里最危险的角色。古巴比伦的《汉谟拉比法典》早写明白：盖的房子塌了压死屋主，工匠偿命——这才叫对称。
他另有几把锋利的小刀。『Lindy 效应』：一样不会自然衰老的东西（一本书、一个观念、一项技术），已经活了多久，大概率还能再活同样久，所以经久不衰的旧东西，往往比时髦的新玩意儿更可信。『via negativa』（减法之道）：变好往往不是靠增添，而是靠删减——戒掉明显有害的（糖、债、噪音、毒朋友），比追逐复杂花哨的『优化』更可靠、更稳健。
贯穿这一切的，是他对『被随机性愚弄』的警惕：成功者总爱把运气讲成本事，而幸存者动人的故事，掩盖了所有沉默的失败者（你只看见中彩票的，看不见买了同样号码却落空的千万人）。在塔勒布看来，谦卑地承认自己不懂、为不可知留足缓冲，远比假装能预测未来更聪明，也更能让你在漫长的不确定里活下来。
taleb.ideas_en:
Taleb has spent his life hammering at one thing: our understanding of 'uncertainty' is almost entirely wrong — and those errors trip us hardest at the most crucial, rarest moments.
His most famous idea is the 'Black Swan': an event almost no one foresees, whose impact is enormous, and which everyone afterward claims they 'should have seen coming' (a financial crash, a pandemic, a disruptive technology). His sharp point: history is not pushed along by countless small events but decided by a handful of Black Swans — yet we pour all our effort into predicting the small, predictable wobbles and stay blind to the extremes that actually rewrite fate. Picture a turkey fed daily by a farmer: it amasses a thousand days of data 'proving' humans love it — right up to the day before Thanksgiving. Its mistake wasn't too little data; it was that the one thing it needed to reckon with lay entirely outside the data it had ever seen.
From this comes his most important contribution: the 'antifragile.' Things come in three kinds — the fragile, which shatters at a shock (porcelain); the robust, which withstands shocks unchanged (stone); and the antifragile, which a moderate shock makes stronger — muscle grows with strain, bone densifies under load, the immune system is fortified by small exposures, a trial-and-error startup ecology evolves through failure. In a world full of Black Swans, he says, the right goal isn't to vainly predict risk but to make your own position antifragile: let surprises mostly fail to hurt you, and occasionally even benefit you.
The matching tactic is the 'barbell strategy': don't bet everything on the middle ground; bet at both ends — keep the great bulk of your resources extremely conservative and rock-solid (guard against ruin first), and put a small slice into high-risk, high-reward bets. The worst case is losing that small slice, while you always keep the chance of being hit by a 'positive Black Swan.'
He also insists on a moral principle — 'skin in the game': if you don't bear the consequences of your judgment, you have no right to make it for others. The expert who only dispenses advice without answering for the outcome, the banker who offloads risk onto society at large — these, to him, are the system's most dangerous figures. Ancient Babylon's Code of Hammurabi spelled it out: if a house collapses and kills its owner, the builder is put to death — that is symmetry.
He carries a few other sharp little knives. The 'Lindy effect': for things that don't naturally age (a book, an idea, a technology), the longer they've already lasted, the longer they're likely to last still — so the enduring old often beats the fashionable new. 'Via negativa,' the way of subtraction: getting better usually comes not from adding but from removing — quitting the plainly harmful (sugar, debt, noise, toxic friends) is more reliable and robust than chasing elaborate 'optimization.'
Threading through it all is his wariness of being 'fooled by randomness': winners love to recast luck as skill, and the survivor's stirring story hides all the silent failures (you see the lottery winner, not the millions who played the same numbers and lost). For Taleb, humbly admitting you don't know and keeping a generous buffer against the unknowable is far smarter than pretending to predict the future — and far more likely to keep you alive through long stretches of uncertainty.

assessments.text: 将《黑天鹅》列入二战以来最具影响力的十二本书之一，称其重塑了大众对风险与罕见事件的理解。
经济学界与统计学界不乏批评，认为他的论证常以雄辩、格言和对人不对事的攻击代替严谨证明，文风傲慢、好斗，结论虽常被引用，方法却屡遭质疑。
公开表达过对塔勒布的赏识，认为他迫使更多人正视稀有而剧烈的风险、以及人类对随机性的系统性盲目。（观点大意，非逐字原话）

assessments_en.text: Listed The Black Swan among the twelve most influential books since World War II, crediting it with reshaping the public's grasp of risk and rare events.

Economists and statisticians have pushed back, arguing he often substitutes eloquence, aphorism, and ad hominem combat for rigorous proof; his style is held to be arrogant and pugnacious, his conclusions much-cited but his methods repeatedly questioned.

Publicly voiced his regard for Taleb, holding that he forced many more people to take seriously rare but violent risk and humanity's systematic blindness to randomness. (Paraphrase, not a verbatim quote.)

quotes: 错过一班火车，只有在你追着它跑时才令人痛苦。
风熄灭蜡烛，却助长大火——面对随机、不确定与混乱，你要做那团火，并祈求来风。
你绝无法用论证彻底说服一个人他错了；只有现实能。
quotes_en: Missing a train is only painful if you run after it.
Wind extinguishes a candle and energizes fire. Likewise with randomness, uncertainty, and chaos: be the fire and wish for the wind.
You will never fully convince someone that he is wrong; only reality can.
works: 《普罗克拉斯提斯之床》(格言集, The Bed of Procrustes, 2010)
《非对称风险 / 利益攸关》(Skin in the Game, 2018)
taleb.lineage: 思想上自认远绍古代怀疑主义者塞克斯都·恩披里柯与散文家蒙田（对人类自负的质疑）、斯多葛的塞内卡（如何面对命运与损失）；近世受卡尔·波普尔（可证伪与不可预测）、哈耶克（知识分散、计划之妄）影响；数学上师承分形几何之父曼德博，把『厚尾』『幂律』引入对极端事件的刻画。常与主流概率统计、效率市场理论及『预测专家』正面交锋。
taleb.lineage_en: He traces his lineage to the ancient skeptic Sextus Empiricus and the essayist Montaigne (their doubt of human conceit) and to the Stoic Seneca (on facing fate and loss); in modern times he draws on Karl Popper (falsifiability and unpredictability) and Hayek (dispersed knowledge, the folly of central planning); mathematically he studied under Benoit Mandelbrot, father of fractal geometry, importing 'fat tails' and power laws into the description of extreme events. He routinely clashes head-on with mainstream probability and statistics, efficient-market theory, and professional 'forecasters.'
taleb.trivia: 自称『practitioner-philosopher』（实践者哲学家），最瞧不起『毫无风险担当的纸上学者』；笃信只读经得起 Lindy 检验的古典旧书，热衷古希腊罗马文献与重量训练、长距离散步；2008 年金融危机中，他参与顾问的尾部风险基金大赚，使『黑天鹅』一词彻底走红；以在社交媒体上与人激烈论战、言辞犀利刻薄著称；坚持烹饪、举重与陪伴亲友，认为这些『有利益攸关、不可外包』的事才是真生活。
taleb.trivia_en: He calls himself a 'practitioner-philosopher' and has the deepest contempt for 'risk-free armchair scholars'; he reads chiefly old classics that pass the Lindy test, loves Greco-Roman texts, weightlifting, and long walks; during the 2008 financial crisis the tail-risk fund he advised profited heavily, propelling the term 'Black Swan' into the mainstream; he is famous for fierce, caustic combat with opponents on social media; and he insists that cooking, lifting, and being with family and friends — things with 'skin in the game' that can't be outsourced — are what real life is made of.

becker.bio: 1930–2014，美国经济学家，芝加哥大学教授，1992 年诺贝尔经济学奖得主。他把经济学的理性选择方法大胆地推进到一向被认为『不属于经济学』的人类行为——家庭、生育、婚姻与离婚、教育、犯罪、歧视、上瘾。早期被主流斥为离经叛道，晚年却被公认为 20 世纪下半叶最具影响力的经济学家之一，开创了现代『家庭经济学』与『人力资本』理论。
becker.bio_en: 1930–2014, an American economist and professor at the University of Chicago, winner of the 1992 Nobel Prize in Economics. He boldly extended the rational-choice methods of economics into domains long considered 'not economics' — the family, fertility, marriage and divorce, education, crime, discrimination, and addiction. Dismissed early on as heterodox, he came to be regarded as one of the most influential economists of the second half of the twentieth century, founding the modern 'economics of the family' and 'human capital' theory.
becker.ideas:
贝克尔的核心信念是：人在生活的几乎每个角落，都在『约束条件下做选择』——不只是买菜炒股，连结婚、离婚、上不上学、生几个孩子、甚至要不要犯罪，背后都有一笔成本-收益的账。这听起来冷冰冰，但威力在于：它让你能解释、甚至预测那些原本被归给『文化』『道德』『天性』的行为。
他一生最重要的贡献，是『人力资本』(human capital)：教育、技能、训练、健康都不是单纯的消费或开销，而是像买机器一样的投资——今天投入金钱与时间，是为了未来更高的产出与收入。个人为何上学、企业为何培训、人为何迁徙，都能用『投资回报』来理解。这一框架彻底改变了经济学看待人的方式，也是他获诺奖的核心理由。
他还把这套方法大胆推进到家庭——结婚、离婚、家务分工与生育，都可看成理性决策。其中著名的是生育的『数量-质量权衡』(quantity–quality trade-off)：当社会变富、教育回报升高，父母倾向给每个孩子更多投入，于是孩子的『质量』越贵，多生的边际代价就越高，理性选择往往偏向『少生精养』；母亲在职场能挣得越多，每生育一次的『时间机会成本』也越高。这解释了一个反直觉现象——越富裕的家庭与社会，往往生得越少。
同样的逻辑被他用到犯罪与歧视上。犯罪在他看来是对『预期收益与被惩罚概率及代价』的理性回应，威慑因此可被设计；歧视则对歧视者本人也有成本——拒绝雇用合格的人，等于把利润让给不歧视的对手。他晚年还与凯文·墨菲提出『理性上瘾』，主张连吸烟、吸毒这类看似失控的行为也含有前瞻的算计成分。
贯穿始终的，是他那句信条：经济分析方法可以用于人类行为的全部。这让他既被誉为打开无数新领域的先驱，也被批为『经济学帝国主义』——把爱、家庭与道德都化约成算账。但即便批评者也承认：他这副『冷』的工具，常能照出温情叙事看不见的激励结构。
becker.ideas_en:
Becker's core conviction was that in nearly every corner of life people are 'making choices under constraints' — not only buying groceries or trading stocks, but marrying, divorcing, staying in school, deciding how many children to have, even whether to commit a crime, all resting on an implicit cost–benefit calculation. It sounds cold, but its power is this: it lets you explain, even predict, behavior that had been chalked up to 'culture,' 'morality,' or 'human nature.'
His single most important contribution is 'human capital': education, skills, training, and health are not mere consumption or expense but investment, like buying a machine — you spend money and time today for higher output and income tomorrow. Why an individual stays in school, why a firm trains its workers, why people migrate, can all be understood as returns on investment. This framework transformed how economics sees people, and was the core reason for his Nobel Prize.
He also pushed the method boldly into the family — marriage, divorce, the household division of labor, and childbearing can all be seen as rational decisions. The famous case is the 'quantity–quality trade-off' in fertility: as a society grows rich and the returns to education rise, parents tend to invest more in each child, so the pricier a child's 'quality' becomes, the higher the marginal cost of an additional child, and the rational choice tilts toward 'fewer children, more heavily invested'; the more a mother can earn at work, the higher the 'opportunity cost of time' for each birth. This explains a counterintuitive pattern — richer families and societies often have fewer children.
The same logic he turned on crime and discrimination. Crime, to him, is a rational response to expected gains weighed against the probability and cost of punishment, so deterrence can be designed; discrimination carries a cost to the discriminator himself — refusing to hire a qualified person hands the profit to a non-discriminating rival. Late in life he and Kevin Murphy proposed 'rational addiction,' arguing that even seemingly out-of-control behaviors like smoking and drug use contain an element of forward-looking calculation.
Running through it all is his creed: the economic approach can be applied to the whole of human behavior. This made him both a pioneer who opened countless new fields and a target of the charge of 'economics imperialism' — reducing love, family, and morality to arithmetic. Yet even critics concede that his 'cold' instrument often reveals the incentive structures that warm narratives cannot see.

assessments.text: 1992 年诺贝尔经济学奖授予他，理由是『把微观经济分析的范围，扩展到此前被置于经济学之外的人类行为与互动的广阔领域』——家庭、教育、犯罪与歧视皆在其中。
批评者（包括许多社会学家与女性主义学者）认为他把爱、家庭、亲子关系都化约为成本-收益计算，是一种『经济学帝国主义』，忽略了文化、权力与情感的不可通约；支持者则反驳：正是这种『冷』的工具，照出了温情叙事看不见的激励结构。

assessments_en.text: The 1992 Nobel Prize in Economics was awarded to him for 'having extended the domain of microeconomic analysis to a wide range of human behaviour and interaction, including non-market behaviour' — family, education, crime, and discrimination among them.

Critics (including many sociologists and feminist scholars) charged that he reduced love, family, and the parent–child bond to cost–benefit calculation — an 'economic imperialism' that ignores the incommensurability of culture, power, and emotion; defenders reply that precisely this 'cold' tool reveals the structure of incentives that warm narratives cannot see.

quotes: 经济分析方法的力量，在于它能毫不畏惧地把同一套框架用于人类行为的全部。（《人类行为的经济分析》大意）
教育与培训，是人对自身最重要的投资——这就是人力资本。（《人力资本》大意）
quotes_en: The power of the economic approach is that it can be applied, without fear, to the whole range of human behavior. (paraphrased, The Economic Approach to Human Behavior)
Education and training are the most important investments in human capital. (paraphrased, Human Capital)
works: 《口味的经济学》（与凯文·墨菲合著）
works_en: The Economic Approach to Human Behavior
becker.lineage: 继承并光大芝加哥学派（米尔顿·弗里德曼、乔治·斯蒂格勒）的价格理论与理性选择；远绍亚当·斯密把人视为回应激励的理性主体的传统；下启现代劳动经济学、家庭经济学与所谓『经济学帝国主义』，并影响了史蒂芬·列维特（《魔鬼经济学》）等一代学者。
becker.lineage_en: He inherited and extended the price theory and rational-choice approach of the Chicago School (Milton Friedman, George Stigler); he traced back to Adam Smith's vision of people as rational agents responding to incentives; and he opened the way for modern labor economics, the economics of the family, and so-called 'economic imperialism,' influencing a generation including Steven Levitt (Freakonomics).
becker.trivia: 他的博士论文研究『歧视的经济学』，当时被认为不像正经经济学，险些不被接受；他常说自己的犯罪经济学，是某次为是否该花时间找车位『算账』时萌生的；与同事凯文·墨菲合作提出『理性上瘾』模型，主张连吸烟、吸毒都能纳入前瞻性的理性选择框架，引发巨大争议。
becker.trivia_en: His doctoral dissertation on 'the economics of discrimination' was at the time thought not to be real economics and nearly went unaccepted; he often said his economics of crime was born when he once 'did the math' on whether to spend time hunting for a parking spot; with his colleague Kevin Murphy he proposed a model of 'rational addiction,' arguing that even smoking and drug use could be folded into a forward-looking rational-choice framework — to great controversy.

zhuxi.bio: 1130–1200，南宋哲学家、教育家，理学（程朱理学）的集大成者。他遍注儒家经典，编定《四书章句集注》，使《大学》《中庸》《论语》《孟子》成为此后数百年科举与读书人的根本教科书。生前学说一度被斥为『伪学』遭禁，身后却被尊为继孔孟之后儒学的正统，影响中国、朝鲜、日本、越南近八百年。
zhuxi.bio_en: 1130–1200, a Southern Song philosopher and educator, the great synthesizer of Neo-Confucianism (the Cheng–Zhu school). He annotated the Confucian classics and compiled the Collected Commentaries on the Four Books, making the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, the Analects, and the Mencius the foundational textbooks of the civil examinations and of educated life for centuries. His teaching was for a time banned as 'false learning,' yet after his death he was venerated as the orthodox successor to Confucius and Mencius, shaping China, Korea, Japan, and Vietnam for nearly eight hundred years.
zhuxi.ideas:
朱熹要回答一个大问题：这个世界，以及人该如何做人，背后到底有没有一个统一的道理？他的答案是『理』。在他看来，万事万物——一草一木、君臣父子、四季运行——背后都有一个使它『之所以如此、又应当如此』的理（原理兼规范）；而构成具体事物的材料、气质，叫『气』。他主张『理在气先』：理是更根本的。每个人的本性（『性』）其实就是这个理（『性即理』），所以人性本善；但人又被先天的『气禀』和后天的『人欲』（私欲）遮蔽，所以现实里会有恶。
成圣的工夫，他叫『格物致知』：一件一件去穷究事物之理，今天格一物、明天格一物，积累到一定程度豁然贯通，便能照见那个贯穿万物的天理。配套的修养是『存天理，灭人欲』——这句常被误读成禁欲。他的本意不是要灭掉吃饭穿衣的正常需求，而是去掉那些『过度的、违背公义的私欲』，让符合天理的部分（该有的人伦情感）保留并端正。
这套学说与陆九渊、以及后来王阳明的『心学』针锋相对：心学说『心即理』，理就在你心中，靠向内顿悟；朱熹说理在万物，要靠向外一点一滴地『格』、循序渐进地下工夫。这场『尊德性 vs 道问学』的分歧，是中国思想史上最重要的争论之一。理解朱熹，就理解了此后东亚那套『读书—格物—修身—齐家』深入骨髓的秩序观从何而来。
zhuxi.ideas_en:
Zhu Xi set out to answer one great question: behind this world — and behind how a person ought to live — is there a single unifying principle? His answer was li (Principle). For him, every thing — a blade of grass, a tree, the bond of ruler and minister or father and son, the turning of the seasons — has behind it a li that makes it 'so, and rightly so' (at once a law and a norm); while the material and disposition that compose a concrete thing he called qi. He held that 'li is prior to qi': Principle is the more fundamental. Each person's nature (xing) just is this li ('the nature is Principle'), so human nature is originally good; yet people are obscured by their inborn 'endowment of qi' and by acquired 'selfish desire,' which is why evil appears in practice.
The work of becoming a sage he called 'the investigation of things to extend knowledge' (gewu zhizhi): probe the principle of one thing today, another tomorrow, until accumulation yields a sudden breakthrough into the Heavenly Principle that runs through all things. The paired discipline is 'preserve Heavenly Principle, extinguish human desire' — a line often misread as asceticism. He did not mean wiping out the normal needs of food and clothing, but removing the 'excessive, justice-violating selfish desires,' keeping and rectifying what accords with Principle (the proper human bonds and feelings).
This stood opposed to the 'learning of the mind' of Lu Jiuyuan and, later, Wang Yangming: the mind-school said 'the mind is Principle,' li is within you, reached by inward sudden insight; Zhu Xi said li is in all things, reached by 'investigating' them step by patient step. This dispute — 'honoring the virtuous nature versus following the path of inquiry' — is among the most important in Chinese intellectual history. To understand Zhu Xi is to understand where East Asia's bone-deep order of 'study — investigate — cultivate the self — order the family' came from.

assessments.text: 朱熹身后，其《四书集注》自元代起被定为科举取士的官方标准，地位近八百年不坠；他被尊称为『朱子』，是孔孟之后对东亚影响最深远的儒者。
明清以降，从王阳明的心学到戴震、再到五四，批评者指责『存天理灭人欲』在实践中沦为压抑人性、束缚个体（尤其束缚女性）的礼教工具；同情者则强调那多半是后人将其僵化，未必是朱熹本意。

assessments_en.text: After his death, from the Yuan dynasty on, his Collected Commentaries on the Four Books were made the official standard for the civil examinations, a status that held for nearly eight centuries; honored as 'Master Zhu,' he is the most far-reaching Confucian influence on East Asia after Confucius and Mencius.

From the Ming and Qing onward — through Wang Yangming's mind-learning, Dai Zhen, and the May Fourth movement — critics charged that 'preserve Heavenly Principle, extinguish human desire' in practice became a ritualist tool for repressing human nature and constraining the individual (women especially); sympathizers stress that this was largely a later ossification, not necessarily Zhu Xi's own intent.

quotes: 问渠那得清如许？为有源头活水来。（《观书有感》）
存天理，灭人欲。（《朱子语类》）
今日格一件，明日格一件，积习既多，然后脱然有贯通处。（《大学章句》大意）
quotes_en: How can the canal be so clear? Because fresh water flows in from the source. (On Reading)
Preserve Heavenly Principle; extinguish selfish human desire. (Classified Conversations of Master Zhu)
Investigate one thing today, another tomorrow; once enough has accumulated, there comes a sudden breakthrough into a thorough understanding. (paraphrased, Commentary on the Great Learning)
works_en: Collected Commentaries on the Four Books
Reflections on Things at Hand (with Lü Zuqian)
The Original Meaning of the Book of Changes
Collected Commentaries on the Book of Songs
zhuxi.lineage: 上承北宋理学的开创者周敦颐、张载与二程（程颢、程颐）——尤其继承程颐的『性即理』；融合儒家伦理与受佛、道刺激而生的形上学；与陆九渊的『心学』对立（鹅湖之会）；下启朝鲜李退溪、日本朱子学，并成为元明清的官方意识形态，也催生了王阳明对它的反动。
zhuxi.lineage_en: He built on the founders of Northern Song Neo-Confucianism — Zhou Dunyi, Zhang Zai, and the Cheng brothers (Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi), inheriting especially Cheng Yi's 'the nature is Principle'; he fused Confucian ethics with a metaphysics spurred by Buddhism and Daoism; he stood opposed to Lu Jiuyuan's 'learning of the mind' (the Goose Lake debate); and he opened the way to Korea's Yi Hwang (Toegye) and Japanese Zhu-Xi studies, became the official ideology of the Yuan, Ming, and Qing, and provoked Wang Yangming's reaction against him.
zhuxi.trivia: 1175 年，他与陆九渊在『鹅湖之会』当面辩论『为学之方』，不欢而散，成为思想史上的名场面；晚年其学说被政敌打成『伪学』，列入『庆元党禁』遭朝廷禁止，门生噤声，他在禁令之中去世，数年后才得平反、备极哀荣；他重建白鹿洞书院、亲订学规，是中国书院教育的奠基者之一。
zhuxi.trivia_en: In 1175 he debated Lu Jiuyuan face to face over 'the method of learning' at the Goose Lake Meeting; they parted unreconciled, in a famous scene of intellectual history. Late in life his teaching was branded 'false learning' by political enemies and banned under the Qingyuan proscription; his disciples fell silent, and he died under the ban, rehabilitated with great honor only years later. He rebuilt the White Deer Grotto Academy and personally drafted its regulations, making him a founder of China's academy (shuyuan) education.

musk.bio: 1971– ，出生于南非的企业家、工程师，特斯拉（电动车）与 SpaceX（火箭）的 CEO，并创办或主导 PayPal、Neuralink（脑机接口）、xAI 等公司，2022 年收购推特（后更名 X）。他以极高的风险偏好、对『人类多行星化』与技术加速的执念著称，是当代最具影响力也最具争议的科技人物之一，长期位居世界首富之列。
musk.bio_en: 1971– , a South African–born entrepreneur and engineer, CEO of Tesla (electric vehicles) and SpaceX (rockets), and founder or driving force behind PayPal, Neuralink (brain–computer interfaces), and xAI, who acquired Twitter (later renamed X) in 2022. Known for an extreme appetite for risk and an obsession with making humanity 'multi-planetary' and accelerating technology, he is among the most influential — and most controversial — figures of the tech era, and has long ranked among the world's richest people.
musk.ideas:
马斯克不是学院派思想家，但他有一套贯穿一切行动的世界观，值得当作一种鲜明的『立场』来理解。其核心是一种『文明尺度的风险管理』：他认为人类文明既脆弱又可能短暂，因此最该做的，是降低那些可能终结文明的存在性风险、并扩大文明这盏『意识之光』能照到的范围。由此推出他的两大执念——让人类成为跨行星物种（殖民火星，作为地球灾难的备份），以及加速可持续能源与人工智能等关键技术。
他另一个反复发出的警告，是低生育率带来的『人口崩溃』：他认为这是文明面临的最大威胁之一，严重性被远远低估，甚至超过气候变化。他的逻辑很直白：若每代人生育数持续低于约 2.1 的『更替水平』，人口便会指数式萎缩，老龄化会拖垮经济与创新，最终『文明不是死于轰然一响，而是死于无人续写』。他因此公开呼吁人们多生孩子，自己也身体力行，有众多子女。
他的方法论是『第一性原理』思维：不从类比和惯例出发，而是把问题拆解到最基本的物理与事实，再从底层重建——这让他敢做被认为不可能的事（可回收火箭、量产电动车），也让他常常无视既有共识。批评者指出他高估技术、低估社会复杂性，言行冲动、放大争议；支持者则认为，正是这种『不接受不可能』的偏执，逼着整个行业向前。理解马斯克，关键是抓住那条主线：用一切手段，延长并扩展人类文明这盏灯。
musk.ideas_en:
Musk is not an academic thinker, but he holds a worldview that runs through all his actions and is worth reading as a distinct 'position.' At its core is a kind of 'civilization-scale risk management': he believes human civilization is both fragile and possibly short-lived, so the most important thing to do is reduce the existential risks that could end it and expand the reach of civilization's 'light of consciousness.' From this flow his two obsessions — making humanity a multi-planetary species (colonizing Mars as a backup against catastrophe on Earth) and accelerating key technologies like sustainable energy and artificial intelligence.
Another warning he sounds repeatedly concerns the 'population collapse' caused by low birth rates: he regards it as one of the greatest threats to civilization, its severity, he argues, vastly underrated, even exceeding climate change. His logic is blunt: if each generation keeps having fewer children than the 'replacement level' of about 2.1, population shrinks exponentially, aging drags down economies and innovation, and in the end 'civilization dies not with a bang but for want of anyone to carry it on.' He therefore publicly urges people to have more children, and has many of his own.
His method is 'first-principles' thinking: rather than reasoning by analogy and convention, he breaks a problem down to basic physics and facts and rebuilds from the ground up — which lets him attempt the supposedly impossible (reusable rockets, mass-market electric cars) and also lets him override established consensus. Critics say he overestimates technology and underestimates social complexity, acts impulsively, and amplifies conflict; supporters say it is exactly this 'refusal to accept impossible' that drags whole industries forward. To understand Musk, grasp the through-line: use every means to prolong and extend the lamp of human civilization.

assessments.text: 在他之前，量产电动车与可回收的轨道级火箭都被主流视为不切实际；特斯拉与 SpaceX 把两者变成现实，重塑了汽车与航天业——这一工程与商业上的成就少有争议。
批评者认为他常做出夸大或失准的预测、管理风格严苛、在社交媒体上放大对立，并倾向把复杂的社会问题（如生育、言论）简化为工程或数字问题；其『人口崩溃』论也被部分人口学者认为夸大，或忽略了移民与结构性因素。

assessments_en.text: Before him, both mass-market electric cars and reusable orbital-class rockets were widely judged impractical; Tesla and SpaceX made both real, reshaping the automotive and aerospace industries — an engineering and commercial achievement that is rarely disputed.

Critics say he often makes exaggerated or inaccurate predictions, runs a harsh management style, amplifies conflict on social media, and tends to reduce complex social problems (fertility, speech) to engineering or numbers; his 'population collapse' thesis is also seen by some demographers as overstated or as ignoring migration and structural factors.

quotes: 人口崩溃是人类文明面临的最大威胁之一——远比人们以为的紧迫。（公开发言，大意）
如果人们不生更多孩子，文明就会崩塌。记住我这句话。（社交媒体发言，大意）
我宁愿乐观而错，也不愿悲观而对。（公开访谈，大意）
quotes_en: Population collapse is one of the biggest threats to the future of human civilization — far more pressing than people assume. (paraphrased, public remarks)
If people don't have more children, civilization is going to crumble. Mark my words. (paraphrased, social-media remarks)
I would rather be optimistic and wrong than pessimistic and right. (paraphrased, interview)
works: 收购并改造 X（原推特）
works_en: Acquisition and overhaul of X (formerly Twitter)
musk.lineage: 思想上受科幻（阿西莫夫《基地》『以知识缩短黑暗时代』）与对存在性风险的关注影响；工程上承自硅谷『第一性原理』与快速迭代文化；在『人类多行星化』『长期主义』上，与彼得·蒂尔、长期主义（longtermism）思潮、有效加速论（e/acc）既有交集也有张力。
musk.lineage_en: Intellectually he is shaped by science fiction (Asimov's Foundation and its idea of using knowledge to shorten a dark age) and by concern with existential risk; in engineering he inherits Silicon Valley's 'first-principles' and rapid-iteration culture; on 'making humanity multi-planetary' and 'longtermism' he both overlaps and is in tension with Peter Thiel, the longtermist movement, and effective accelerationism (e/acc).
musk.trivia: 他常用阿西莫夫《基地》系列解释自己『为文明买保险』的动机；以工作狂与激进时间表著称，常被调侃『马斯克时间』（承诺得早、兑现得晚）；公开称自己有多名子女，并把『生育不足』当作长期忧患反复倡议；早年靠 PayPal 套现后，几乎把全部身家投入特斯拉与 SpaceX，一度濒临破产。
musk.trivia_en: He often invokes Asimov's Foundation series to explain his drive to 'buy insurance for civilization'; he is famed as a workaholic with aggressive timelines, mocked for 'Musk time' (promise early, deliver late); he has publicly said he has many children and repeatedly campaigns on 'under-reproduction' as a long-term danger; after cashing out of PayPal early on, he poured almost his entire fortune into Tesla and SpaceX and at one point came close to bankruptcy.

sartre.bio: 1905–1980，法国哲学家、剧作家、小说家，20 世纪存在主义的标志性人物。巴黎高师出身，与波伏娃结为终身伴侣。代表作《存在与虚无》奠定其存在主义哲学，戏剧《禁闭》《苍蝇》与小说《恶心》使其思想广为流传。他深度介入政治，二战后成为法国最有影响力的公共知识分子；1964 年获诺贝尔文学奖却主动拒绝，以保全知识分子的独立。
sartre.bio_en: 1905–1980, a French philosopher, playwright, and novelist, the emblematic figure of twentieth-century existentialism. A graduate of the École Normale Supérieure, he formed a lifelong partnership with Beauvoir. His Being and Nothingness laid the foundation of his existentialist philosophy, while the plays No Exit and The Flies and the novel Nausea carried his ideas to a wide public. Deeply engaged in politics, he became postwar France's most influential public intellectual; awarded the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature, he declined it to preserve his independence as an intellectual.
sartre.ideas:
萨特存在主义最有名的口号是『存在先于本质』。意思是：人不像一把裁纸刀——刀在被造出来之前，工匠心里已有它的用途（本质）；人是先存在（被抛到世上），再通过自己的选择，一点一点造就自己是谁。没有上帝、没有现成的人性蓝图替你预先规定『你该成为什么』。这既是解放，也是重担。
由此他得出一个让人不安的结论：人『被判处自由』。你逃不掉选择——连『不选择』也是一种选择，而且没有任何外在权威（神、天性、社会角色）能替你的选择背书或卸责。面对这种彻底的自由与随之而来的责任，人会感到『焦虑』。
为了逃避这份重担，人最常用的伎俩，他叫『自欺』（mauvaise foi）：假装自己别无选择——『我天生就是这样的人』『社会、父母要求我必须如此』『这是我的天职、我的本分』。他著名地举例：一个把自己完全等同于角色、演得一丝不苟的咖啡馆侍者，正是在用『我只是个侍者』来掩盖『我本可以是别的』这份自由。把任何身份（包括『为人父母是天职』『传宗接代是本分』）当成不可违抗的命运，在萨特看来都是自欺。
他还有一句常被误解的话：『他人即地狱』。它不是说别人都讨厌，而是说：我们太容易活在他人的目光与评判里，让别人来定义我们是谁，从而出卖了自己的自由。萨特的伦理因此落在『本真性』上——清醒地认领你的自由，为你的选择负全责，不躲进任何现成的剧本背后。理解萨特，就理解了现代人那种『没人替我做主、也没人替我担保』的处境。
sartre.ideas_en:
Existentialism's most famous slogan from Sartre is 'existence precedes essence.' It means: a person is not like a paper-knife — before the knife is made, the craftsman already has its purpose (its essence) in mind; a person first exists (is thrown into the world) and only then, through his own choices, makes himself, bit by bit, into who he is. There is no God, no ready-made blueprint of human nature, to dictate in advance 'what you ought to become.' This is at once a liberation and a burden.
From this he draws an unsettling conclusion: a person is 'condemned to be free.' You cannot escape choosing — even 'not choosing' is a choice — and no external authority (God, nature, a social role) can underwrite your choice or relieve you of responsibility for it. Facing this total freedom and the responsibility that comes with it, a person feels 'anguish.'
