Trained in the Austrian school yet building a system of his own, he was one of the most imaginative economists of the twentieth century. Still in his twenties he wrote The Theory of Economic Development, arguing that 'entrepreneurs' and 'innovation' are the true engine of capitalism; late in life, in Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy, he predicted that capitalism would unravel because of its own success. His life was turbulent — he served as Austria's finance minister and as a bank president, both ending in failure — before he found his footing in scholarship.
schumpeter.ideas:
熊彼特的核心洞见可以浓缩成一个画面：经济不是一台慢慢长大的机器，而是一片不断有新树苗顶翻老树的森林。他反对当时主流（也是今天许多人脑中默认）的『均衡』图景——以为市场总会平稳地走向供需平衡。在他看来，真正重要的事，恰恰发生在均衡被打破的时刻。

他最著名的概念是『创造性毁灭』（creative destruction）：资本主义的进步，从来不是把旧东西修补得更好，而是用全新的产品、技术与组织方式，把旧的整批淘汰掉——汽车淘汰马车，电商冲垮百货公司。这个过程对被淘汰的一方是残酷的，却是整个系统保持活力的根本机制。增长不是积累，而是替换。

推动这场替换的主角，是『企业家』。要注意：熊彼特说的企业家不等于资本家或老板，而是任何把『新组合』付诸实现的人——把已有的资源用一种从没有过的方式重新拼起来。企业家的利润，本质上是他短暂领先于模仿者的奖赏；一旦别人跟上，利润就被竞争抹平，于是又逼出下一次创新。由此他也解释了经济为何呈周期性波动：创新成群结队地涌现，又成群结队地被消化。

晚年他抛出一个悲观又深刻的预言：资本主义会死，但不是死于马克思所说的失败，而是死于它的成功。繁荣会催生庞大、官僚化的大公司，让创新变得例行公事、让企业家精神枯萎；同时养出一批受过良好教育、却对体制充满敌意的知识分子。理性化的、舒适的资本主义，会亲手腐蚀掉支撑它的那种冒险文化。这个判断至今仍被反复引用与争论。
schumpeter.ideas_en:
Schumpeter's central insight can be compressed into a single picture: an economy is not a machine that slowly grows, but a forest in which new saplings keep toppling old trees. He rejected the 'equilibrium' image that dominated his day (and still sits by default in many minds) — the notion that markets always glide smoothly toward a balance of supply and demand. For him, what truly matters happens precisely when equilibrium is broken.

His most famous concept is 'creative destruction': the progress of capitalism is never a matter of patching up the old to work better, but of using wholly new products, technologies, and ways of organizing to scrap the old wholesale — cars displacing carriages, e-commerce wrecking department stores. The process is brutal for those displaced, yet it is the very mechanism that keeps the whole system alive. Growth is not accumulation but replacement.

The protagonist driving this replacement is the 'entrepreneur.' Note: Schumpeter's entrepreneur is not the same as a capitalist or a boss, but anyone who realizes a 'new combination' — reassembling existing resources in a way never tried before. Entrepreneurial profit is essentially the reward for a brief lead over imitators; once others catch up, competition erases the profit, forcing the next innovation. From this he also explained why economies move in cycles: innovations arrive in clusters and are digested in clusters.

Late in life he offered a pessimistic, profound prediction: capitalism will die — not from the failure Marx foretold, but from its own success. Prosperity breeds vast, bureaucratized corporations that turn innovation into routine and let the entrepreneurial spirit wither; it also raises a class of well-educated intellectuals hostile to the very system. Rationalized, comfortable capitalism corrodes, with its own hands, the culture of risk that sustains it. The judgment is still quoted and contested today.

assessments.text: 管理学家德鲁克多次推崇熊彼特，认为他把『创新与企业家精神是经济核心动力』看得比同时代专注均衡分析的主流更贴近现实，并称他为真正重要的现代经济学家。
在熊彼特身后数十年，『创造性毁灭』成为商业与科技评论中被引用最频繁的概念之一；《经济学人》长期以他的名字命名其商业专栏，足见其影响之持久。

assessments_en.text: The management thinker Drucker repeatedly praised Schumpeter, holding that he grasped 'innovation and entrepreneurship as the core driver of the economy' more realistically than the equilibrium-focused mainstream of his time, and calling him a genuinely important modern economist.

Decades after his death, 'creative destruction' became one of the most frequently cited concepts in business and technology commentary; The Economist long named its business column after him, a measure of his enduring influence.

quotes: 通常被设想的问题，是资本主义如何管理现存的结构；而真正相关的问题，是它如何创造并摧毁这些结构。（《资本主义、社会主义与民主》）
没有创新就没有企业家，没有企业家的成就就没有资本主义的回报与动力。（大意）
quotes_en: The problem that is usually being visualized is how capitalism administers existing structures, whereas the relevant problem is how it creates and destroys them. (Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy)
Without innovations, no entrepreneurs; without entrepreneurial achievement, no capitalist returns and no capitalist propulsion. (paraphrased)
schumpeter.lineage: 他受奥地利学派（门格尔、庞巴维克）训练，却不完全归属任何学派，自成一体。其思想深刻塑造了演化经济学、创新研究与现代创业理论；纳尔逊与温特的演化经济学、克里斯坦森的颠覆式创新研究，乃至硅谷把『创造性毁灭』挂在嘴边的产业文化，都可上溯到他。
schumpeter.lineage_en: Trained in the Austrian school (Menger, Böhm-Bawerk) yet belonging fully to no school, he built a framework of his own. His thought profoundly shaped evolutionary economics, innovation studies, and modern entrepreneurship theory; the evolutionary economics of Nelson and Winter, Christensen's work on disruptive innovation, and even the Silicon Valley industrial culture that keeps 'creative destruction' on its lips can all be traced back to him.
schumpeter.trivia: 熊彼特曾打趣说，自己年轻时立下三个志愿：成为维也纳最伟大的经济学家、奥地利最好的骑手、以及维也纳最迷人的情人——他说三个里实现了两个，但从不肯说是哪两个。他确实当过奥地利财政部长，又做过一家银行的行长，双双以失败收场，之后才安心回到讲台与书桌。
schumpeter.trivia_en: Schumpeter liked to joke that in his youth he set himself three ambitions: to become the greatest economist in Vienna, the finest horseman in Austria, and the most charming lover in Vienna — and he claimed to have achieved two of the three, though he never said which two. He did serve as Austria's finance minister and then as president of a bank, both ending in failure, after which he settled contentedly back into the lectern and the desk.

singer.bio: 迈克尔·辛格（Michael A. Singer，1947 年生），美国冥想导师与畅销书作家。他在攻读经济学博士期间经历了一次深刻的内在觉醒，此后退居佛罗里达乡间静修，并于 1975 年创立 Temenos 静修中心。出人意料的是，他后来还创办过一家大型医疗软件公司，亲历商界的大起大落，使他的灵性教导格外接地气。代表作《臣服实验》与《清醒地活》（The Untethered Soul）畅销全球，被广泛归入当代正念与心灵成长的经典之列。
singer.bio_en: Michael A. Singer (born 1947) is an American meditation teacher and best-selling author. During his doctoral studies in economics he underwent a profound inner awakening, after which he withdrew to rural Florida to practice and, in 1975, founded the Temenos retreat center. Unexpectedly, he later also built a large medical-software company, living through the dramatic rises and falls of business — which lends his spiritual teaching an unusually grounded, practical edge. His best-known works, The Surrender Experiment and The Untethered Soul, are worldwide bestsellers, widely counted among the classics of contemporary mindfulness and inner growth.
singer.ideas:
辛格的教导，核心只有一个简单却极难做到的转向：你不是你脑子里那个声音，你是『觉察到那个声音的人』。

他请你留意：脑中几乎一刻不停地有个声音在评论、担忧、计划、抱怨。大多数人把这个声音当成『我』，于是它焦虑你就焦虑、它愤怒你就愤怒。辛格说，既然你能听见它，你就不是它——你是它背后那个观察者、那份觉知。仅仅是认出这一点，就能在你和你的情绪之间撑开一道宝贵的空隙：情绪照样来，但不再能直接接管你。

他的第二个关键词是『臣服』（surrender）。这常被误解为消极认命，其实正相反。辛格说的臣服，是停止用内心的好恶去抗拒已经发生的现实——不是不行动，而是先不与事实较劲，让那股被堵住的能量流过去，再从清明（而非情绪反应）出发去回应。他用『内在的刺』作比喻：心里若扎着一根刺（一段旧痛、一个心结），你有两个选择——一辈子小心翼翼地保护它、安排整个生活去避免碰到它，或者干脆把刺拔掉、让伤口愈合。多数人选了前者，于是被自己的旧伤暗暗支配了一生。

他还有一个生动的说法：把那些不断浮现的念头和情绪，当成天气一样让它们『穿过』你，而不是抓住、放大、住进去。你不需要压抑它们，也不需要听从它们，只需要不挡它们的路。他自己的《臣服实验》记录了一个激进的尝试：几十年间，凡是生活送到面前、而内心本能想抗拒的事，他都试着说『好』——结果被这股顺流推着，意外地从一个隐士变成了软件公司的创始人。这本书想说明的是：当你不再让那个恐惧的声音替你做主，生命自身的流动，往往比你紧抓不放的计划走得更远。
singer.ideas_en:
Singer's teaching turns on a single pivot — simple to state, extremely hard to do: you are not the voice in your head; you are 'the one who is aware of that voice.'

He asks you to notice that there is a voice in your mind commenting, worrying, planning, complaining almost without pause. Most people take this voice to be 'me,' so when it is anxious they are anxious, when it is angry they are angry. Singer says that since you can hear it, you are not it — you are the observer behind it, the awareness itself. Merely recognizing this opens a precious gap between you and your emotions: the feelings still come, but they can no longer directly take you over.

His second key word is 'surrender.' This is often misread as passive resignation; it is the opposite. The surrender Singer means is to stop using your inner likes and dislikes to resist what has already happened — not inaction, but first declining to wrestle with the fact, letting the blocked energy pass through, and then responding from clarity rather than emotional reaction. He uses the image of an 'inner thorn': if a thorn is lodged in your heart (an old hurt, a knot), you have two choices — spend a lifetime carefully protecting it, arranging your whole life to avoid touching it, or simply pull the thorn out and let the wound heal. Most people choose the former, and so are quietly ruled by their old wounds for life.

He has another vivid formulation: let the thoughts and emotions that keep surfacing 'pass through' you like weather, rather than grabbing, amplifying, and moving into them. You needn't suppress them, nor obey them; you need only not block their way. His own book The Surrender Experiment records a radical attempt: for decades, whenever life brought something his inner self instinctively wanted to resist, he tried saying 'yes' — and, carried by that flow, he turned unexpectedly from a hermit into the founder of a software company. The book's point is this: when you stop letting the frightened voice decide for you, the movement of life itself often goes further than the plans you cling to.

assessments.text: 主持人奥普拉曾在节目《超级灵魂星期天》中专访辛格，并多次推荐《清醒地活》，称它帮助许多读者第一次意识到『我并不等于我脑中的念头』。
《清醒地活》与《臣服实验》长期位居《纽约时报》畅销书榜，被广泛视为当代以平实语言讲述东方冥想智慧的代表作。

assessments_en.text: The host Oprah interviewed Singer on her program Super Soul Sunday and has repeatedly recommended The Untethered Soul, saying it helped many readers realize for the first time that 'I am not the same as the thoughts in my head.'

The Untethered Soul and The Surrender Experiment have long sat on the New York Times bestseller lists, widely regarded as leading works that convey Eastern meditative wisdom in plain, accessible language.

quotes: 如果你想获得自由，就要愿意放下那根扎在心里的刺，而不是花一辈子去保护它。（《清醒地活》大意）
你内心那个不停说话的声音，并不是你——你是那个能听见它的人。（《清醒地活》大意）
quotes_en: If you want to be free, you must be willing to let go of the thorn lodged in your heart, rather than spend a lifetime protecting it. (The Untethered Soul, paraphrased)
The voice that never stops talking inside you is not you — you are the one who hears it. (The Untethered Soul, paraphrased)
works: 《清醒地活：超越自我的旅程》（The Untethered Soul, 2007）
works_en: The Untethered Soul: The Journey Beyond Yourself (2007)
singer.lineage: 辛格的思想融合了东方冥想（瑜伽、禅与吠檀多的『觉知即真我』）与西方心理自助传统，但他刻意不绑定任何单一宗教。他承袭『观照念头』这一古老修习，用极通俗的现代语言重新讲述，因而在不接触宗教术语的大众读者中影响深远，常与埃克哈特·托勒等当代灵性作家并列。
singer.lineage_en: Singer's thought blends Eastern meditation (yoga, Zen, and the Vedanta notion that 'awareness is the true self') with the Western self-help tradition, yet he deliberately ties himself to no single religion. He inherits the ancient practice of 'witnessing one's thoughts' and retells it in plain modern language, which gives him deep reach among general readers who would never approach religious jargon; he is often placed alongside contemporary spiritual writers such as Eckhart Tolle.
singer.trivia: 辛格的人生本身就是其教导的注脚：一个住在树林里打坐的隐士，因为持续对生活『说好』，竟一路把自己创办的医疗软件公司做到上市规模；后来公司卷入一桩与他个人行为无关的法律风波，他又以同样的『臣服』心态平静面对，最终获得澄清。这段经历成了《臣服实验》最生动的素材。
singer.trivia_en: Singer's life is itself a footnote to his teaching: a hermit meditating in the woods, by continually saying 'yes' to life, ended up growing the medical-software company he founded to public-listing scale; when the company was later caught in a legal storm unrelated to his own conduct, he met it with the same attitude of 'surrender,' calmly, and was eventually cleared. The episode became the most vivid material in The Surrender Experiment.

wittgenstein.bio: 1889–1951，生于维也纳一个富甲奥匈帝国的钢铁工业家族。早年在英国研习航空工程，因对数学基础的兴趣转投剑桥，师从罗素与弗雷格的逻辑学传统。一战中他作为奥军志愿入伍、屡上前线，并在战壕与战俘营里写成《逻辑哲学论》。战后他放弃巨额遗产，先后当过乡村小学教师、园丁、医院勤杂工，一度自认已解决全部哲学问题而离开学界；十余年后重返剑桥，彻底翻新自己的思想，遗著《哲学研究》成为二十世纪最有影响的哲学著作之一。
wittgenstein.bio_en: 1889–1951, born in Vienna into a steel-industry family among the wealthiest in Austria-Hungary. He first studied aeronautical engineering in England, then, drawn to the foundations of mathematics, went to Cambridge under the logical tradition of Russell and Frege. In the First World War he volunteered for the Austrian army, repeatedly saw the front, and wrote the Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus in the trenches and a prisoner-of-war camp. Afterward he gave away an enormous inheritance and worked in turn as a village schoolteacher, a gardener, and a hospital orderly, having concluded for a time that he had solved all of philosophy and left academia; more than a decade later he returned to Cambridge, overhauled his own thinking entirely, and his posthumous Philosophical Investigations became one of the most influential philosophical works of the twentieth century.
wittgenstein.ideas:
维特根斯坦一生其实给出了两套几乎相反的哲学，常被称作『前期』与『后期』，而贯穿两者的母题只有一个：哲学的混乱，多半是语言出了岔子。
前期的《逻辑哲学论》试图为语言划定边界。他主张语言之所以能描述世界，是因为命题像一幅『图画』，其结构对应着事实的结构；凡是能说的，都能说清楚，而伦理、人生意义、上帝这些最要紧的东西，恰恰超出了语言能如实描画的范围——于是有了那句著名的收尾：『凡不可说的，应当沉默。』注意，他不是说这些不重要，恰恰相反，他认为它们重要到无法被命题装下，只能显示、不能言说。
后期他几乎推翻了自己。《哲学研究》里，他不再问『语言的本质是什么』，而问『我们实际上怎么用语言』。他提出『语言游戏』：词的意义不在它指向的某个对象，而在它在具体生活场景里的用法——『水！』可以是请求、警告、命令、答案，全看你在玩哪一局。由此引出『意义即用法』。他又用『家族相似』打掉了人们对定义的执念：『游戏』并没有一条人人共有的本质，棋类、球类、单人纸牌只是像一家人那样彼此交叠相似而已。
他最深的一击，是『私人语言论证』与『甲虫盒子』：设想每个人都有一个只有自己能看的盒子，里面装着他称为『甲虫』的东西——那么这个词的意义根本不可能由盒中之物来定，因为它在公共交流里使不上力。借此他说明：意义、规则、理解，都根植于共同的『生活形式』，而非藏在各人私密的内心。
于是他把哲学本身重新定义为一种『治疗』：哲学问题往往不是有待解答的难题，而是被语言绊住后产生的迷惑；哲学家的任务，是『给苍蝇指出飞出捕蝇瓶的路』——把纠缠解开，让那个伪问题消失，而不是再盖一座理论的高楼。这一转向深刻改变了此后人们对『什么才算一个真问题』的理解。
wittgenstein.ideas_en:
Wittgenstein in fact produced two almost opposite philosophies, usually called the 'early' and the 'later,' and only one motif runs through both: philosophical confusion is mostly language gone wrong.
The early Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus tries to draw the limits of language. He argues that language can describe the world because a proposition is like a 'picture' whose structure mirrors the structure of a fact; whatever can be said can be said clearly, while the things that matter most — ethics, the meaning of life, God — fall precisely outside what language can truthfully picture. Hence the famous closing line: 'Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.' Note that he does not mean these things are unimportant; on the contrary, he holds them so important that no proposition can contain them — they can only be shown, not said.
Later he all but overturned himself. In the Philosophical Investigations he stops asking 'what is the essence of language' and asks instead 'how do we actually use it.' He proposes 'language games': the meaning of a word lies not in some object it names but in its use within a concrete situation of life — 'Water!' can be a request, a warning, a command, an answer, depending on which game you are playing. From this comes 'meaning is use.' With 'family resemblance' he then dismantles our craving for definitions: 'game' has no single essence shared by all — board games, ball games, solitaire merely overlap and resemble one another the way members of a family do.
His deepest stroke is the 'private-language argument' and the 'beetle-in-the-box': suppose everyone had a box only they could look into, holding something they called a 'beetle'; then the meaning of that word could not possibly be fixed by the thing in the box, for it does no work in public exchange. By this he shows that meaning, rules, and understanding are rooted in a shared 'form of life,' not hidden in each person's private inner world.
So he redefined philosophy itself as a kind of 'therapy': philosophical problems are often not puzzles awaiting solution but confusions produced by being tripped up by language; the philosopher's task is to 'show the fly the way out of the fly-bottle' — to untangle the knot so the pseudo-problem dissolves, not to erect yet another theoretical edifice. This turn profoundly changed how people afterward understood what even counts as a genuine question.

assessments.text: 将青年维特根斯坦引入剑桥的伯特兰·罗素称他为『我所认识的、最完美地体现了传统意义上天才的人——充满激情、深刻、炽烈而专横』，并为《逻辑哲学论》作序（尽管维氏认为罗素根本没读懂他）。
石里克、卡尔纳普等维也纳学派成员奉《逻辑哲学论》为逻辑实证主义的圣经；而维特根斯坦后期『意义即用法』的转向，又反过来成为对实证主义的最有力批评之一。

assessments_en.text: Russell, who brought the young Wittgenstein into Cambridge, called him 'perhaps the most perfect example I have ever known of genius as traditionally conceived — passionate, profound, intense, and dominating,' and wrote the introduction to the Tractatus (though Wittgenstein felt Russell had not understood him at all).

Members of the Vienna Circle such as Schlick and Carnap revered the Tractatus as a bible of logical positivism; yet Wittgenstein's later turn to 'meaning is use' became, in turn, one of the most powerful criticisms of that very positivism.

quotes: 凡不可说的，应当保持沉默。（《逻辑哲学论》命题七）
我的语言的界限，意味着我的世界的界限。（《逻辑哲学论》5.6）
一个词的意义，就是它在语言中的用法。（《哲学研究》大意）
quotes_en: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent. (Tractatus, proposition 7)
The limits of my language mean the limits of my world. (Tractatus 5.6)
The meaning of a word is its use in the language. (Philosophical Investigations, paraphrased)
works_en: The Blue and Brown Books (dictated lecture notes)
wittgenstein.lineage: 他承接弗雷格与罗素开创的现代逻辑与分析哲学传统；前期《逻辑哲学论》直接催生了维也纳学派的逻辑实证主义，后期《哲学研究》则开启了以日常语言为分析对象的『牛津日常语言学派』，深刻影响了赖尔、奥斯汀、克里普克等几代哲学家，至今仍是语言哲学与心灵哲学绕不开的源头。
wittgenstein.lineage_en: He inherited the modern logical and analytic tradition begun by Frege and Russell; his early Tractatus directly inspired the logical positivism of the Vienna Circle, while his later Investigations launched the 'ordinary-language philosophy' of Oxford, deeply shaping generations of philosophers such as Ryle, Austin, and Kripke, and remaining an inescapable source for the philosophy of language and of mind.
wittgenstein.trivia: 他出身的家族富可敌国，却将继承的巨额财产悉数转赠兄姊与艺术家（包括诗人里尔克），自己力求清贫。生前只正式出版过一本哲学书《逻辑哲学论》、一篇文章和一本给小学生的拼写词典；他还亲手为姐姐在维也纳设计了一座以极简精确著称的现代主义住宅，连暖气片的位置都反复推敲。
wittgenstein.trivia_en: Though born into a family of near-imperial wealth, he gave away his entire inheritance to his siblings and to artists (the poet Rilke among them), and sought a life of plainness. In his lifetime he formally published only one book of philosophy, the Tractatus, plus a single article and a spelling dictionary for schoolchildren; he also designed, with his own hand, an austerely precise modernist house for his sister in Vienna, reworking even the placement of the radiators.

fromm.bio: 1900–1980，生于德国法兰克福的犹太家庭。早年同时受弗洛伊德精神分析与马克思社会理论影响，是法兰克福学派（批判理论）早期成员；纳粹上台后流亡美国，长期讲学行医。他把精神分析从『个人潜意识』扩展到『社会性格』——人如何被时代与经济塑形。代表作《逃避自由》《爱的艺术》风行全球，使他成为二十世纪最具公共影响力的心理学家之一。
fromm.bio_en: 1900–1980, born in Frankfurt, Germany, into a Jewish family. Shaped early by both Freudian psychoanalysis and Marxist social theory, he was an early member of the Frankfurt School of critical theory; after the Nazis took power he emigrated to the United States, where he taught and practiced for decades. He widened psychoanalysis from the 'individual unconscious' to 'social character' — how people are molded by their era and economy. His bestsellers Escape from Freedom and The Art of Loving made him one of the 20th century's most publicly influential psychologists.
fromm.ideas:
弗洛姆想弄懂一件事：现代人明明自由了，为什么反而更焦虑、更空虚？
他的第一个回答是《逃避自由》：当人从传统、宗教、宗族的束缚里解放出来，也就失去了归属与确定，自由反而成了沉重的孤独。于是许多人转身『逃避自由』——投靠权威、随大流变成和别人一样的『自动人』、或以破坏发泄。法西斯的群众心理就这么来的。
他最广为人知的是《爱的艺术》：爱不是你『掉』进去的好运，而是一门要学、要练的本事。成熟的爱有四个要素——关心、责任、尊重、了解。尊重，意味着希望对方按他自己的样子成长，而不是变成对我有用的样子；了解，是真去懂他，而非用我的想象覆盖他。他狠狠区分两种爱：不成熟的爱说『因为我需要你，所以我爱你』；成熟的爱说『因为我爱你，所以我需要你』。爱的本质是给予，而非索取或占有。
晚年《占有还是存在》把这条线推到整个人生：你靠『拥有什么』（财产、头衔、把伴侣也当资产去掌控）确认自己，还是靠『成为什么』（去爱、去创造、去经历）来活着？前者越抓越怕失去，后者在给予中反而丰盈。
fromm.ideas_en:
Fromm wanted to crack one puzzle: modern people are freer than ever — so why are they more anxious and empty?
His first answer is Escape from Freedom: once people are freed from the bonds of tradition, religion, and clan, they also lose belonging and certainty, and freedom becomes a heavy loneliness. So many people turn around and 'escape from freedom' — submitting to authority, conforming into an 'automaton' just like everyone else, or venting through destruction. This, he argued, is the mass psychology behind fascism.
He is best known for The Art of Loving: love is not luck you 'fall' into, but a skill to be learned and practiced. Mature love has four elements — care, responsibility, respect, and knowledge. Respect means wanting the other to grow in their own way, not into something useful to me; knowledge means truly understanding them rather than papering over them with my own projection. He sharply distinguished two kinds of love: immature love says 'I love you because I need you'; mature love says 'I need you because I love you.' The essence of love is giving, not taking or possessing.
His late work To Have or To Be? extends this across all of life: do you confirm yourself by 'having' (property, titles, controlling even your partner as an asset), or by 'being' (loving, creating, experiencing)? The former clings ever tighter and fears loss; the latter grows richer through giving.

assessments.text: 作为批判理论早期成员，他率先把精神分析与马克思的社会批判结合，开创社会心理学的一支。
《爱的艺术》全球销量数以千万计，被译成数十种语言，是史上最畅销的心理学著作之一。

assessments_en.text: As an early member of critical theory, he was among the first to fuse psychoanalysis with Marxian social critique, founding a strand of social psychology.
The Art of Loving has sold tens of millions of copies in dozens of languages — one of the best-selling psychology books ever written.

quotes: 不成熟的爱说：『因为我需要你，所以我爱你。』成熟的爱说：『因为我爱你，所以我需要你。』（《爱的艺术》）
爱首先是给予，而不是接受。（《爱的艺术》）
人生最主要的任务，是把自己生出来。
quotes_en: Immature love says: 'I love you because I need you.' Mature love says: 'I need you because I love you.' (The Art of Loving)
Love is primarily giving, not receiving. (The Art of Loving)
Man's main task in life is to give birth to himself.
fromm.lineage: 综合弗洛伊德与马克思，是法兰克福学派早期成员；与霍妮、沙利文同属新精神分析的『文化学派』；其人本取向深刻影响了马斯洛、罗杰斯等人本主义心理学家。
fromm.lineage_en: Synthesizing Freud and Marx, he was an early member of the Frankfurt School; with Horney and Sullivan he belonged to the 'cultural school' of neo-psychoanalysis; his humanistic orientation deeply influenced humanistic psychologists such as Maslow and Rogers.
fromm.trivia: 他主张『爱的艺术』所言——爱是需要专注与纪律的长期实践；也热衷把深奥理论写成人人能读的小书，相信心理学该走出诊室、帮普通人把日子过好。
fromm.trivia_en: He held, as The Art of Loving preaches, that love is a long practice demanding concentration and discipline; he was also devoted to turning difficult theory into small books anyone could read, believing psychology should leave the clinic and help ordinary people live better.

dostoevsky.bio: 1821–1881，俄国小说家。年轻时因参加进步知识分子小组被捕、判死刑，行刑前一刻才改判流放西伯利亚——这场『假处决』与四年苦役彻底重塑了他。归来后在贫病、癫痫与赌债中写出《罪与罚》《白痴》《群魔》《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》，把小说变成拷问信仰、自由、善恶与人性深渊的哲学现场，被尊为兼具心理深度与思想强度的现代文学高峰。
dostoevsky.bio_en: 1821–1881, Russian novelist. Arrested in his youth for joining a circle of progressive intellectuals, sentenced to death and reprieved only at the last instant before the firing squad, then exiled to four years of hard labor in Siberia — this 'mock execution' and penal servitude remade him utterly. Returning amid poverty, epilepsy, and gambling debts, he wrote Crime and Punishment, The Idiot, Demons, and The Brothers Karamazov, turning the novel into a philosophical arena interrogating faith, freedom, good and evil, and the human abyss — revered as a summit of modern literature for joining psychological depth with intellectual intensity.
dostoevsky.ideas:
陀思妥耶夫斯基不写『应该怎样的人』，他写真实、矛盾、深不见底的人。
他最锋利的一击在《地下室手记》：当时流行一种信念——只要用理性与科学把社会安排妥当（他讥为『水晶宫』），人就会幸福。陀氏冷笑：你看错了人。人最珍视的，不是利益与幸福，而是『按自己的意志活』——哪怕这意志任性、自毁、不划算。他说，人甚至会故意选择痛苦，只为证明自己是个『人』，而非一架按规律演奏的『钢琴键』；只为坚持『二二得四』也可以被他偏说成『二二得五』。这是对一切『为你好』式强制改造最深的反抗。
另一条贯穿始终的追问，借伊万·卡拉马佐夫之口：『如果没有上帝，是否一切都被允许？』他既写尽无信仰带来的虚无与恶，又不肯给廉价答案。
而他的出路往往不在论证里，而在受苦与爱中：人通过承担苦难、彼此怜悯，重新成为人。自由是可怕的重负，但用自由去换面包（《宗教大法官》），是更深的堕落。
dostoevsky.ideas_en:
Dostoevsky doesn't write 'the person one ought to be'; he writes the real, contradictory, bottomless human being.
His sharpest blow is in Notes from Underground: a fashionable belief held that if society were arranged rationally and scientifically (he mocked it as the 'Crystal Palace'), people would be happy. Dostoevsky sneers: you have misread human beings. What a person prizes most is not advantage or happiness but living 'by one's own will' — even if that will is willful, self-destructive, and unprofitable. He says a person will even deliberately choose suffering just to prove he is a 'man' and not a 'piano key' played by the laws of nature; just to insist that 'two times two makes four' could, if he wills it, be said to make five. This is the deepest revolt against every 'for your own good' coercion to improve someone.
Another lifelong question runs through him, voiced by Ivan Karamazov: 'If there is no God, is everything permitted?' He portrays in full the nihilism and evil unbelief can bring, yet refuses any cheap answer.
His way out lies not in argument but in suffering and love: by bearing suffering and showing one another mercy, people become human again. Freedom is a terrible burden, but trading freedom for bread (the Grand Inquisitor) is a deeper fall.

assessments.text: 称陀思妥耶夫斯基是『唯一能教给我心理学的人』，对其洞察人性深渊推崇备至。
《地下室手记》被广泛视为存在主义文学的先声，深刻影响了萨特、加缪等人。

assessments_en.text: Called Dostoevsky 'the only psychologist from whom I had anything to learn,' prizing his insight into the human abyss.
Notes from Underground is widely seen as a forerunner of existentialist literature, deeply influencing Sartre, Camus, and others.

quotes: 人不是钢琴键，他甚至会故意选择痛苦，只为证明自己是人、而非按规律演奏的琴键。（《地下室手记》大意）
如果没有上帝，那么一切都被允许。（《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》中伊万之意）
美将拯救世界。（《白痴》）
quotes_en: Man is not a piano key; he will even deliberately choose suffering, just to prove he is a man and not a key played by the laws of nature. (Notes from Underground, paraphrased)
If there is no God, everything is permitted. (the sense of Ivan in The Brothers Karamazov)
Beauty will save the world. (The Idiot)
dostoevsky.lineage: 承俄国东正教与普希金、果戈理的传统，将哲思注入小说；其对自由、虚无与人性深渊的拷问，直接启发了尼采与存在主义（萨特、加缪），亦为弗洛伊德所重。
dostoevsky.lineage_en: Heir to Russian Orthodoxy and the tradition of Pushkin and Gogol, he poured philosophy into the novel; his interrogation of freedom, nihilism, and the human abyss directly inspired Nietzsche and existentialism (Sartre, Camus), and was prized by Freud.
dostoevsky.trivia: 1849 年他被押上刑场、蒙眼待射，临刻才传来沙皇的缓刑令——这场假处决让他终生铭记生命之珍贵；他患癫痫，又深陷赌瘾，《赌徒》几乎是亲历写照。
dostoevsky.trivia_en: In 1849 he was led to the execution ground, blindfolded before the firing squad, when the Tsar's reprieve arrived at the last instant — this mock execution left him forever marked by life's preciousness; epileptic and deep in gambling addiction, his novel The Gambler reads almost as lived experience.

rousseau.bio: 1712–1778，生于日内瓦的启蒙思想家、作家、作曲家。出身贫寒、自学成才，一生漂泊，与同时代哲人屡屡决裂。他石破天惊地断言：人本性善良，是文明与社会把人异化、败坏。《社会契约论》提出『主权在民』与公意，深刻影响法国大革命；《爱弥儿》重塑教育观；《忏悔录》开创袒露自我的现代自传。他被尊为浪漫主义之父。
rousseau.bio_en: 1712–1778, an Enlightenment thinker, writer, and composer born in Geneva. Of humble origin and largely self-taught, he lived a wandering life and repeatedly broke with the philosophers of his day. He made the startling claim that human beings are naturally good and that civilization and society alienate and corrupt them. His Social Contract proposed popular sovereignty and the 'general will,' deeply influencing the French Revolution; Emile reshaped ideas of education; and his Confessions founded the modern, self-revealing autobiography. He is honored as the father of Romanticism.
rousseau.ideas:
卢梭一生都在追问：人本自由善良，为何处处身陷枷锁、彼此倾轧？
他的诊断惊世骇俗：不是人性坏，是文明把人带坏了。在《论人类不平等的起源》里，他区分两种自爱——『自爱』(amour de soi)是天然、健康的自我保存；而『自尊/虚荣』(amour-propre)是进入社会后才滋生的、与他人攀比之心。一旦有了它，人就开始活在别人的眼光里：要排名、要体面、要被艳羡。他有句名言——野蛮人活在自己之内，社会人却永远活在自己之外，只懂得靠别人的评价过活。世俗的成功、名望与地位，正是 amour-propre 的祭坛：我们拼命争取『在别人眼中是谁』，却忘了问『自己究竟是谁』。
《社会契约论》开篇即说：人生而自由，却无往不在枷锁之中。他要找的，是一种既进入社会、又不丧失自由与本真的活法——靠『公意』重建正当的共同体，靠『自然教育』（《爱弥儿》）养出不被虚荣腐蚀的人。
rousseau.ideas_en:
Rousseau spent his life asking: if humans are born free and good, why are they everywhere in chains, trampling one another?
His diagnosis was scandalous: human nature is not bad — civilization has corrupted it. In the Discourse on Inequality he distinguishes two kinds of self-love: amour de soi, the natural, healthy drive to preserve oneself; and amour-propre, the comparative vanity that arises only once we enter society. Once it takes hold, a person begins to live in others' eyes: craving rank, respectability, envy. In his famous words, the savage lives within himself, while the social man always lives outside himself, knowing how to live only in others' opinion. Worldly success, fame, and status are precisely the altar of amour-propre: we strive to be 'someone in others' eyes' and forget to ask who we ourselves are.
The Social Contract opens: man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains. What he sought was a way to enter society without losing freedom and authenticity — rebuilding a legitimate community through the 'general will,' and raising, through 'natural education' (Emile), people uncorrupted by vanity.

assessments.text: 深受卢梭影响，称他为『道德世界的牛顿』，并说卢梭让他学会了尊重普通人。
被尊为浪漫主义之父；其『主权在民』与对文明的批判，深刻影响了法国大革命、现代教育与民主思想。

assessments_en.text: Deeply influenced by Rousseau, he called him 'the Newton of the moral world' and said Rousseau taught him to respect ordinary people.
Honored as the father of Romanticism; his 'popular sovereignty' and critique of civilization deeply shaped the French Revolution, modern education, and democratic thought.

quotes: 人生而自由，却无往不在枷锁之中。（《社会契约论》）
野蛮人活在自己之内；社会人则永远活在自己之外，只知道靠别人的看法而活。（《论人类不平等的起源》大意）
出自造物主之手的东西都是好的，一到人的手里就变坏了。（《爱弥儿》开篇）
quotes_en: Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains. (The Social Contract)
The savage lives within himself; the social man always lives outside himself, and knows how to live only in the opinion of others. (Discourse on Inequality, paraphrased)
Everything is good as it leaves the hands of the Author of things; everything degenerates in the hands of man. (opening of Emile)
works_en: Discourse on the Origin of Inequality
rousseau.lineage: 承洛克的社会契约传统又激烈反转之；深刻影响康德、浪漫主义运动与法国大革命；其自然教育思想启迪现代教育学，对人性善的信念与霍布斯、后世弗洛伊德形成对照。
rousseau.lineage_en: Heir to Locke's social-contract tradition yet a fierce reversal of it; he profoundly influenced Kant, the Romantic movement, and the French Revolution; his idea of natural education inspired modern pedagogy, and his faith in natural goodness stands in contrast to Hobbes and, later, Freud.
rousseau.trivia: 他既是启蒙巨子，又激烈批判启蒙的理性与文明；《忏悔录》以前所未有的坦白剖白自己，开创现代自传，却也暴露了他把五个亲生孩子送进育婴堂的矛盾；晚年深陷被迫害的妄想，与几乎所有朋友决裂。
rousseau.trivia_en: At once a giant of the Enlightenment and a fierce critic of its reason and civilization; his Confessions laid himself bare with unprecedented candor, founding the modern autobiography — yet also exposing the contradiction that he sent all five of his own children to a foundling hospital; in his last years he sank into persecutory delusion and broke with nearly every friend.

piketty.bio: 托马·皮凯蒂（Thomas Piketty），1971 年生于法国巴黎近郊，经济学家。22 岁以财富分配理论的论文获博士学位，曾短暂任教于麻省理工学院，后回到法国，参与创办巴黎经济学院。他长期研究收入与财富的长期演变，2013 年出版《21 世纪资本论》，以三个世纪的税收与遗产数据重新点燃了关于不平等的全球讨论，使一位学院派经济学家罕见地成为公共人物。
piketty.bio_en: Thomas Piketty, born in 1971 in a suburb of Paris, is a French economist. He earned his doctorate at twenty-two with a thesis on the theory of wealth distribution, taught briefly at MIT, then returned to France and helped found the Paris School of Economics. He has spent his career studying the long-run evolution of income and wealth, and in 2013 published Capital in the Twenty-First Century, which used three centuries of tax and inheritance data to reignite a global conversation about inequality and made an academic economist, unusually, a public figure.
piketty.ideas:
皮凯蒂最有名的命题，可以浓缩成一个不等式：r > g。这里的 r 是资本的年回报率（房产、股票、债券等财产带来的收益），g 是整个经济的增长率（约等于普通人收入增长的速度）。他用大量历史数据论证：在人类历史的大多数时期，r 都高于 g——也就是说，已经握有财富的人，其财产增值的速度，超过了靠劳动挣钱的人收入增长的速度。
这听起来抽象，后果却很具体：如果钱生钱比干活挣钱更快，那么财富就会像滚雪球一样，越来越向已经富有的人（尤其是继承了财产的人）集中，不平等于是『自我放大』。他指出，20 世纪中叶那段不平等罕见缩小的时期，并非市场的自然恩赐，而是两次世界大战、大萧条与战后高税收『摧毁了旧资本』的特殊结果；一旦这些冲击过去，r > g 的老规律又让财富重新向顶端聚拢。
为把抽象讲实在，他爱用一个区分：『靠劳动挣来的不平等』与『靠继承得来的不平等』。前者是这一代人凭本事拉开的差距，社会相对能接受；后者是财产跨代自动累积、让出身决定命运，他认为这才是侵蚀『机会平等』的真正危险——一个号称崇尚奋斗的社会，可能正悄悄滑回『拼爹』的世袭逻辑。
他给出的药方主要有两味：一是『透明』——让财富与税收数据公开可查，因为关于不平等的争论太久建立在猜测而非事实上；二是『累进税』，尤其是对最高财富与遗产征收的累进税，用以打断资本无限自我累积的链条。他承认这些主张带有政治色彩、也引来诸多争议（有人质疑 r > g 是否真是铁律、累进重税是否伤害增长），但他坚持：关于不平等，先得有可靠的数据和长历史的眼光，才谈得上明智的判断。这正是他最大的贡献——把一个常被情绪与口号裹挟的话题，重新拉回到可测量、可检验的事实地基上。
piketty.ideas_en:
Piketty's most famous proposition can be compressed into one inequality: r > g. Here r is the annual return on capital (the yield from property — real estate, stocks, bonds), and g is the growth rate of the whole economy (roughly, the pace at which ordinary incomes grow). With a mass of historical data he argues that across most of human history r has exceeded g — meaning that those who already hold wealth see it grow faster than the incomes of those who work for a living.
This sounds abstract, but its consequence is concrete: if money makes money faster than labor earns it, wealth snowballs toward those already rich (especially those who inherited it), and inequality 'amplifies itself.' The mid-twentieth-century stretch in which inequality rarely narrowed, he argues, was not the market's natural gift but the special result of two world wars, the Depression, and high postwar taxes 'destroying old capital'; once those shocks passed, the old law of r > g gathered wealth back to the top.
To make the abstraction tangible he favors a distinction: inequality earned by labor versus inequality received by inheritance. The first is the gap one generation opens by its own ability, which society can relatively accept; the second is property accumulating automatically across generations until birth decides destiny — and this, he holds, is the real danger eroding 'equality of opportunity': a society that claims to prize striving may be quietly sliding back toward a hereditary logic.
His prescription is mainly twofold: transparency — making wealth and tax data open and checkable, because the argument over inequality has too long rested on guesswork rather than fact; and progressive taxation, especially on the highest wealth and inheritances, to break the chain of capital's limitless self-accumulation. He concedes these proposals are politically colored and much disputed (some doubt whether r > g is truly an iron law, or whether heavy progressive taxes harm growth), but he insists that on inequality, reliable data and a long historical view must come first before wise judgment is even possible. That is his largest contribution — pulling a subject so often swept along by emotion and slogan back onto a foundation of measurable, testable fact.

assessments.text: 该报曾刊文质疑《21世纪资本论》部分财富数据的处理，引发广泛辩论；皮凯蒂逐条回应，争论本身反而把不平等数据的方法论推到了公共视野中央。
这位诺贝尔经济学奖得主称《21世纪资本论》是『近年最重要的经济学著作之一』，认为它把不平等重新置于经济学讨论的中心。

assessments_en.text: The paper published a piece questioning the handling of some wealth data in Capital in the Twenty-First Century, touching off a wide debate; Piketty answered point by point, and the dispute itself pushed the methodology of inequality data to the center of public view.
The Nobel laureate called Capital in the Twenty-First Century 'one of the most important economics books of recent years,' crediting it with returning inequality to the center of economic discussion.

quotes: 当资本回报率超过产出与收入的增长率，资本主义就自动地制造出难以承受、且任意的不平等。（《21世纪资本论》大意）
不平等本身未必是坏事：关键问题在于它是否合乎情理，其根据是否站得住脚。（《21世纪资本论》大意）
quotes_en: When the rate of return on capital exceeds the rate of growth of output and income, capitalism automatically generates arbitrary and unsustainable inequalities. (Capital in the Twenty-First Century, paraphrased)
Inequality is not necessarily bad in itself: the key question is whether it is justified, whether there are reasons for it. (Capital in the Twenty-First Century, paraphrased)
works: 《21世纪资本论》(Capital in the Twenty-First Century, 2013)
《平等简史》(A Brief History of Equality, 2021)
《高收入在法国，1901–1998》(早期实证研究)
piketty.lineage: 承接库兹涅茨以来对长期收入分配的实证传统，并大幅扩展其数据跨度；与伊曼纽尔·赛斯、加布里埃尔·祖克曼等人长期合作，共同建立了『世界不平等数据库』(World Inequality Database)，把税收与遗产档案变成研究不平等的标准工具。
piketty.lineage_en: He extends the empirical tradition of long-run income distribution running from Simon Kuznets, vastly widening its data span; in long collaboration with Emmanuel Saez, Gabriel Zucman and others he built the World Inequality Database, turning tax and inheritance archives into a standard instrument for studying inequality.
piketty.trivia: 《21世纪资本论》是一部厚达七百页、满是图表的学术著作，却意外登上各国畅销榜、成为现象级读物，被打趣为『最多人买、却最少人读完』的经济学书之一。皮凯蒂本人则保持着鲜明的法国学院风格，长期婉拒法国政府授予的荣誉勋位，理由是政府不该由它来决定谁有功绩。
piketty.trivia_en: Capital in the Twenty-First Century, a seven-hundred-page academic work thick with charts, improbably topped bestseller lists worldwide and became a publishing phenomenon — joked about as one of the most bought yet least finished economics books. Piketty himself keeps a distinctly French academic independence, having long declined the Legion of Honour offered by the French government, on the ground that it is not for the state to decide who has merit.
works_en: Top Incomes in France, 1901–1998 (early empirical study)

locke.bio: 约翰·洛克（John Locke），1632 年生于英格兰萨默塞特郡，哲学家、医生与政治思想家，被誉为『自由主义之父』与英国经验论的奠基人之一。他亲历英国内战、复辟与 1688 年『光荣革命』的动荡年代，曾因卷入政治流亡荷兰，归国后于 1689–1690 年间集中出版了奠定其声名的几部著作。他的思想深刻影响了后来的美国《独立宣言》与现代宪政。
locke.bio_en: John Locke, born in 1632 in Somerset, England, was a philosopher, physician, and political thinker, hailed as the 'father of liberalism' and a founder of British empiricism. He lived through the turbulent age of the Civil War, the Restoration, and the Glorious Revolution of 1688; entangled in politics, he spent years in exile in Holland, and after his return published, in 1689–1690, the works that secured his fame. His thought deeply shaped the later American Declaration of Independence and modern constitutionalism.
locke.ideas:
洛克的思想可分两大支：一支讲『知识从哪来』，一支讲『权力从哪来』，两支都从同一种精神出发——凡事要问根据、讲经验、讲同意，不轻信现成的权威。
在认识论上，他提出著名的『白板说』：人心生来不是写满天赋观念的书，而是一块白板（tabula rasa），我们的一切知识都来自后天的经验——外部世界经由感官留下印象，内心再对这些印象加以反省、组合。这一主张把知识的来源从『天生』拉回到『经历』，为后来的科学精神与教育观念铺了路：人之所以成为什么样，很大程度取决于他经历了什么、被怎样教养。
在政治哲学上，他的影响更为深远。他设想一种『自然状态』：在政府出现之前，人本就拥有一些谁也不能剥夺的『天赋权利』——生命、自由与财产。他对财产的论证尤为著名：自然万物本属众人共有，但一个人把自己的劳动『掺入』某物（开垦一块荒地、采摘果实），那物便正当地归他所有——因为人对自己的身体与劳动拥有所有权。不过他给这种获取加了一条限制，后世称为『洛克但书』：占有时须为他人『留下足够且同样好的』。
由此他推出政府的来历与边界：人们之所以走出自然状态、组成政府，是为了更可靠地保护这些既有的权利；因此政府的正当性不来自君权神授，而来自『被统治者的同意』。政府是受托者，一旦它反过来侵害人民的生命、自由与财产，背弃了托付，人民便有正当的『反抗权』。这套『天赋权利—同意—有限政府—反抗权』的逻辑，成了近代宪政、分权制衡与人权观念的源头之一。
他还以《论宗教宽容》主张：信仰是良心之事，国家不应用强力统一人的灵魂——为现代政教分离与宽容原则立下基石。洛克的气质是温和、讲理、重证据的：他不爱极端的体系，偏好从经验与常识出发、一步步讲清道理。
locke.ideas_en:
Locke's thought runs in two great branches — one on where knowledge comes from, the other on where power comes from — both springing from the same spirit: ask for grounds, appeal to experience, appeal to consent, and do not trust ready-made authority.
In epistemology he advanced the famous doctrine of the 'blank slate': the mind is born not a book filled with innate ideas but a tabula rasa, and all our knowledge comes from later experience — the outer world leaving impressions through the senses, the mind then reflecting on and combining them. This pulled the source of knowledge from 'inborn' back to 'lived,' paving the way for the scientific temper and for a view of education: what a person becomes depends largely on what he has undergone and how he was raised.
In political philosophy his influence runs deeper still. He imagined a 'state of nature': before government, people already possess certain rights no one may strip away — life, liberty, and property. His argument for property is especially famous: nature's goods belong in common to all, but when a person 'mixes' his labor with something (tilling waste ground, gathering fruit), it becomes rightly his — for a person owns his own body and labor. To this acquisition he attached a limit, later called the Lockean proviso: in taking, one must leave 'enough, and as good' for others.
From this he derived the origin and the bounds of government: people leave the state of nature and form government the better to protect rights they already hold; so a government's legitimacy comes not from divine right but from 'the consent of the governed.' Government is a trustee, and should it instead assail the people's life, liberty, and property, betraying the trust, the people hold a rightful 'right of revolution.' This logic — natural rights, consent, limited government, the right of resistance — became one of the sources of modern constitutionalism, the separation of powers, and the idea of human rights.
In A Letter Concerning Toleration he further argued that faith is a matter of conscience, and the state should not force the unity of souls — laying a cornerstone for the modern separation of church and state and for toleration. Locke's temper is mild, reasonable, evidence-minded: no lover of extreme systems, he prefers to start from experience and common sense and reason a matter clear, step by step.

assessments.text: 美国《独立宣言》中『生命、自由与追求幸福』的权利表述，公认深受洛克『生命、自由、财产』思想的影响；杰斐逊将洛克列为他最敬仰的几位思想家之一。
这位法国启蒙思想家在《哲学通信》中盛赞洛克，称他像一位明智的解剖学家一样耐心解剖人类心智，把形而上学的玄想换成了脚踏实地的考察。

assessments_en.text: The phrasing of 'life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness' in the American Declaration of Independence is widely held to owe much to Locke's 'life, liberty, property'; Jefferson named Locke among the thinkers he most admired.

In his Philosophical Letters the French Enlightenment writer lavishly praised Locke, likening him to a wise anatomist patiently dissecting the human mind, trading metaphysical speculation for down-to-earth inquiry.

quotes: 人人皆有财产权于其自身之上；除他本人外，任何人对此都没有权利。他身体的劳动、双手的工作，正当地属于他。（《政府论·下篇》大意）
法律的目的不是废除或限制自由，而是保全并扩大自由。（《政府论·下篇》大意）
凡缺乏证据支撑的笃信程度，都是我们对真理的热爱出了偏差。（《人类理解论》大意）
quotes_en: Every man has a property in his own person; this nobody has any right to but himself. The labour of his body and the work of his hands are properly his. (Second Treatise of Government, paraphrased)
The end of law is not to abolish or restrain, but to preserve and enlarge freedom. (Second Treatise of Government, paraphrased)
Whoever holds a belief with a confidence beyond what the evidence warrants has let his love of truth go astray. (An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, paraphrased)
works: 《人类理解论》(An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, 1689)
locke.lineage: 上承培根与霍布斯的经验论与契约论传统，又与之分道：他温和化了霍布斯的君主主权，转向有限政府与同意。下启贝克莱、休谟的经验论一脉，并经孟德斯鸠、卢梭与美国开国者，深刻塑造了现代自由主义、宪政与人权话语。
locke.lineage_en: He inherits the empiricist and contract traditions of Bacon and Hobbes, yet parts from them: softening Hobbes's sovereign absolutism toward limited government and consent. He opens the empiricist line running on to Berkeley and Hume, and through Montesquieu, Rousseau, and the American founders profoundly shaped modern liberalism, constitutionalism, and the language of human rights.
locke.trivia: 洛克受过正规医学训练，行医的本事一度救了他后来的政治庇护人沙夫茨伯里伯爵的命——一次肝脓肿手术的成功，让他从此深得这位权臣信任，也把他卷入了英格兰最高层的政治。他终身未婚，晚年寄居于友人家中，安静写作至 1704 年去世。
locke.trivia_en: Locke was a trained physician, and his medical skill once saved the life of his later political patron, the Earl of Shaftesbury — the success of an operation on a liver abscess won him the statesman's lasting trust and drew him into the highest politics of England. He never married, spent his last years lodging in the home of friends, and wrote quietly until his death in 1704.

mlk.bio: 马丁·路德·金（Martin Luther King Jr.），1929 年生于美国佐治亚州亚特兰大，浸信会牧师、美国民权运动的领袖。他出身牧师世家，于波士顿大学获神学博士，1955 年因领导『蒙哥马利公交抵制』而崭露头角。此后十余年，他以非暴力直接行动推动废除种族隔离，1963 年在华盛顿发表《我有一个梦想》演说，1964 年获诺贝尔和平奖，1968 年在田纳西州孟菲斯遇刺身亡，年仅 39 岁。
mlk.bio_en: Martin Luther King Jr., born in 1929 in Atlanta, Georgia, was a Baptist minister and leader of the American civil-rights movement. Born into a family of preachers, he earned a doctorate in theology at Boston University and rose to prominence in 1955 leading the Montgomery bus boycott. Over the following decade and more he pressed, through nonviolent direct action, for the end of racial segregation; he delivered the 'I Have a Dream' speech in Washington in 1963, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964, and was assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee, in 1968, at just thirty-nine.
mlk.ideas:
金的思想，是把宗教信仰、哲学与街头行动熔成一炉的『行动中的伦理学』。它的核心是『非暴力直接行动』——一种既不沉默忍受、也不以暴制暴的第三条路。
这条路的精神资源有三股：基督教『爱仇敌』的教义、印度甘地的『非暴力不合作』(satyagraha)，以及美国梭罗的『公民不服从』。金把它们整合为一套方法：通过游行、静坐、抵制等公开而和平的方式，主动违抗不义之法、并甘愿承受被捕与惩罚，以此把隐藏的不义暴露在世人眼前，唤醒旁观者的良知。他强调，非暴力针对的是『不义』本身，而非作恶的个人；其目标不是羞辱或击败对手，而是赢得对方、最终达成和解与『所爱的共同体』(beloved community)。
他对『爱』有精微的辨析。他借用希腊文区分：打动人心的不是 eros（情爱）或 philia（友爱），而是 agape——一种不计回报、甚至施于敌人的、为对方福祉着想的善意。在他看来，这种爱不是软弱，而是一种主动改变现实的力量。
金还有一套关于『正义与时间』的洞见。面对『时机未到、耐心等待』的劝告，他在《伯明翰狱中书简》里尖锐回应：太久以来，『等待』几乎总意味着『永不』；对身受其苦的人，迟来的正义就是被拒绝的正义。他既相信『道德宇宙的弧线漫长，但终将弯向正义』，又坚持这道弧线不会自己弯曲——必须有人以行动去施力。他区分了两种秩序：一种是压制冲突、表面平静的『消极和平』，一种是确立了公道的『积极和平』；真正值得追求的是后者。
晚年，他把视野从种族隔离扩展到更广的经济不公与反战，发起『穷人运动』，主张正义不仅是法律上的平等，也关乎贫困者的尊严与生计。他雄辩、充满道德激情，又始终把宏大的理想落到具体的行动与人的尊严上——这正是他思想最动人的地方。
mlk.ideas_en:
King's thought is an 'ethics in action,' fusing religious faith, philosophy, and street-level struggle into one. At its core is 'nonviolent direct action' — a third way that neither suffers in silence nor answers force with force.
This way drew on three springs: the Christian teaching to 'love your enemies,' Gandhi's nonviolent noncooperation (satyagraha), and Thoreau's civil disobedience. King forged them into a method: through marches, sit-ins, and boycotts — open and peaceful — to defy unjust law deliberately and willingly bear arrest and punishment, thereby exposing hidden injustice to the world's eyes and rousing the conscience of the onlooker. Nonviolence, he stressed, is aimed at injustice itself, not at the person who does wrong; its goal is not to humiliate or defeat the opponent but to win him over, toward reconciliation and a 'beloved community.'
He parsed 'love' with care. Borrowing from the Greek, he distinguished: what moves the heart of his work is not eros (romantic love) or philia (friendship) but agape — an unconditional goodwill, extended even to the enemy, that seeks the other's good. Such love, in his eyes, is no weakness but a force that actively changes reality.
King also held an insight about justice and time. Against the counsel to 'wait, the time is not ripe,' he answered sharply in the Letter from Birmingham Jail: for too long 'wait' has meant 'never'; to those who suffer, justice too long delayed is justice denied. He believed that 'the arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice,' yet insisted the arc does not bend on its own — someone must put force to it. He distinguished two orders: a 'negative peace' that suppresses conflict for surface calm, and a 'positive peace' that establishes justice; only the latter is worth pursuing.
In his last years he widened his gaze from segregation to broader economic injustice and to opposing war, launching the Poor People's Campaign and arguing that justice is not only legal equality but the dignity and livelihood of the poor. Eloquent and morally impassioned, he nonetheless always brought the grand ideal down to concrete action and to the dignity of the human person — and that is the most moving thing in his thought.

assessments.text: 1983 年美国设立『马丁·路德·金纪念日』为联邦假日（每年一月第三个星期一），他成为极少数获此殊荣的非总统人物之一；其形象长期被视为美国良知与平权理想的象征。
1964 年授予他诺贝尔和平奖时，委员会称他为『第一个把爱的原则化为有力的政治行动工具』的西方人物之一，表彰其以非暴力争取种族平等。

assessments_en.text: In 1983 the United States established Martin Luther King Jr. Day as a federal holiday (the third Monday of January), making him one of very few non-presidents so honored; his image has long stood as a symbol of the American conscience and the ideal of equal rights.

In awarding him the 1964 Nobel Peace Prize, the committee honored him as one who turned the principle of love into a forceful instrument of political action, achieving racial justice through nonviolence.

quotes: 任何一处的不公，都是对所有地方公义的威胁。（《伯明翰狱中书简》）
我有一个梦想：我的四个孩子有一天将生活在一个不以肤色、而以品格来评判他们的国度。（1963 年华盛顿演说）
最终，我们记住的不是敌人的话语，而是朋友的沉默。（大意）
quotes_en: Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere. (Letter from Birmingham Jail)
I have a dream that my four little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the color of their skin but by the content of their character. (Washington address, 1963)
In the end, we will remember not the words of our enemies, but the silence of our friends. (paraphrased)
works: 《迈向自由：蒙哥马利的故事》(Stride Toward Freedom, 1958)
《伯明翰狱中书简》(Letter from Birmingham Jail, 1963)
《我们为何不能再等待》(Why We Can't Wait, 1964)
《我们向何处去：混乱还是共同体？》(Where Do We Go from Here, 1967)
mlk.lineage: 思想上承耶稣登山宝训、甘地的非暴力与梭罗的公民不服从，并融入美国黑人教会的讲道传统；下启此后全球的民权、反种族隔离与公民抗争运动，从南非到东欧，许多和平抗争者都以他为方法与精神的典范。
mlk.lineage_en: His thought descends from the Sermon on the Mount, Gandhi's nonviolence, and Thoreau's civil disobedience, fused with the preaching tradition of the Black American church; it opens onto later movements for civil rights, anti-apartheid struggle, and civil resistance worldwide, from South Africa to Eastern Europe, where many peaceful protesters took him as a model of method and of spirit.
mlk.trivia: 1963 年在华盛顿林肯纪念堂前，金本已准备了讲稿，但当福音歌手玛哈丽娅·杰克逊在台下高喊『告诉他们那个梦想，马丁！』，他便推开讲稿即兴讲出了那段『我有一个梦想』——美国历史上最著名的演说之一，竟有一半是临场而生。
mlk.trivia_en: In 1963, before the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, King had a prepared text; but when the gospel singer Mahalia Jackson called out from behind him, 'Tell them about the dream, Martin!,' he pushed the script aside and improvised the 'I Have a Dream' passage — so that one of the most famous speeches in American history was, in half, born on the spot.
works_en: Stride Toward Freedom: The Montgomery Story (1958)
Where Do We Go from Here: Chaos or Community? (1967)

berlin.bio: 以赛亚·伯林（Isaiah Berlin），1909 年生于俄国里加（今属拉脱维亚）一个犹太家庭，少年时亲历俄国革命，后随家移居英国。他成为牛津大学的哲学家与思想史家，以博学、谈锋与对观念之力量的敏感著称，被誉为 20 世纪最重要的自由主义思想家之一。1957 年获封爵士，1966 年参与创办牛津沃尔夫森学院并任首任院长，1997 年去世。
berlin.bio_en: Isaiah Berlin, born in 1909 in Riga, Russia (now Latvia), into a Jewish family, witnessed the Russian Revolution as a boy before his family settled in England. He became an Oxford philosopher and historian of ideas, renowned for his learning, his conversation, and his sensitivity to the power of ideas, and is counted among the most important liberal thinkers of the twentieth century. He was knighted in 1957, helped found Wolfson College, Oxford, in 1966 and served as its first president, and died in 1997.
berlin.ideas:
伯林思想的两块基石，是『两种自由』与『价值多元主义』，二者紧密相连。
第一块，他在《两种自由概念》里区分了『消极自由』与『积极自由』。消极自由是『免于……的自由』——指一个人不受他人干涉、能在多大范围内自行其是的那片空间，问题是『没人挡着我做我想做的事吗？』积极自由是『去做……的自由』，或曰『自我主宰』——指人成为自己主人、按自己理性意志行动，问题是『我是不是真正自己在做主？』伯林承认积极自由本身是真实的善，但他警惕它的一种危险滑变：一旦有人区分出你『真实的、高级的自我』与你『当下的、低级的欲望』，就可能以『帮你实现真正的自由』为名，强迫你服从某种『理性』或集体意志——『强迫人自由』正是诸多专制最动听的说辞。历经 20 世纪极权之祸，他对这种以崇高之名行强制之实的逻辑格外戒惧。
第二块更为根本，即价值多元主义。伯林反对一个自柏拉图以来的深层假设——以为所有真正的善（自由、平等、正义、仁慈、效率、忠诚……）最终必能彼此和谐，汇成一个无矛盾的完美整体。他主张恰恰相反：人类珍视的诸多终极价值是多元的，且常常真实地冲突、无法通约（不能用同一把尺换算）。自由可能伤害平等，仁慈可能妨碍公正，自发可能损及安全——它们都是真的善，却不能同时全得。因此人生与政治充满无法消除的两难，我们只能在具体处境中做出有得有失的取舍，而没有一劳永逸的公式。
这并不导向虚无：伯林不是说『怎样都行』，而是说价值虽多元却有限、可理解，人类能凭想象进入彼此不同的视野。他真正的敌人，是那种相信自己掌握了唯一终极答案、并要按此蓝图彻底改造人类的『一元论』狂热——历史证明，正是这种『为完美未来不惜代价』的确信，铺就了通向最大规模强制与杀戮的路。他因此偏爱温和、可纠错、给多样性留余地的政治，而非许诺天堂的宏大工程。伯林为人博学、宽厚、健谈，一生写下大量思想史随笔，让维柯、赫尔德、托尔斯泰、迈斯特等常被忽略的思想家重新被听见。
berlin.ideas_en:
Two stones bear up Berlin's thought — the 'two concepts of liberty' and 'value pluralism' — and they are tightly linked.
The first: in 'Two Concepts of Liberty' he distinguished negative from positive liberty. Negative liberty is 'freedom from' — the space within which a person may act unobstructed by others; its question is 'is anyone stopping me from doing what I want?' Positive liberty is 'freedom to,' or self-mastery — being one's own master, acting by one's own rational will; its question is 'am I truly the one in charge?' Berlin granted that positive liberty is a genuine good, but he watched for a dangerous slide: once someone splits your 'true, higher self' from your 'present, lower desires,' he may, in the name of 'helping you realize your real freedom,' force you to obey some 'reason' or collective will — 'forcing men to be free' being the most seductive pretext of many tyrannies. Having lived through the totalitarian disasters of the twentieth century, he was especially wary of this logic of coercion in the name of the sublime.
The second, more fundamental, is value pluralism. Berlin rejected a deep assumption running since Plato — that all true goods (liberty, equality, justice, mercy, efficiency, loyalty) must finally harmonize into one perfect, contradiction-free whole. He held the opposite: the ultimate values human beings prize are plural, and often genuinely conflict, and are incommensurable (not convertible by a single measure). Liberty may injure equality, mercy may obstruct justice, spontaneity may cost security — all are real goods, yet cannot all be had at once. So life and politics are full of dilemmas that cannot be dissolved; we can only make trade-offs, with gains and losses, within concrete situations — there is no once-and-for-all formula.
This does not lead to nihilism: Berlin did not say 'anything goes,' but that values, though plural, are finite and intelligible, and human beings can enter, by imagination, horizons not their own. His true enemy was the 'monist' fervor that believes it holds the single final answer and would remake humanity by that blueprint at any cost — for history shows that just this conviction, 'no price too high for a perfect future,' paved the road to coercion and slaughter on the largest scale. He therefore preferred a politics that is moderate, correctable, and leaves room for diversity, over grand projects that promise heaven. Learned, generous, and famously talkative, Berlin wrote a great body of essays in the history of ideas, letting often-neglected thinkers — Vico, Herder, Tolstoy, de Maistre — be heard again.

assessments.text: 这篇 1958 年的牛津就职演讲，被公认为 20 世纪政治哲学最具影响力的文本之一，『消极／积极自由』之分至今仍是讨论自由问题的基本框架。
这位英国学者称伯林为他那一代最杰出的谈话者与思想史家之一，赞其能让早已沉默的思想家重新开口、让冷僻的观念变得鲜活可感。

assessments_en.by: The legacy of 'Two Concepts of Liberty'
assessments_en.text: This 1958 Oxford inaugural lecture is widely regarded as one of the most influential texts of twentieth-century political philosophy; the distinction between negative and positive liberty remains a basic framework for discussing freedom.

The British scholar called Berlin one of the finest talkers and historians of ideas of his generation, praising his power to make long-silent thinkers speak again and to bring obscure ideas vividly to life.

quotes: 强迫人自由，是一切政治理论中最危险、也最动听的诡辩之一。（《两种自由概念》大意）
正因为人类的目的多元，且并非全都可以彼此通约，冲突与悲剧才永远无法从人的生活中被彻底清除。（《两种自由概念》大意）
若想真正自由，就得放弃那个诱人的幻觉：以为一切美好之物终能完美地合为一体。（大意）
quotes_en: To force men to be free is one of the most dangerous, and most seductive, sophistries in all of political theory. (Two Concepts of Liberty, paraphrased)

Because the ends of men are many, and not all of them are commensurable, the possibility of conflict and of tragedy can never be wholly eliminated from human life. (Two Concepts of Liberty, paraphrased)
If you would be truly free, you must give up the seductive illusion that all good things can be perfectly combined into one. (paraphrased)
works: 《两种自由概念》(Two Concepts of Liberty, 1958)
《刺猬与狐狸》(The Hedgehog and the Fox, 1953)
《俄国思想家》(Russian Thinkers, 论文集)
berlin.lineage: 思想上承启蒙的自由主义，又受维柯、赫尔德等『反启蒙』思想家启发，发展出对多样性与历史语境的尊重；与波普尔同属对极权主义的深刻批判者。其『价值多元主义』深刻影响了后来的政治哲学，从约翰·格雷到伯纳德·威廉斯等都受其沾溉。
berlin.lineage_en: His thought inherits Enlightenment liberalism, yet is stirred by 'Counter-Enlightenment' figures like Vico and Herder into a respect for diversity and historical context; with Karl Popper he stands among the deep critics of totalitarianism. His 'value pluralism' profoundly shaped later political philosophy, from John Gray to Bernard Williams.
berlin.trivia: 伯林以滔滔不绝、语速惊人的谈吐闻名，据说能在一顿饭间纵论古今、令满座倾倒；他笑称自己『高估了几乎每一位与他交谈过的人』。他在二战期间曾任职于英国驻华盛顿使馆，其犀利的政情报告据传连丘吉尔都爱读——还闹出过把音乐家欧文·柏林错认成他、邀来共进午餐的趣闻。
berlin.trivia_en: Berlin was famous for talk of astonishing speed and fluency, said to range over all history in a single dinner and leave the table spellbound; he joked that he had 'overestimated almost everyone' he ever spoke with. During the Second World War he served at the British embassy in Washington, where his sharp political dispatches were reputedly read with relish even by Churchill — and gave rise to the tale of the songwriter Irving Berlin being mistaken for him and invited to lunch.

bauman.bio: 齐格蒙特·鲍曼（Zygmunt Bauman），1925 年生于波兰一个犹太家庭，社会学家。二战期间为躲避纳粹流亡苏联，战后任教于华沙大学，1968 年因波兰的反犹清洗被迫离开祖国，辗转后定居英国，长期任教于利兹大学。他著作极丰、晚年笔耕不辍，以『液态现代性』这一概念享誉世界，被视为当代最重要的社会理论家之一，2017 年于利兹去世。
bauman.bio_en: Zygmunt Bauman, born in 1925 in Poland into a Jewish family, was a sociologist. He fled to the Soviet Union to escape the Nazis during the Second World War, taught after it at the University of Warsaw, and in 1968 was forced from his homeland by an antisemitic purge; after wandering he settled in Britain, teaching for many years at the University of Leeds. Prolific and writing to the end of his long life, he won world renown for the concept of 'liquid modernity' and is regarded as one of the most important social theorists of our time. He died in Leeds in 2017.
bauman.ideas:
鲍曼最有标志性的概念是『液态现代性』。他用『固态』与『液态』作比，刻画现代社会的一场深刻转变。早期现代（『固态现代』）虽然也在打碎传统，但它想用新的坚固结构来取代旧的——稳定的工厂、终身的职业、持久的婚姻、清晰的阶级与制度。而我们身处的『液态现代』，则是连这些新结构本身也变得流动不居：工作朝不保夕、关系说散就散、身份不断重塑、规则随时改写。液体的特点是留不住形状——鲍曼说，今天的社会正是如此，一切坚固的都尚未凝固就又化开了。
这种流动带来一个悖论：人空前自由，却也空前不安。你可以不断重新选择职业、伴侣、自我形象，但代价是没有什么能让你稳稳依靠；自由与不安全成了同一枚硬币的两面。
他对消费社会有犀利的诊断：在液态现代里，人不仅是消费者，连人本身也被卷入消费的逻辑——我们像挑选商品一样挑选关系与身份，也像商品一样被他人挑选、被『保质期』衡量。由此他提出一个尖锐的区分：社会把人分成有能力消费的『正常人』，和买不起、消费不动的『有缺陷的消费者』。后者是这个体系里最受冷落的一群——工业时代的穷人至少还是被需要的劳动力，而消费社会里的底层，连被剥削的位置都没有，沦为『多余的人』，被系统当作废弃物排除在外。这种『被宣判为冗余』，在他看来是当代最深的伤害。
鲍曼的另一项重要工作，是对现代性『阴暗面』的反思。在《现代性与大屠杀》中，他提出一个令人不安的论点：纳粹的种族屠杀并非文明的偶然倒退，而恰恰借助了现代性自身的工具——科层制的分工、技术理性、把人化约为可管理的数字。当道德责任被层层流程稀释、当『他者』被官僚机器抽象成处理对象，普通人也可能平静地参与暴行。这提醒我们：现代的高效与秩序，本身并不保证善。
鲍曼的笔调忧郁、人道而温厚。他不开宏大药方，更像一个清醒的诊断者，执意让人看见流动时代里那些被牺牲、被遗忘的人，并守护『为他者负责』这一伦理的底线。
bauman.ideas_en:
Bauman's most signature concept is 'liquid modernity.' With the figures of 'solid' and 'liquid' he portrays a deep transformation of modern society. Early modernity ('solid modernity') also broke up tradition, but it meant to replace the old solids with new ones — stable factories, lifelong careers, lasting marriages, clear classes and institutions. The 'liquid modernity' we inhabit is one in which even these new structures have themselves turned fluid: work is precarious, relationships dissolve at a word, identities are endlessly remade, rules rewritten at any moment. A liquid holds no shape — and so, Bauman says, is today's society: everything solid melts again before it has set.
This fluidity brings a paradox: people are freer than ever, yet more insecure than ever. You may keep re-choosing your career, your partner, your self-image, but the price is that nothing offers steady footing; freedom and insecurity are two faces of one coin.
He diagnosed consumer society sharply: in liquid modernity people are not only consumers — the human being itself is drawn into the logic of consumption. We pick relationships and identities as we pick goods, and are picked, in turn, like goods, measured by a 'shelf life.' From this he drew a pointed distinction: society sorts people into 'normal' consumers able to buy, and 'flawed consumers' who cannot afford to. The latter are the most neglected in the system — the poor of the industrial age were at least needed as labor, but the bottom of consumer society holds not even the place of the exploited, becoming 'the redundant,' excluded by the system as waste. This 'being sentenced as surplus' is, in his eyes, the deepest harm of the present.
Another of Bauman's major works reflects on the 'dark side' of modernity. In Modernity and the Holocaust he advanced an unsettling thesis: the Nazi genocide was no chance relapse of civilization but drew precisely on modernity's own tools — bureaucratic division of labor, technical reason, the reduction of human beings to manageable numbers. When moral responsibility is diluted through layers of procedure, and the 'other' is abstracted by the bureaucratic machine into an object to be processed, ordinary people too may take part calmly in atrocity. It is a reminder: modern efficiency and order do not, in themselves, guarantee goodness.
Bauman's tone is melancholy, humane, and gentle. He offers no grand cure; he is rather a clear-eyed diagnostician, insisting that we see those sacrificed and forgotten in the age of flux, and guarding the ethical bedrock of 'responsibility for the other.'

assessments.by: 欧洲阿马尔菲社会学奖
assessments.text: 1989 年，《现代性与大屠杀》为鲍曼赢得欧洲阿马尔菲社会学与社会理论奖，该书被誉为对现代性阴暗面最深刻的社会学反思之一。
1998 年，鲍曼获颁德国法兰克福市的阿多诺奖，表彰其对当代社会、伦理与现代性的批判性贡献。

assessments_en.text: In 1989 Modernity and the Holocaust won Bauman the European Amalfi Prize for Sociology and Social Theory; the book is regarded as one of the most profound sociological reflections on the dark side of modernity.
In 1998 Bauman received the Adorno Prize from the city of Frankfurt, honoring his critical contributions to the understanding of contemporary society, ethics, and modernity.

quotes: 在液态现代的世界里，一切都是暂时的；流动性已取代固着，成为人之处境的常态。（大意）
怀疑的终结，正是一切暴行的开端。（《现代性与大屠杀》大意）
如今我们都被迫去过一种『传记式地解决系统性矛盾』的生活——用个人的努力，去消化本是社会造成的问题。（大意）
quotes_en: In a liquid-modern world, everything is provisional; flux, not fixity, has become the normal human condition. (paraphrased)
The end of doubt is the beginning of all atrocity. (Modernity and the Holocaust, paraphrased)
We are now forced to seek biographical solutions to systemic contradictions — to absorb, by private effort, problems that society itself created. (paraphrased)
works: 《现代性与大屠杀》(Modernity and the Holocaust, 1989)
《工作、消费主义与新穷人》(Work, Consumerism and the New Poor, 1998)
《废弃的生命》(Wasted Lives: Modernity and Its Outcasts, 2004)
bauman.lineage: 思想上汲取马克思对资本主义的批判、韦伯对科层制与现代理性的分析，以及列维纳斯『为他者负责』的伦理学；他把这些资源转向对消费社会、全球化与流动时代的诊断，影响了大批研究现代性、消费与社会排斥的后辈学者。
bauman.lineage_en: His thought draws on Marx's critique of capitalism, Weber's analysis of bureaucracy and modern reason, and Levinas's ethics of 'responsibility for the other'; he turned these resources toward diagnosing consumer society, globalization, and the age of flux, influencing many later scholars of modernity, consumption, and social exclusion.
bauman.trivia: 鲍曼一生著述逾五十种，绝大多数完成于 60 岁退休『之后』——退休对他不是封笔，反而开启了最高产的三十年。他与同为学者的妻子雅尼娜相伴六十余载，曾说自己的写作几乎都是与她对话的延续；他用旧式打字机工作，对数字时代既批判又好奇。
bauman.trivia_en: Bauman wrote more than fifty books, the great majority completed after he retired at sixty — retirement was for him no closing of the pen but the start of his most prolific thirty years. He shared more than sixty years with his wife Janina, herself a writer, and said his work was almost a continuation of his conversation with her; he worked on an old-fashioned typewriter, at once critical of and curious about the digital age.
works_en: Work, Consumerism and the New Poor (1998)
Wasted Lives: Modernity and Its Outcasts (2004)

calvin.bio: 1509–1564，法国出身的神学家、宗教改革家，新教加尔文宗（归正宗）的奠基者。早年在巴黎与奥尔良研习法律与人文学，1530 年代初皈依新教，因法国迫害而流亡。1536 年出版《基督教要义》，并被卷入日内瓦的教会与城邦改革，几经驱逐与召回，最终把日内瓦建成欧洲新教的中心与流亡者的庇护所。他治学严谨、性情冷峻，影响远及苏格兰长老会、英格兰清教徒与北美殖民地。
calvin.bio_en: 1509–1564, a French-born theologian and reformer, founder of the Calvinist (Reformed) branch of Protestantism. Trained in law and the humanities at Paris and Orléans, he embraced the Reformation in the early 1530s and fled persecution in France. In 1536 he published the Institutes of the Christian Religion and was drawn into reforming the church and city of Geneva; after expulsion and recall he made Geneva a center of Protestantism and a refuge for exiles. Rigorous and austere, his influence reached Scottish Presbyterianism, English Puritanism, and colonial North America.
calvin.ideas:
加尔文神学的起点，是一个让现代人本能抵触、却被他推到极致的判断：人在上帝面前彻底无能为力。他继承奥古斯丁的『原罪』传统，主张人性已被罪『全然败坏』——这不是说人一无是处，而是说人凭自己再怎么努力，也无法靠近上帝、赚得救恩。既然人无力自救，救恩就只能完全是上帝白白的恩典（拉丁文 sola gratia，唯独恩典）。
由此引出他最著名也最具争议的『预定论』：早在创世之前，上帝就已拣选了哪些人得救、哪些人沉沦；这一拣选不取决于人将来的善行或信心，而纯出于上帝主权的自由。人无法用功德去交换，也无法靠表现去改写。乍听之下近乎冷酷，但加尔文的本意，是把救恩的根基从摇摆不定的人的努力，彻底挪到不变的上帝身上——对真心相信的人，这反而是一种确据与安慰：你之被爱，不靠你自己挣来。
要理解他，得抓住贯穿全部的一个词：上帝的『主权』。在加尔文眼里，宇宙的每一处都在上帝的掌管之下，没有真正的偶然。与之配套的，是他对《圣经》权威的高举——信仰的最终标准是圣经本身，而非教会传统或人的理性，这也是新教与罗马教会的根本分野之一。
一个常被忽略却影响深远的侧面，是他的『天职』观。既然人无法靠劳作赚得救恩，工作就不再是赎罪的手段；但加尔文反而赋予日常劳动新的尊严：无论农夫、商人还是仆役，本分的工作都是上帝亲自交派的『呼召』，理应勤勉、诚实、卓越地去做，以荣耀上帝。后来社会学家韦伯在《新教伦理与资本主义精神》里提出，正是这种『把世俗职业当作天职、克勤克俭却不为享乐』的心态，意外催生了近代资本主义的精神——这是后人的诠释，加尔文本人未必这样想，却点出了他思想惊人的现实穿透力。
加尔文也是一位制度建设者。他在日内瓦推行严格的教会纪律与道德规训，把城市治理与宗教生活紧密交织，使之被称为新教的『罗马』。这套体制造就了高度自律的社群，也有严苛的一面——1553 年反三位一体的学者塞尔维特在日内瓦被判火刑，加尔文涉入其中，成为后世批评他不宽容的著名污点。如何评价他，至今仍在『把救恩从人的功劳里彻底解放出来』的深刻，与『不容异见的严厉』之间拉扯。
calvin.ideas_en:
Calvin's theology begins from a judgment modern readers instinctively resist, yet which he pushed to its limit: before God, human beings are utterly powerless to save themselves. Inheriting Augustine's doctrine of original sin, he held that human nature is 'totally depraved' by sin — not that people are worthless, but that no amount of one's own striving can draw near to God or earn salvation. Since we cannot save ourselves, salvation can only be God's free, unearned gift (Latin sola gratia, 'grace alone').
From this follows his most famous and most disputed teaching, predestination: before the world was made, God already chose who would be saved and who lost; this choosing rests not on a person's future deeds or faith but purely on the freedom of God's sovereignty. No one can trade merit for it, and no one can rewrite it by performance. It sounds nearly cruel at first, but Calvin's intent was to move the ground of salvation off the wavering efforts of human beings and onto the unchanging God — and for the genuine believer this is meant as assurance and comfort: that you are loved does not depend on your earning it.
To grasp him, hold on to one word that runs through everything: God's 'sovereignty.' In Calvin's eyes every corner of the universe lies under God's governance; there is no genuine chance. Paired with this is his exaltation of the authority of Scripture — the final standard of faith is the Bible itself, not church tradition or human reason, one of the root divisions between Protestantism and Rome.
An often-overlooked but far-reaching side of his thought is his notion of 'vocation,' or calling. Since work cannot earn salvation, labor is no longer a means of atonement; yet Calvin instead gave everyday work a new dignity: whether farmer, merchant, or servant, one's honest work is a 'calling' assigned by God himself, to be done diligently, honestly, and excellently for God's glory. The sociologist Max Weber later argued, in The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism, that precisely this mindset — treating a worldly occupation as a calling, working hard and thriftily yet not for enjoyment — unexpectedly bred the spirit of modern capitalism. That is a later interpretation Calvin himself might not have shared, but it points to the startling real-world reach of his ideas.
Calvin was also a builder of institutions. In Geneva he enforced strict church discipline and moral regulation, weaving civic governance tightly together with religious life until the city was called the 'Rome' of Protestantism. This order produced a highly self-disciplined community, but also had a harsh face — in 1553 the anti-Trinitarian scholar Servetus was condemned to burn at Geneva, with Calvin implicated, a famous stain that later critics cite for his intolerance. How to judge him is still pulled between the depth of 'freeing salvation entirely from human merit' and the severity of 'brooking no dissent.'

assessments.text: 在《新教伦理与资本主义精神》中，韦伯认为加尔文的预定论带来一种独特的心理后果：信徒既无法靠善行改变上帝的拣选，又渴望确认自己属于得救者，便把『在世俗职业中持续而有条理的成功』当作蒙拣选的旁证，从而催生出克勤克俭、理性化经营的『资本主义精神』（大意）。
20 世纪改革宗神学家巴特虽重构了加尔文的预定论（使之以基督为中心），却对其极为推崇。1922 年他在致挞乃森的信中形容研读加尔文如同面对『一道瀑布、一片原始森林、一种近乎魔力的力量，仿佛径直从喜马拉雅山降下』，叹其浩瀚难以把握（大意）。

assessments_en.text: In The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism, Weber argued that Calvin's predestination produced a peculiar psychological effect: believers could not alter God's election by good works, yet longed for assurance that they were among the saved, and so came to treat 'steady, methodical success in a worldly calling' as a sign of election — which bred the diligent, thrifty, rationalized 'spirit of capitalism' (paraphrased).

The twentieth-century Reformed theologian Barth, though he reworked Calvin's doctrine of election to center it on Christ, revered him deeply. In a 1922 letter to Thurneysen he described studying Calvin as facing 'a waterfall, a primeval forest, a demonic power, something straight down from the Himalayas,' marveling at a vastness almost too great to grasp (paraphrased).

quotes: 我们所拥有的几乎全部真智慧……都包含两个部分：对上帝的认识，与对我们自己的认识。（《基督教要义》开篇）
我们称『预定』为上帝永恒的定旨：他借此自行决定，要让每一个人成为怎样的人。（《基督教要义》卷三）
主啊，我把我的心献给你——迅速而真诚。（加尔文的箴言与印章铭文）
quotes_en: Nearly all the wisdom we possess… consists of two parts: the knowledge of God and of ourselves. (Institutes of the Christian Religion, opening)
We call predestination God's eternal decree, by which he determined with himself what he willed to become of each man. (Institutes, Book III)
My heart I offer to you, Lord, promptly and sincerely. (Calvin's motto and the inscription on his seal)
works_en: On the Eternal Predestination of God
calvin.lineage: 上承奥古斯丁的恩典与原罪论及保罗书信，与路德同属宗教改革阵营而更趋系统化；下启加尔文宗／归正宗、苏格兰长老会（诺克斯）与英美清教徒，并经韦伯的社会学诠释进入现代关于资本主义与劳动伦理的讨论，20 世纪又由卡尔·巴特等改革宗神学家重新激活。
calvin.lineage_en: He drew on Augustine's teaching of grace and original sin and on the letters of Paul, and stood with Luther in the Reformation while systematizing it further; he gave rise to Calvinism/the Reformed churches, to Scottish Presbyterianism (Knox), and to the English and American Puritans, entered modern debate over capitalism and the work ethic through Weber's sociology, and was revived in the twentieth century by Reformed theologians such as Karl Barth.
calvin.trivia: 加尔文本想做个安静的学者。1536 年他途经日内瓦，改革家法雷尔力劝他留下相助；见他推辞，法雷尔竟厉声警告：若他只顾自己的研究而弃日内瓦于不顾，上帝必咒诅他的安逸——加尔文后来说这话吓得他不敢成行，从此把一生交给了这座城。他体弱多病，却几乎工作到死；他的个人印章是一只手捧着一颗燃烧的心，配着箴言『主啊，我把心献上，迅速而真诚』。
calvin.trivia_en: Calvin had wanted the quiet life of a scholar. Passing through Geneva in 1536, he was pressed by the reformer Farel to stay and help; when he demurred, Farel thundered a warning that God would curse his leisure if he abandoned Geneva for his own studies — Calvin later said the words so frightened him that he dared not leave, and from then on gave his life to the city. Frail and often ill, he worked almost to his death; his personal seal showed a hand offering a burning heart, with the motto 'My heart I offer to you, Lord, promptly and sincerely.'

schrodinger.bio: 埃尔温·薛定谔（1887–1961），奥地利物理学家，量子力学的奠基人之一。1926 年提出以他命名的波动方程，用连续的『波』来描述微观粒子的状态，与海森堡的矩阵力学殊途同归，并因此与狄拉克共获 1933 年诺贝尔物理学奖。他厌恶纳粹、几度辗转流亡，最终在都柏林安顿。除物理外，他兴趣极广，晚年转向生命科学与哲学，写出影响深远的小书《生命是什么》。
schrodinger.bio_en: Erwin Schrödinger (1887–1961), Austrian physicist and one of the founders of quantum mechanics. In 1926 he proposed the wave equation that bears his name, describing the state of microscopic particles by a continuous 'wave' — an approach that proved equivalent to Heisenberg's matrix mechanics, and for which he shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Dirac. Loathing Nazism, he went into exile several times and finally settled in Dublin. Beyond physics his interests were wide-ranging; in later life he turned to the life sciences and philosophy, writing the deeply influential little book What Is Life?
schrodinger.ideas:
薛定谔的思想横跨三个看似无关、实则一脉的领域，串起它们的，是一个反复出现的追问：连续与离散、整体与部件、物质与心灵，究竟如何统一。
第一是波动力学。20 世纪 20 年代，物理学家发现电子既像粒子又像波。薛定谔抓住后者，写下一个方程，把粒子的状态描述成一个在空间里铺开、随时间演化的『波函数』。打个比方：经典物理把电子当成一颗小球，有确定的位置和速度；薛定谔则说，在被观测之前，它更像一片弥散的概率云，方程告诉你这片云如何流动。这套数学极其成功——今天的化学键、半导体、激光，背后都是它。但它带来一个哲学难题：那片『波』到底是真实存在，还是只是我们知识的记账方式？这个问题他争论了一辈子。
第二是那只著名的猫。很多人以为『薛定谔的猫』是他得意的发现，恰恰相反——那是他 1935 年设计来嘲讽主流解释的。当时流行的看法认为，微观粒子在观测前处于多种状态的『叠加』。薛定谔说：好，那我把一只猫、一个放射性原子和一瓶毒药关进盒子，让原子衰变与否决定猫的生死；按你们的逻辑，开盒前这只猫岂不是既死又活？他用这个荒诞画面逼问：**叠加这种说法用在微观世界尚可，一旦天真地推广到猫这样的宏观之物，就明显荒谬——那么微观与宏观的界线到底在哪？**这个『测量问题』至今没有公认答案。
第三是《生命是什么》。1944 年他以物理学家的眼光追问：生命凭什么能在混乱的分子热运动中维持精确的秩序、并把它一代代准确传下去？他大胆推测，遗传信息一定存储在一种『非周期晶体』里——既像晶体那样稳定，又不单调重复，从而能用有限的原子编码海量信息；他还用『以负熵为食』来描述生命如何抵抗走向无序的自然倾向。这本书当时尚不知 DNA 为何物，却启发了沃森、克里克等一代人投身分子生物学，被许多人视为这门学科的精神起点。
贯穿这三者的，是薛定谔晚年愈发明确的一种哲学倾向：他深受古印度吠檀多影响，怀疑把世界切成一块块物质、再切出一个个独立心灵的常识图景，倾向于认为意识在根本上是一体的。**他始终提醒人：我们能写下描述世界的方程，并不等于我们已经理解了世界本身。**
schrodinger.ideas_en:
Schrödinger's thought spans three seemingly unrelated yet inwardly connected fields, threaded by a recurring question: how are the continuous and the discrete, the whole and the part, matter and mind, ultimately unified?
The first is wave mechanics. In the 1920s physicists found that the electron behaves both like a particle and like a wave. Schrödinger seized on the latter and wrote an equation describing a particle's state as a 'wave function' spread out in space and evolving in time. By analogy: classical physics treats the electron as a tiny ball with a definite position and speed; Schrödinger says that, before observation, it is more like a diffuse cloud of probability, and the equation tells you how that cloud flows. The mathematics is extraordinarily successful — chemical bonds, semiconductors, lasers all rest on it. But it raises a philosophical puzzle: is that 'wave' really real, or merely a bookkeeping of our knowledge? He argued over this all his life.
The second is the famous cat. Many imagine 'Schrödinger's cat' was a prized discovery of his; quite the opposite — he devised it in 1935 to mock the mainstream interpretation. The fashionable view held that, before observation, a microscopic particle exists in a 'superposition' of several states. Schrödinger said: fine, then let me shut a cat, a radioactive atom, and a vial of poison in a box, with the atom's decay deciding whether the cat lives or dies; by your logic, before the box is opened isn't the cat both dead and alive? With this absurd picture he pressed the question: **superposition may pass in the microscopic world, but once naïvely extended to a macroscopic thing like a cat it becomes plainly absurd — so where exactly is the line between micro and macro?** This 'measurement problem' still has no agreed answer.
The third is What Is Life? In 1944, with a physicist's eye, he asked: how can life maintain precise order amid the chaotic thermal motion of molecules, and pass it down accurately generation after generation? He boldly conjectured that hereditary information must be stored in an 'aperiodic crystal' — as stable as a crystal yet not monotonously repeating, so that a finite number of atoms could encode vast information; and he described how life resists the natural drift toward disorder by 'feeding on negative entropy.' The book, written before DNA was understood, inspired a generation including Watson and Crick to enter molecular biology, and is regarded by many as that discipline's spiritual starting point.
Running through all three is a philosophical leaning that grew clearer in his later years: deeply influenced by ancient Indian Vedanta, he doubted the commonsense picture that cuts the world into separate pieces of matter and then into separate, independent minds, and inclined to think that consciousness is at bottom one. **He always reminded us: that we can write down equations describing the world does not mean we have understood the world itself.**

assessments.text: DNA 双螺旋的共同发现者多次表示，年轻时读到《生命是什么》深受触动，是它把自己从物理学引向了对基因的探索。
对薛定谔的波动力学评价极高，认为其工作出自真正的天才（大意）；两人晚年都对量子力学的主流诠释心怀不安，常有书信往还、互为同道。
正是玻恩把薛定谔的波函数解释为概率幅，这一解释成为量子力学的标准；薛定谔本人却始终不接受，足见这位老友之间分歧之深。

assessments_en.text: The co-discoverer of the DNA double helix said more than once that reading What Is Life? in his youth moved him deeply and drew him from physics toward the study of the gene.

He rated Schrödinger's wave mechanics very highly, holding that the work sprang from true genius (paraphrased); both men in later years were uneasy with the mainstream interpretation of quantum mechanics and corresponded often as kindred spirits.

It was Born who interpreted Schrödinger's wave function as a probability amplitude — the interpretation that became standard in quantum mechanics; Schrödinger himself never accepted it, a measure of how deep the disagreement ran between the old friends.

quotes: 我所说的那种『非周期晶体』，正是生命物质的物质载体。
生命以负熵为食。
意识从来只以单数被经验，从无复数（大意）。
我把整套量子力学都视为一种猜测，纵然是极其成功的猜测（大意）。
quotes_en: The 'aperiodic crystal' I speak of is the material carrier of living matter.
Life feeds on negative entropy.
Consciousness is never experienced in the plural, only in the singular. (paraphrased)
I regard the whole of quantum mechanics as a conjecture — an extraordinarily successful one, but a conjecture. (paraphrased)
works: 《量子化作为本征值问题》（1926 年系列论文，确立波动方程）
《自然与希腊人》（Nature and the Greeks, 1954）
《我的世界观》（My View of the World）
works_en: 'Quantisation as a Problem of Proper Values' (the 1926 series of papers establishing the wave equation)
schrodinger.lineage: 他直接承接德布罗意的『物质波』假说，将其发展为完整的波动力学；与海森堡、玻恩、狄拉克共同奠定量子力学的数学骨架，却在诠释上与哥本哈根学派长期对立。哲学上深受叔本华与古印度吠檀多影响。向下，他的《生命是什么》成为分子生物学的思想火种，影响了沃森、克里克、威尔金斯等一代人。
schrodinger.lineage_en: He took up de Broglie's hypothesis of 'matter waves' directly and developed it into a full wave mechanics; together with Heisenberg, Born, and Dirac he laid the mathematical skeleton of quantum mechanics, while long opposing the Copenhagen school on interpretation. Philosophically he was deeply shaped by Schopenhauer and ancient Indian Vedanta. Downstream, his What Is Life? became an intellectual spark for molecular biology, influencing a generation including Watson, Crick, and Wilkins.
schrodinger.trivia: 1933 年他与狄拉克分享诺贝尔物理学奖。那只『猫』本是他用来反对、而非支持主流量子诠释的思想实验，如今却成了流行文化里最知名的科学意象。他一生私生活不循常规，曾与妻子及情人共同生活。流亡途中他辗转牛津、格拉茨，最终在爱尔兰都柏林高等研究院安身十余年，《生命是什么》正源于他在都柏林的系列公开演讲。
schrodinger.trivia_en: In 1933 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Dirac. The 'cat' was a thought experiment he devised to oppose, not endorse, the mainstream interpretation of quantum mechanics, yet it has become the most famous scientific image in popular culture. His personal life was unconventional throughout, at one point sharing a household with both his wife and a lover. In exile he moved through Oxford and Graz before settling for over a decade at the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies in Ireland — What Is Life? grew out of a series of public lectures he gave there.

spinoza.bio: 巴鲁赫·斯宾诺莎（1632–1677），出生于阿姆斯特丹的葡萄牙裔犹太家庭。因其激进的神学—哲学观点，24 岁时被犹太社群以最严厉的『herem』（禁令）逐出，从此与原生社群彻底决裂。此后他以磨制光学镜片为生，谢绝海德堡大学的教席以保全思想自由，过着简朴独居的生活，45 岁因肺病去世。其代表作《伦理学》在他身后才出版，旋即被列为禁书，却深刻影响了后世从黑格尔、尼采到爱因斯坦的无数人。
spinoza.bio_en: Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677) was born into a Portuguese-Jewish family in Amsterdam. For his radical theological-philosophical views he was expelled at twenty-four from the Jewish community under its harshest ban (herem), severing him from the world he was born into. He then earned his living grinding optical lenses, declined a chair at Heidelberg to keep his freedom of thought, and lived simply and alone, dying of a lung illness at forty-five. His masterwork, the Ethics, appeared only after his death and was promptly banned — yet it shaped countless later minds, from Hegel and Nietzsche to Einstein.
spinoza.ideas:
斯宾诺莎最惊人的主张是『神即自然』（Deus sive Natura）：他不承认一个高居世界之外、会发怒会偏爱的人格神，而认为存在的只有唯一的实体——你可以叫它『神』，也可以叫它『自然』，万物都只是这唯一实体的不同表现。这在当时是惊世骇俗的异端，却也是一种深沉的敬畏：神不在自然之外，神就是这套有其必然法则的整体。

由此推出他的决定论：万物都依其必然的因果而发生，没有什么是『本可以不这样』的。这听起来冷酷，斯宾诺莎却从中引出自由——所谓自由，不是为所欲为，而是『理解必然』。一块被抛出的石头若有意识，会以为自己『想』飞；人也常把被原因推动的冲动误当成自由意志。真正的自由，是看清推动自己的原因，从被动变为主动。

他最实用的遗产，是一套情感的几何学。在《伦理学》里他像证几何题一样剖析喜悦、悲伤、希望、恐惧、嫉妒。核心洞见是：情感分『被动』与『主动』两种。被动情感来自我们对事物认识不清，它奴役我们；而当我们清楚理解一种情感的成因，它就不再以同样的方式控制我们——他说，一种受苦的情感，一旦我们对它形成清晰明确的观念，就不再是受苦。于是斯宾诺莎式的救赎，不是压抑情感，而是用理解照亮它。

他还提出『conatus』（努力）：每个存在都努力维持自身的存在，这是一切欲望与价值的根源——我们认为某物好，往往不是因为它本身好，而是因为我们欲求它。最终他指向一种『对神（自然）的理智之爱』：当我们从『永恒的角度』理解万物的必然，狭隘的恐惧与怨恨会松动，心灵获得一种沉静的自由与喜悦。
spinoza.ideas_en:
Spinoza's most startling claim is 'God, or Nature' (Deus sive Natura): he denies a personal God standing outside the world, who rages and favors, and holds that only one substance exists — call it 'God' or call it 'Nature' — of which all things are merely different expressions.
